{{Infobox song contest national year
| Year = 1957
| Broadcaster = [[Swiss Broadcasting Corporation]] (SRG SSR)
| Country = Switzerland
| Selection process = {{lang|de|Internationaler Schlagerwettbewerb}} ''1957''
| Selection date = 11 February 1957
| Song = {{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}
| Artist = [[Lys Assia]]
| Writer = {{Unbulleted list|[[Géo Voumard]]|[[Émile Gardaz]]}}
| Final result = 8th, 5 votes
}}

Switzerland was represented at the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1957]] with the song "{{lang|fr|L'enfant que j'étais|i=no}}", composed by [[Géo Voumard]], with lyrics by [[Émile Gardaz]], and performed by [[Lys Assia]]. The Swiss participating broadcaster, the [[Swiss Broadcasting Corporation]] (SRG SSR), selected its entry through a national final. Assia had already represented Switzerland at the {{escyr|1956||previous contest}} performing both Swiss entries, and winning with "{{lang|fr|[[Refrain (Lys Assia song)|Refrain]]|i=no}}".

==Before Eurovision==
=== {{lang|de|Internationaler Schlagerwettbewerb 1957}} ===
The [[Swiss Broadcasting Corporation]] (SRG SSR) held a national final to select its entry for the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1957]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=27 January 1957 |title=Das schwarze Brett: Europäischer Schlagerwettbewerb 1957 |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |page=24 |language=de |issue=4 |oclc=638310336}}</ref> Songwriters who applied for the selection were required to have Swiss citizenship or to have been residing in Switzerland for at least ten years and could submit up to three songs.<ref name="da rules">{{cite news |date=8 November 1956 |title=IIe Concours international de la Chanson |trans-title=2nd International Song Contest |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/324701/view?page=21 |access-date=27 July 2025 |work=Radio Je vois tout |location= |page=2085 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=34 |issue=45}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news |date=2 November 1956 |title=Europäischer Schlagerwettbewerb 1957 |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=TGW19561102-01.2.17.9 |access-date=30 July 2025 |work={{ill|Berner Tagwacht|de}} |page=4 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=64 |issue=268 |oclc=1367998098}}</ref> SRG SSR opened a submission window in autumn 1956, with the deadline on 5 January 1957.<ref name="da rules" /><ref name=":4" /> The broadcaster received 109 songs (69 in German, 22 in French, and 18 in Italian<ref name="langsubs">{{Cite web |title=Schweizer Ausscheidung - Finale Suisse - Finale Svizzera 1957 |url=https://vorstadtmusic.ch/1957.html |access-date=22 January 2025 |website=Vorstadt Music & Records}}</ref>) from 75 songwriters.<ref name=":0" />

The internal jury in [[Bern]] were tasked with choosing at most twenty songs<ref name="da rules"/> and ultimately selected eleven songs to compete in the selection.<ref name="bern">{{cite news |title=Concours National — Grand Prix Eurovision 1957 de la Chanson européene |trans-title=National Competition — Eurovision Grand Prix 1957 |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/325498/view?page=18&p=separate& |access-date=27 July 2025 |date=24 January 1957 |location= |page=18 |language=fr |work=Radio Je vois tout |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]]}}</ref><ref name="composer it"/>

The national final, entitled ''Internationaler Schlagerwettbewerb 1957'', was held on 11 February 1957 at 21:00 [[Central European Time|CET]] (20:00 [[Coordinated Universal Time|UTC]]) at the Embassysaal in [[Badrutt's Palace Hotel]], [[St. Moritz]].<ref name="composer it">{{cite news |title=Sarà scelta lunedi la più bella canzone svizzera |trans-title=The most beautiful Swiss song will be chosen on Monday |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=xbtXhJoB2WlOfa--QAJ4 |access-date=22 January 2025 |work=Eco di Locarno |date=9 February 1957 |location=[[Locarno]], Switzerland |page=3 |language=it |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}}}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite news |date=10 February 1957 |title=Télé-Suisse |work=Télévision Programme Magazine |page=23 |language=fr |volume=3 |issue=68 |oclc=472721214}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=10 February 1957 |title=Montag 11. Februar 1957 |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |pages=VI–VII |language=de |issue=6 |oclc=638310336}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=9 February 1957 |title=Anlässe dieser Tage |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=EDP19570209-01.2.6 |access-date=30 July 2025 |work={{ill|Engadiner Post|de}} |page=2 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=66 |issue=17 |issn=1661-0105 |oclc=806846627}}</ref> It was broadcast on [[Schweizer Fernsehen|German-]] and [[Télévision Suisse Romande|French-speaking Swiss Television]] as well as on the radio stations [[Radio SRF 1|Beromünster]], [[La Première (Switzerland)|Sottens]], and [[RSI Rete Uno|Monte Ceneri]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":14">{{Cite news |date=10 February 1957 |title=Fernseh-Programme |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |page=XXX |language=de |issue=6 |oclc=638310336}}</ref> The director was [[Franco Marazzi]].<ref name=":9" /> The program was presented by [[Heidi Abel]] in German and French, and by {{Interlanguage link|Giuseppe Albertini (journalist)|lt=Giuseppe Albertini|it|Giuseppe Albertini (giornalista)}} in Italian.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=17 February 1957 |title=Das schwarze Brett: Schlagertage in St. Moritz |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |page=24 |language=de |issue=7 |oclc=638310336}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite news |date=5 February 1957 |title=St. Moritz |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=EDP19570205-01.2.2.4 |access-date=30 July 2025 |work={{ill|Engadiner Post|de}} |page=1 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=66 |issue=15 |issn=1661-0105 |oclc=806846627}}</ref><ref name="heidi" /> The artists were accompanied by [[Radiotelevisione svizzera|RSI]]'s orchestra Radiosa under the musical direction of [[Fernando Paggi]].<ref name="heidi">{{cite news |last= |first= |date=12 February 1957 |title=Per una canzone «nazionale» |trans-title=For a "national" song |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=-r1ihpoB2WlOfa--GSDY |access-date=22 January 2025 |work=[[Giornale del Popolo]] |location=[[Lugano]], Switzerland |page=2 |language=it |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}} |volume=32 |issue=36 |issn=1660-9662 |oclc=1393541669}}</ref><ref name="all da scores">{{cite news |last=Marino |first= |date=13 February 1957 |title='L'enfant que j'étais' ha vinto a St. Moritz il Festival della canzone svizzera |trans-title='L'enfant que j'étais' wins the Swiss Song Festival in St. Moritz |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=_dL7mpoB2WlOfa--Tvdn |access-date=22 January 2025 |work=Libera Stampa |location=[[Lugano]], Switzerland |page=2 |language=it |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}} |volume=45 |issue=37 |oclc=732473625}}</ref><ref name="results claim 2">{{Cite magazine |date=21 February 1957 |title=Quelques instants avec Émile Gardaz et Géo Voumard |trans-title=A few moments with Émile Gardaz and Géo Voumard |url=https://scriptorium.ch/zoom/325522/view?page=11 |access-date=22 October 2024 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=11 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=35 |issue=8}}</ref> The eleven entries were performed by [[Lys Assia]], Jo Roland and Gianni Ferraresi, with Lys Assia performing five songs, Jo Roland three, and Gianni Ferraresi also three songs.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":5" /> Three entries were sung in German, four in French, and four in Italian.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Villani |first=Silvano |date=12 February 1957 |title=Trasmesso alla televisione: il Festival svizzero della canzone |work=[[Corriere della Sera]] |page=6 |language=it |volume=82 |issue=37 |oclc=1371227030}}</ref> The running order was decided by a draw.<ref name="stm jury" /> The overall sound and image quality of the broadcast was so low that three songs had to be repeated upon the request of the jury of St. Moritz.<ref name="all da scores" /><ref name=":10">{{Cite news |date=12 February 1957 |title=Deux Lausannois (et Lys Assia) remportent la finale suisse de la chanson |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/154854/view?page=10 |access-date=10 August 2025 |work=La Nouvelle Revue de Lausanne |page=10 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=89 |issue=35 |oclc=806845439}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> [[Los Paraguayos]] performed as the interval act.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 March 1957 |title=Melodischer Kampf um einen grossen Preis |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |pages=12–13 |language=de |issue=9 |oclc=638310336}}</ref> 

Four regional juries, located in [[Basel]] (representing radio [[Radio SRF 1|Beromünster]]), [[Geneva]] (for radio [[La Première (Switzerland)|Sottens]]), [[Lugano]] (for radio [[RSI Rete Uno|Monte Ceneri]]), and St. Moritz (representing Swiss Television), decided the winner.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="stm jury" /><ref name=":2" /> Each jury consisted of ten members, with each jury member giving one vote to their favourite song.<ref name="all da scores" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite news |date=14 February 1957 |title='L'enfant que j'étais' canzone svizzera 1957 |trans-title='L'enfant que j'étais' Swiss song of 1957 |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=zrtXhJoB2WlOfa--SQIx |access-date=24 September 2025 |work=L'Eco di Locarno |language=it |volume=32 |issue=19 |page=2 |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}}}}</ref><ref name="stm jury" /> The jury members from St. Mortiz were present within the location of the final, while the remaining juries delivered their votes in their respective cities.<ref name="all da scores" /> The ten jurors from Geneva consisted of Marius Berthet (jury president), Jean-Pierre Allenbach, Robert Burnier, {{ill|Raymond Colbert (radio personality)|lt=Raymond Colbert|fr}}, Jo Excoffier, Frank Guibat, Lisette Martin, Robert Pibouleau, Clairette Sacchi, and [[Julien-François Zbinden]].<ref name="stm jury">{{Cite magazine |date=7 February 1957 |title=Le Grand Prix Européen de la Chanson |trans-title=The European Song Grand Prix |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/325512/view?page=24&p=separate& |access-date=23 July 2025 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=24 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=35 |issue=6}}</ref> In the Luganese jury, Bruno Pagnamenta was the jury president.<ref name=":12" /> The juries gave their votes via telephone.<ref name=":10" />

Following the voting, three songs tied for first place with 8 votes each: "{{lang|fr|La Vie|i=no}}" and "{{lang|fr|Avec vingt sous|i=no}}", sung by Jo Roland, and "{{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}", performed by Lys Assia.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=3 March 1957 |title=Melodischer Kampf um einen grossen Preis |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |pages=12–13 |language=de |issue=9 |oclc=638310336}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> After all three songs had been performed once more, a revote of the tying entries took place to decide the winner.<ref name="results claim 2"/> The winner was the song "{{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}", composed by [[Géo Voumard]], with lyrics by [[Émile Gardaz]], arranged by Mario Robbiani, and performed by [[Lys Assia]].<ref name="all da scores" /><ref name=":2" /> The songwriters Gardaz and Voumard had already won both the national final and the Eurovision Song Contest for {{esccnty|Switzerland|y=1956|t=Switzerland in 1956}}, in both occasions also with Lys Assia as singer.<ref name=":42">{{Cite news |date=1 May 1956 |title=La finale suisse du concours international de la chanson |trans-title=The Swiss final of the international song contest |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=EXR19560501-01.2.74 |access-date=8 November 2023 |work=[[L'Express (Neuchâtel)|Feuille d'Avis de Neuchâtel]] |page=11 |language=fr}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite book |last=O'Connor |first=John Kennedy |title=The Eurovision Song Contest: The Official History |publisher=Carlton |year=2010 |isbn=978-1-84732-521-1 |edition=Updated |location=London |pages=8–9 |oclc=699877063}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite news |date=13 February 1957 |title=Cronaca Ticinese: Saranno ancora gli autori del fortunato 'Refrain' a rappresentare la Svizzera al Gran Premio della Canzone |url=http://www2.sbt.ti.ch/quotidiani-public-pdf/main_part.php?fullscreen=true&paper=gdp&day=13&month=2&year=1957&page=2 |access-date=18 ===Releases===
"{{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}" by [[Lys Assia]] was first recorded and released on a single under the same title in 1957.<ref name="lal">{{cite AV media |last=Assia |first=Lys |title=L'enfant Que J'étais |type=Vinyl |language=fr |publisher=[[Telefunken]] |id=U 55 039 }}</ref> In 1998, the song was featured in a CD compilation titled "{{lang|de|Concours Eurovision De La Chanson 1956-1998: Schweizer Beiträge|i=no}}", which compiled every Swiss Eurovision entry at the time.<ref name="vorstadt">{{cite AV media |last= |first= |title=Concours Eurovision De La Chanson 1956-1998: Schweizer Beiträge |type=CD |language=de |publisher=Vorstadt Records |id=VRS 990 001-2 }}</ref>

Jo Roland would also release "{{lang|fr|La Vie|i=no}}" and by "{{lang|fr|Avec vingt sous|i=no}}" in his debut single, titled after the former song, in 1957.<ref name="jrl">{{cite AV media |last=Roland |first=Jo |title=La Vie |type=Vinyl |language=fr |publisher=[[Decca Records|Decca]] |id=18 438 }}</ref><ref name="jo">{{Cite magazine |date=25 October 1962 |title=Un Oscar qui s'apelle: Jo Roland |trans-title=An Oscar named: Jo Roland |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/322510/view?page=5&p=separate& |access-date=1 November 2026 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=5 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume= |issue=}}</ref> Gianni Ferraresi would release "{{lang|it|Bellissima|i=no}}" two years later.<ref name="gfb">{{cite AV media |last=Ferraresi |first=Gianni |title=Bellissima |type=Vinyl |language=it |publisher={{ill|Music (casa discografica)|it|lt=Music}} |id=EPM 10141 }}</ref> Studio recordings of all competing entries have been preserved in the [[Swiss National Sound Archives]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Canzoni presentate al festival svizzero della canzone a Saint Moritz (DAT12995) |url=https://www.fonoteca.ch/cgi-bin/oecgi4.exe/inet_fnbasedetail?REC_ID=89781.027&LNG_ID=ENU |access-date=9 March 2026 |website=Swiss National Sound Archives (catalog) |publisher=[[Swiss National Sound Archives]] |place=[[Lugano]] |id=DAT12995}}</ref>

== At Eurovision ==
[[File:Lys Assia (1957).jpg|thumb|[[Lys Assia]] represented Switzerland in the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1957]]]]

At the Eurovision Song Contest 1957 in [[Frankfurt]], the Swiss entry was performed tenth and last in the running order, following {{esccnty|Denmark|y=1957}}.<ref name="1957results">{{cite web |title=Final of Frankfurt 1957 – Eurovision Song Contest |url=https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220517112718/https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final |archive-date=17 May 2022 |access-date=3 June 2022 |publisher=European Broadcasting Union}}</ref> The Swiss entry was conducted at the contest by the event's musical director [[Willy Berking]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Thorsson |first=Leif |title=Melodifestivalen genom tiderna: de Svenska uttagningarna och de internationella finalerna |last2=Verhage |first2=Martin |publisher=Premium |year=2006 |isbn=91-89136-29-2 |edition=2nd |location=Stockholm |page=350 |language=sv |oclc=185355414}}</ref> At the close of voting, Switzerland had received five votes in total; the country finished shared eight among the ten participants.<ref name="1957final">{{cite web |title=Frankfurt 1957 |url=https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final |publisher=Eurovision Song Contest |access-date=28 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327160227/https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final/results/switzerland |archive-date=27 March 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="1957detailed"/>

The contest was broadcast in Switzerland on French-speaking [[Télévision Suisse Romande|TSR]] with commentary by [[Robert Beauvais]], on [[SRF 1|German-speaking television]], as well as on radio [[Radio SRF 1|Beromünster]] and [[RTS Première|Sottens]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 March 1957 |title=Radio Beromünster + UKW |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=WVF19570301-02.2.20 |access-date=3 August 2025 |work=Walliser Volksfreund |page=3 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=38 |issue=17 |oclc=806848191}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2 March 1957 |title=Radio Sottens |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=LGE19570302-01.2.12 |access-date=3 August 2025 |work=[[La Gruyère (newspaper)|La Gruyère]] |page=3 |language=fr |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=76 |issue=26 |issn=2296-2409 |oclc=806828885}}</ref><ref name=":14" /> Excerpts were broadcast on 11 March 1957 at 20:00 CET on the second program of radio [[RSI Rete Uno|Monte Ceneri]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 March 1957 |title=Lundi 11 mars: Second programme |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/325528/view?page=29 |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=29 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=35 |issue=10}}</ref>

=== Voting ===
Each participating broadcaster assembled a ten-member jury panel.<ref name=":13">{{Cite journal |date=January–February 1957 |title=Grand Prix Eurovision 1957 de la Chanson européenne |journal=Bulletin de l'U.E.R. |language=fr |publisher=[[European Broadcasting Union]] |volume=8 |issue=41 |page= |pages=109–113 |oclc=473721192}}</ref> Every jury member could give one vote to their favourite song.<ref name=":13" />

'''''Mom Rajawongse'' Adulakit Kitiyakara''' ({{langx|th|อดุลกิติ์ กิติยากร}}; {{RTGS|''Adunlakit Kitiyakon''}}: 2 November 1930 – 5 May 2004), was the chief-president of the supreme judicature of Thailand, and former member of the [[Privy Council of Thailand]]. He was a member of the House of Kitiyakara, the Princely House descended from the [[Chakri dynasty]]. He was the elder brother of [[Sirikit|Queen Sirikit]], consort of [[Bhumibol Adulyadej|King Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX) of Thailand]].

==Biography==
Mom Rajawongse Adulakit was born on 2 November 1930, at Deves Palace in Bangkok. He was the second son of Prince (Mom Chao) [[Nakkhatra Mangkala]] (later the Prince of Chantaburi II, son of [[Kitiyakara Voralaksana|Prince Kitiyakara Voralaksana, Prince of Chantaburi]]) and Mom Luang [[Bua Kitiyakara|Bua Sanidvongs]]. His name was given by [[Prajadhipok|King Prajadhipok (Rama VII) of Siam]]. His name means ''The great honorary''.

He had three siblings: one elder brother and two younger sisters:
* [[Kalyanakit Kitiyakara|Prof. Dr. Mom Rajawongse Kalyanakit Kitiyakara]] (born 20 September 1929, died 15 May 1987)
* [[Sirikit|Mom Rajawongse Sirikit Kitiyakara]] (later Queen Sirikit of Thailand) (born 12 August 1932, died 24 October 2025)
* [[Busba Kitiyakara|Mom Rajawongse Busba Kitiyakara]] (born 2 August 1934)

When he was 2, his father was created Charge d' affaires of [[Washington, D.C.]], after the [[1932 Siamese Revolution]]. And Mom Luang Bua, his consort followed his husband to the United States after gave birth to the first daughter, [[Sirikit|Mom Rajawongse Sirikit]]. The couple moved to the United States with their first son [[Kalyanakit Kitiyakara|Mom Rajawongse Kalyanakit Kitiyakara]]. He lived with his grandmother [[Absornsaman Dhevakul|Princess (Mom Chao) Apsornsaman Kitiyakara]] and his aunt [[Chitbanchong Kitiyakara|Mom Chao Chitbanchong Kitiyakara]].

==Education and work==
Mom Rajawongse Adulakit graduated from  [[Saint Gabriel's College (Thailand)|Saint Gabriel's College]]. After his father was appointed Ambassador to the [[Court of St. James's]], (i.e. [[Thai Ambassador to the United Kingdom|Ambassador to the United Kingdom]]), he studied engineering in [[Portsmouth Technical College]]. After having graduated from college, he continued to study law at the Inn of Court (Middle Temple), the famous law school in [[England]].{{clarify|date=November 2017}}

When he moved back to [[Thailand]], he continued studying at The Institute of Legal Education of The Thai Bar. After graduation, he worked as a judge in [[Ministry of Justice (Thailand)|Ministry of Justice]]. Moreover, he worked as a teacher in the faculty of law, [[Thammasat University]]. In 1966, [[Bhumibol Adulyadej|King Bhumibol Adulyadej]] created him a judge of [[Chiang Mai]] Court. He and his family moved to Chiang Mai for 3 years. Later in 1974, he studied at the [[National Defence College of Thailand]]. After graduation, he was created President of Children and Family Court until he retired. He has been a member of the Privy Council since then.

==Marriage==
While he was in [[England]], he met his cousin, Princess Phasawali Yugala (daughter of Prince [[Bhanubandhu Yugala]] and [[Soiraya Sanidvongse|Mom Luang Soiraya Sanidvongse]]). Their relatives was from [[Suvabandhu Sanidvongse|Mom Rajawongse Suvabandhu Sanidvongse]], Princess Phansawali's grandfather was the elder brother of [[Sadan Sanidvongse|Mom Rajawongse Sadan Sanidvongse]], Adulakit's grandfather. They began engaged in February 1956. And then came back to Thailand. The marriage was performed by [[Bhumibol Adulyadej|King Bhumibol Adulyadej]] and [[Sirikit|Queen Sirikit]], Adulakit's younger sister at [[Klai Kangwon Palace]].

The couple have 2 daughters:

* ''Mom Luang'' [[Soamsawali|Soamsawali Kitiyakara]], (born 13 July 1957) later Princess Soamsawali of Thailand, married [[Vajiralongkorn|Crown Prince Maha Vajiralongkorn]], has 1 daughter, then divorced in 1991.
* ''Mom Luang'' [[Sarali Kitiyakara]], (born 8 April 1966) married Thiradej Chirathiwat, has 2 sons.

Mom Rajawongse Adulyakit Kitiyakara died on 5 May 2004, at [[Bangkok Hospital]], at the age of 74.

==Royal decorations==
* [[File:Order of Chula Chom Klao - 1st Class (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Knight Grand Cross (First Class) of the Most Illustrious [[Order of Chula Chom Klao]] (1991)
* [[File:Order of the White Elephant - Special Class (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Knight Grand Cordon (Special Class) of the Most Exalted [[Order of the White Elephant]] (1989)
* [[File:Order of the Crown of Thailand - Special Class (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Knight Grand Cordon (Special Class) of the Most Noble [[Order of the Crown of Thailand]] (1985)
* [[File:Chakrabarti Mala Medal (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Chakrabarti Mala Medal (1988)
* [[File:King Rama IX Royal Cypher Medal (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] King Rama IX Royal Cypher Medal, 2nd Class (1992)

At the time of the 2006 National Census, the village's population was 1,400 in 334 households.<ref name="2006 Ardabil Province"> {{cite web |script-title=fa:سرشماري عمومي نفوس و مسكن 1385 : استان |url=https://irandataportal.syr.edu/wp-content/uploads/Ardabil.xls |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115211527/https://irandataportal.syr.edu/wp-content/uploads/Ardabil.xls village as 1,305 people in 453 households.<ref name="2016 Ardabil Province"> {{cite web |script-title=fa:سرشماري عمومي نفوس و مسكن 1395 : استان اردبیل |trans-title=General Population and Housing Census 2016: Ardabil Province |language=fa |website={{lang|fa|rtl=yes|مرکز آمار ایران}} [Statistical Centre of Iran] |url=https://www.amar.org.ir/Portals/0/census/1395/results/abadi/CN95_HouseholdPopulationVillage_24.xlsx |access-date=19 June 2025}}</ref>

==Geography==
Andabil is on the northeastern outskirts of the city of [[Khalkhal, Ardabil|Khalkhal]], along Route 22.<ref name="WDB">{{cite web|url=http://www.worldcitydb.com/andabil_-4278016.html|title=Andabil|publisher=World City Database|access-date=July 2, 2009|archive-date=July 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200727213659/https://www.worldcitydb.com/andabil_-4278016.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> It is 1.2 miles from Khalkhal, 2.1 miles from [[Aliabad, Khalkhal|Aliabad]], 2.2 miles from [[Bagh, Ardabil|Bagh]], 2.1 miles from [[Khujin]] and 1.4 miles from [[Khaneqah-e Sadat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fallingrain.com/world/IR/32/Andabil.html|title=Andabil, Iran|publisher=Falling Rain Gazetteer|access-date=July 2, 2009}}</ref> Route 22 connects the village to Khalkhal city center to the southwest and to the town of Nav in the northeast, eventually joining the north–south direction Route 49 that connects to [[Azerbaijan]].<ref name="WDB"/>

1383163543.content:
{{Short description|None}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2015}} {{Use Australian English|date=May 2015}} This is a '''list''' of the current channels available on [[digital terrestrial television in Australia]]. The commercial channels available to viewers depend on location and station ownership. The process of [[Regional television in Australia#Aggregation|aggregation]] during the late 80s to mid 90s saw regional stations take on affiliations with metropolitan channels for programming, a practice that has continued into digital television with affiliated stations carrying various multichannels from their metropolitan counterparts. Metropolitan in this list therefore refers to the capitals of Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth, where stations were historically [[Owned-and-operated station|owned and operated]] by the networks rather than affiliates. Regional and remote in this list refers to all other areas which also cover the capitals of Canberra, Hobart and Darwin. In areas not covered by terrestrial transmissions, the digital channels are provided by the free-to-view [[Viewer Access Satellite Television|VAST]] satellite platform. The television channels on this platform are all encoded in [[H.264]] (MPEG-4) and subject to a MPEG-LA controlled transmission [[H.264#Patent licensing|patent licensing]] tax which is included in the VAST broadcaster cost and varies on viewership figures. Terrestrial transmissions, which do not inccur a patent licensing tax, have mostly transitioned to H.264 (MPEG-4), with select channels still using [[H.262]] (MPEG-2). {|class="wikitable" !colspan=3|Broadcaster availability |- |{{Yes|Nationwide}} |{{Beta|Metropolitan}} |{{Partial|Regional/remote}} |} ==Public broadcasters== === Australian Broadcasting Corporation === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%; width:100%;" ! width="10%"| DVB name ! width="6%" | LCN ! width="10%"| Broadcast hours ! width="10%"| Format ! width="28%"| Programming content ! width="33%"| Availability |- |rowspan=2|[[ABC TV (Australian TV channel)|ABC TV]] |2 |rowspan=4|24 hours |rowspan=2|[[576i]] [[standard-definition television|SDTV]]

'''Basanta Choudhury''' also known as '''Basanta Chowdhury''' (5 May 1928 – 20 June 2000), was an Indian actor in [[Cinema of West Bengal|Bengali]] and [[Bollywood|Hindi]] films. He worked with directors [[Asit Sen (actor)|Asit Sen]], [[Rajen Tarafdar]], Ajay Kar and Bijay Bose, often in leading roles.<ref>{{cite news |title=Films from the heart |url=https://www.thehindu.com/features/magazine/films-from-the-heart/article2417951.ece |work=The Hindu |date=3 September 2011 |access-date=2013-04-29}}</ref> He was a former [[Sheriff of Kolkata]].

Choudhury's collection of [[Kashmir shawl|Kashmiri]] and [[Persia]]n [[shawl]]s was enviable. Director [[Satyajit Ray]] admired those collections and used them for his masterpieces.

== Birth and childhood ==
Basanta Chowdhury was born into an affluent [[Kayastha]] [[Zamindar]] Datta Chowdhury family of Andul, [[Howrah]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.anandabazar.com/district/howrah-hoogly/%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%A6-%E0%A6%B2-%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%AC-%E0%A7%9C-%E0%A6%95-%E0%A6%98-%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%9C-%E0%A6%A6-%E0%A6%98%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AD-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%A8-1.88161|title=আন্দুল রাজবাড়িকে ঘিরে জাদুঘরের ভাবনা – Anandabazar|last=আবসার|first=নুরুল|work=Anandabazar Patrika|access-date=2018-07-26|language=bn}}</ref> In circa 1886, his great-great forefather Apurba Krishna Dutta Chaudhuri discontinued the surname 'Dutta' and moved from his ancestral place [[Andul]] to [[Nagpur]] to practice law. He later became the Law Lecturer in the Morris College (the present-day [[Vasantrao Naik Government Institute of Arts and Social Sciences|Vasantrao Naik Government Institute of Arts and Social Sciences (VNGIASS)]]). His son was Phani Bhusan Chaudhuri, whose son Shiddhish Chandra Chowdhury. Shiddhish and Kamala Devi had two sons – Basanta & Prasanta. Both of them grew up in Nagpur. Basanta graduated from Morris college. In 1945, he completed his Matriculation Examination from Deena Nath High School [[Nagpur]]. After shifting to [[Kolkata]], Chowdhury stayed in [[Ranikuthi]] in [[Tollygunge]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.anandabazar.com/supplementary/patrika/sweet-memorabilia-of-actor-basanta-chowdhury-written-by-shankarlal-bhattacharya-1.169176|title=রাগ বসন্ত|work=Anandabazar Patrika|access-date=2018-07-26|language=bn|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726203228/https://www.anandabazar.com/supplementary/patrika/sweet-memorabilia-of-actor-basanta-chowdhury-written-by-shankarlal-bhattacharya-1.169176|url-status=live}}</ref>

He was a [[numismatist]] i.e. an expert collector of [[Ganesha]] idols, rare coins, paper currency and was a collector of Kashmiri and Persian shawls.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://halfsamosa.in/6-best-films-basanta-choudhury-sophisticated-actor-almost-forgotten/|title=6 best films of Basanta Choudhury – a sophisticated actor almost forgotten{{!}} Half Samosa|date=2017-04-10|work=Half Samosa|access-date=2018-07-26|language=en-US|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726170105/http://halfsamosa.in/6-best-films-basanta-choudhury-sophisticated-actor-almost-forgotten/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Basanta Chowdhury..jpg|thumb|Basanta Chowdhury receiving [[Bengal Film Journalists' Association – Best Actor Award]] from then [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] Smt. [[Indira Gandhi]] in1966 CE for the movie '''Raja Rammohan''<nowiki/>'.]]
His first film was ''Mahaprasthaner Pathe'' by director Kartik Chattopadhay in 1952. Some of his memorable films are, ''Bhagaban Shri Krishna Chaitanya'', ''Jadu Bhatta'', ''Andhare Alo'', ''[[Deep Jwele Jaai]]'' with [[Suchitra Sen]], ''Anushtoop Chhanda'', ''Abhaya O Srikanta'', ''Raja Rammohan Roy'', ''Diba Ratrir Kabya'', ''[[Devi Chaudhurani]]''. He was also involved with amateur theater and radio.

== Awards ==
In 1965, actor Chowdhury was awarded the Best Actor Prize for his film "Raja Rammohan" by B.F.J.A. In 1996, he also received Bangla Stage Centenary [[Star Theatre, Kolkata|Star Theater]] award from [[University of Calcutta|Calcutta University]]. He had also acted in several Hindi films.

The actor had been the [[Sheriff of Kolkata]]. He was also appointed the Chairman of [[Nandan (Kolkata)|Nandan-West Bengal Film Centre]] in Kolkata.

== Death ==

The actor suffered from [[lung cancer]] for quite some time. He died on 20 June 2000 in Kolkata.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/archive/releases98/lyr2000/rjun2000/r21062000.html|title=Untitled Page|access-date=25 May 2016|archive-date=17 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617004500/http://pib.nic.in/archive/releases98/lyr2000/rjun2000/r21062000.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Wairoa Aerodrome''' {{airport codes|WIR|NZWO}} is a small airport located at the end of Airport Road, on the northern outskirts of [[Wairoa]], in [[Hawke's Bay]], New Zealand.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wairoadc.govt.nz/services/airport/ |title=Airport |publisher=Wairoa District Council |access-date=15 October 2019}}</ref> Wairoa Aerodrome provides a service for light aircraft and is used mainly for [[Air charter|charter]] operations. Airport landing charge in 2024 NZ$14. Touch and go charges are cumulative, so not suitable for circuit training


==Airlines and destinations==
[[Sunair]] connects Wairoa Aerodrome to [[Hawke's Bay Airport]] (Napier).

[[ATC-NS]] | speed = {{cvt|300|km/h}} | elevation = | map = [[File:Sanyo　Shinkansen map.png|frameless]] | map_state = show }} The {{nihongo|'''San'yō Shinkansen'''|山陽新幹線||{{lit|Southern Mountain new main line}}|lead=yes}} is a line of the Japanese [[Shinkansen]] [[high-speed rail]] network, connecting [[Shin-Ōsaka Station|Shin-Osaka]] in [[Osaka]] with [[Hakata Station]] in [[Fukuoka]], the two largest cities in western Japan. Operated by the [[West Japan Railway Company]] (JR West), it is a westward continuation of the [[Tōkaidō Shinkansen]] and also serves other major cities in between on [[Honshu]] and [[Kyushu]] islands such as [[Kobe]], [[Himeji, Hyōgo|Himeji]], [[Okayama]], [[Hiroshima]], and [[Kitakyushu]], through the [[Shin-Kanmon Tunnel]]. The [[Kyushu Shinkansen]] continues south of Hakata to [[Kagoshima]]. The San'yō Shinkansen connects Hakata with Osaka in two and a half hours, with trains operating at a maximum speed of {{convert|300|km/h|mph|abbr=on|0}} for most of the journey.{{cite magazine |script-title = ja:300km/hのトップランナー|trans-title= 300 km/h Top Runners|magazine=[[Japan Railfan Magazine]]| volume = 52| issue = 612| page =14| publisher = Kōyūsha Co., Ltd.| location = Japan| date = April 2012}} Some ''[[Nozomi (train)|Nozomi]]'' trains operate continuously on San'yō and Tōkaidō Shinkansen lines, connecting Tokyo and Hakata in five hours. == History == [[File:Hikari-railstar-osaka-2004-04.jpg|thumb|left|alt=700 series ''Hikari Rail Star'' train|700 series ''Hikari Rail Star'' train]] Construction of the San'yō Shinkansen between [[Shin-Ōsaka Station|Shin-Ōsaka]] and [[Okayama Station|Okayama]] was authorized on 9 September 1965, and commenced on March 16, 1967. Construction between [[Okayama Station|Okayama]] and [[Hakata station|Hakata]] commenced on 10 February 1970. The Shin-Ōsaka to Okayama segment opened on March 15, 1972; the remainder of the line opened on March 10, 1975.{{Cite journal |last=Taniguchi |first=Mamoru |date=1993 |title=The Japanese Shinkansen |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23288577 |journal=[[Built Environment (journal)|Built environment]] |volume=19 |issue=3/4 |page=216 |jstor=23288577 }} The first [[Hikari (train)|Hikari]] trains, using [[0 Series Shinkansen|0 series]] trains, made the Shin-Ōsaka to Hakata run in 3 hours 44 minutes. This was shortened to 2 hours 59 minutes in 1986 with an increase in maximum speed to {{convert|220|km/h|abbr=on}}. [[100 Series Shinkansen|100 series]] trains, introduced in 1989, boosted maximum speed to {{convert|230|km/h|abbr=on}} and reduced travel time to 2 hours 49 minutes. [[File:19970117 img1622.jpg|thumb|left|Damage following the [[Great Hanshin earthquake]] in [[Nishinomiya]], [[Hyogo]]]] Tokyo to Hakata ''[[Nozomi (train)|Nozomi]]'' services began on 18 March 1993, using [[300 Series Shinkansen|300 series]] trains. The Shin-Ōsaka to Hakata run was reduced to 2 hours 32 minutes, at a maximum speed of {{convert|270|km/h|abbr=on}}. On 22 March 1997, the [[500 Series Shinkansen|500 series]] entered service on ''Nozomi'' services between Shin-Ōsaka and Hakata, reducing that run to 2 hours 17 minutes at a maximum speed of {{convert|300|km/h|0|abbr=on}}. The [[700 Series Shinkansen|700 series]] was introduced on Tokyo-Hakata ''Nozomi'' services on 13 March 1999, coinciding with the opening of [[Asa Station]], and on 11 March 2000, 700 series trains were introduced on ''[[Hikari (train)|Hikari Rail Star]]'' services. Ogori Station was renamed Shin-Yamaguchi Station on 1 October 2003. The [[N700 Series Shinkansen|N700 series]] was launched on ''Nozomi'' services on 1 July 2007, with a top speed of {{convert|300|km/h|0|abbr=on}} (compared to {{convert|285|km/h|disp=or|abbr=on}} for the 700 series). From the start of the revised timetable on 12 March 2011, new ''[[Mizuho (train)|Mizuho]]'' and ''[[Sakura (train)|Sakura]]'' inter-running services commenced between Shin-Ōsaka and Kagoshima on the [[Kyushu Shinkansen]] using new [[N700 Series Shinkansen#8-car S sets (N700-7000 series)|N700-7000 and N700-8000]] series 8-car trainsets. This boosted JR West's market share in the Osaka-Kagoshima passenger market from 13% in March 2011 to 35% in March 2012. JR West began offering discounted advance purchase fares on this route in July 2013 in an effort to compete for market share with new [[low-cost carrier|low-cost airlines]] such as [[Peach Aviation|Peach]].{{cite news|title=Budget airlines challenge Shinkansen|url=http://the-japan-news.com/news/article/0000369788|access-date=19 July 2013|newspaper=Bloomberg|date=11 July 2013|archive-date=30 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130730234116/http://the-japan-news.com/news/article/0000369788|url-status=live}} With the launch of ''Mizuho'' and ''Sakura'' services, nearly all of the ''Hikari'' services operating solely on the San'yō Shinkansen (mostly ''Rail Star'' services) were discontinued as it was deemed redundant. === Future plans === In an announcement by JR Central, JR West, and JR Kyushu made on 17 October 2023, the companies stated that all onboard smoking rooms on the Tokaido, San'yo, and Kyushu Shinkansen trains would be abolished by Q2 2024.{{Cite web |last=Kinoshita |first=Kenji |date=17 October 2023 |title=東海道・山陽・九州新幹線の車内喫煙ルーム、2024年春にすべて廃止 |trans-title=All smoking rooms on Tokaido, Sanyo, and Kyushu Shinkansen trains will be abolished in spring 2024. |url=https://news.mynavi.jp/article/20231017-2795090/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231018011801/https://news.mynavi.jp/article/20231017-2795090/ |archive-date=18 October 2023 |access-date=19 October 2023 |website=MyNavi Corporation}} In addition, all smoking rooms located on station platforms on the Sanyo Shinkansen would also be abolished. In July 2024 JR West announced that the [[500 Series Shinkansen|500 Series]] trains would be phased out, and trains on the San'yō Shinkansen standardized to the [[N700S Series Shinkansen|N700 Series]]. Four of the existing 500 Series trainsets are expected to be retired by 2026, with the last two retired by 2027.{{cite web |url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUF195CD0Z10C24A7000000/|title=JR西日本、新幹線500系が27年引退へ 車両の共通化進む|date=24 July 2024|publisher=The Nikkei|access-date=24 July 2024|language=ja}} == Service == === Stopping patterns === ''Kodama'' trains stop at all stations; other services have varying stopping patterns. All trains stop at Shin-Osaka, Shin-Kobe, Okayama, Hiroshima, Kokura, and Hakata. Travelers using a [[Japan Rail Pass]] are required to purchase a special ticket to use the express ''Nozomi'' or ''Mizuho'' services. '''Korn Dabbaransi''' ({{langx|th|กร ทัพพะรังสี}}, {{RTGS|Kon Thappharangsi}}, alternatively transcribed as '''Thapparangsi''' or ''Dabaransi'', {{IPA|th|kɔːn tʰáppʰáraŋsǐː}}; born 14 September 1945) is a Thai politician. He was the leader of the [[National Development Party (Thailand)|National Development Party]] from 1998 to 2003. Korn served as deputy prime minister and as a cabinet minister in several governments. He currently serves as the President of the Thai-Chinese Friendship Association.

==Family and education==
Korn Dapparansi is a fourth generation [[Thai Chinese]]. He is a grandson of former deputy prime minister [[Phin Choonhavan]] and a nephew of former prime minister [[Chatichai Choonhavan]].<ref>{{Citation |first=Yoko |last=Ueda |chapter=The Entrepreneurs of Khorat |title=Money & power in provincial Thailand |publisher=NIAS Publishing |year=2000 |page=182 |isbn=9788787062701 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-gW9Z0-q_xwC&dq=korn+thapparangsi&pg=PA182}}</ref><ref>[http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/201901/17/WS5c3fd8e9a3106c65c34e4f05_2.html Close bond with China inherited from ancestors]</ref> He graduated from [[Saint Gabriel's College, Bangkok]] and the [[University of Massachusetts]].<ref name="APECF"/>

==Political career==
He entered politics in 1974, representing the [[Thai Nation Party]] of his uncles Chatichai and [[Pramarn Adireksarn]]. Korn served as Deputy Minister of Industry in the government of General [[Prem Tinsulanonda]] from 1986 to 1988.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_44.htm Assembly XLIV] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120723054321/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_44.htm |date=2012-07-23 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> He was a minister to the [[Office of the Prime Minister (Thailand)|Office of Prime Minister]] in his uncle Chatichai's cabinet from 1990 to 1991.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_46.htm Assembly XLVI] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605013950/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_46.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> After the military coup d'état of 1991, he was again Minister to the Office of Prime Minister in the short-lived military-backed government of [[Suchinda Kraprayoon]].<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_48.htm Assembly XLVIII] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014013/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_48.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> After the events of the [[Black May (1992)|Black May]] 1992, that toppled the Suchinda administration, he left the Thai Nation Party and founded the [[National Development Party (Thailand)|National Development Party]], together with Chatichai.<ref>{{Citation |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o2zfXluLbtcC&dq=chart+pattana+Party+thailand&pg=PA7 |first=Surin |last=Maisrikrod |title=Thailands Two General Elections in 1992: Democracy Sustained |publisher=Institute of South East Asian Studies |year=1992 |page=7|isbn=9789813016521 }}</ref>

In December 1994, Korn was again appointed Minister to the Office of Prime Minister by Prime Minister [[Chuan Leekpai]], he held that position until the government lost its majority in 1995.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_50.htm Assembly L] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126195458/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_50.htm |date=2012-01-26 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> In [[Chavalit Yongchaiyudh]]'s coalition government, Korn held the position of Deputy Prime Minister and [[Ministry of Industry (Thailand)|Minister of Industry]] from 1996 to 1997.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_52.htm Assembly LII] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014117/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_52.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> In 1998, Korn took over the chairmanship of the National Development Party from Chatichai. In October of that year, he was made Deputy Prime Minister again under Chuan Leekpai, holding the [[Ministry of Public Health (Thailand)|public health portfolio]] additionally.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_53.htm Assembly LIII] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110821105143/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_53.htm |date=2011-08-21 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref>

In the succeeding cabinet of [[Thaksin Shinawatra]], Korn was again Deputy Prime Minister from March 2002 to November 2003, when Thaksin dropped the National Development Party from his coalition. Thereupon Korn defected to the Prime Minister's [[Thai Rak Thai Party]].<ref>{{Citation |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_33MsnXELzIC&dq=%22chart+pattana%22&pg=PA32 |first=Michael Kelly |last=Connors |chapter=Thaksin's Thailand: Thai Politics in 2003-04 |title=Thailand's Economic Recovery |publisher=Institute of Southeast Asian Studies |year=2006 |page=32|isbn=9789812303523 }}</ref> He was called up to the cabinet as [[Ministry of Science and Technology (Thailand)|Minister of Science and Technology]] again in March 2004, serving until August 2005.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_54.htm Assembly LIV] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014148/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_54.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref><ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_55.htm Assembly LV] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014222/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_55.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref>

In 2007, Korn left Thai Rak Thai for the [[Pracharaj Party|Royalist People's Party]] (Pracharaj) of [[Sanoh Thienthong]], became deputy leader, but resigned from the party in October of the same year, to re-join the Thai Nation Party after 15 years.<ref>{{Citation |title=Mr. Korn quits Pracharaj to join Chart Thai |publisher=NNT National News Bureau of Thailand |date=31 October 2007 |url=http://thainews.prd.go.th/en/news.php?id=255010310016 |accessdate=22 March 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715184908/http://thainews.prd.go.th/en/news.php?id=255010310016 |archive-date=15 July 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Other offices==
Korn was the president of the [[International Badminton Federation]] (IBF).<ref name="APECF">[http://www.apecf.org/en/leadership/korn_dabbaransi.html Co-Chairman: Korn Dabbaransi – Former Deputy Prime Minister of Thailand], Asia Pacific Exchange & Cooperation Foundation, retrieved on 22 March 2012</ref> He has been the chairman of the [[Thai-Chinese Friendship Association]] since 2002.<ref>{{Citation |first=Sun |last=Guangyong |title=Thai diplomat: CPC serves people  |newspaper=People's Daily Online |date=22 June 2011 |url=http://english.people.com.cn/90001/90780/7417149.html |accessdate=22 March 2012}}</ref>

==Honours==
===National honours===
* [[File:Order of the White Elephant - Special Class (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Knight Grand Cordon (Special Class) of the Most Exalted [[Order of the White Elephant]] (1989)
* [[File:Order of the Crown of Thailand - Special Class (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Knight Grand Cordon (Special Class) of the Most Noble [[Order of the Crown of Thailand]] (1988)
* [[File:Serving Free Peoples Medal (Thailand) ribbon.svg|60px]] Serving Free People's Medal (1968)

===Foreign honours===
* {{flag|Brunei}}:
** [[File:First_Class_of_the_Order_of_Paduka_Seri_Laila_Jasa_(PSLJ).svg|60x60px]] First Class of the Most Distinguished [[Order of Paduka Seri Laila Jasa]] (2002)<ref>ราชกิจจานุเบกษา, [http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/00104046.PDF แก้คำผิด ประกาศสำนักนายกรัฐมนตรี เรื่อง พระราชทานพระบรมราชานุญาตให้ประดับเครื่องราชอิสริยาภรณ์ต่างประเทศ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330162545/http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/00104046.PDF |date=2019-03-30 }}, เล่ม ๑๑๙ ตอนที่ ๑๙ ข หน้า ๒๗, ๑๒ พฤศจิกายน ๒๕๔๕</ref>
* {{flag|Sweden}}:
** [[File:Order of the Polar Star (after 1975) - Commander Grand Cross.svg|60px]] Commander Grand Cross of the [[Order of the Polar Star]] (2003)<ref>ราชกิจจานุเบกษา, [http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/00122104.PDF ประกาศสำนักนายกรัฐมนตรี เรื่อง พระราชทานพระบรมราชานุญาตให้ประดับเครื่องราชอิสริยาภรณ์ต่างประเทศ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131006113303/http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/00122104.PDF |date=2013-10-06 }}, เล่ม ๑๒๐ ตอนที่ ๔ ข หน้า ๕, ๗ มีนาคม ๒๕๔๖</ref>

==Political career==
He entered politics in 1974, representing the [[Thai Nation Party]] of his uncles Chatichai and [[Pramarn Adireksarn]]. Korn served as Deputy Minister of Industry in the government of General [[Prem Tinsulanonda]] from 1986 to 1988.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_44.htm Assembly XLIV] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120723054321/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_44.htm |date=2012-07-23 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> He was a minister to the [[Office of the Prime Minister (Thailand)|Office of Prime Minister]] in his uncle Chatichai's cabinet from 1990 to 1991.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_46.htm Assembly XLVI] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605013950/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_46.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> After the military coup d'état of 1991, he was again Minister to the Office of Prime Minister in the short-lived military-backed government of [[Suchinda Kraprayoon]].<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_48.htm Assembly XLVIII] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014013/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_48.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> After the events of the [[Black May (1992)|Black May]] 1992, that toppled the Suchinda administration, he left the Thai Nation Party and founded the [[National Development Party (Thailand)|National Development Party]], together with Chatichai.<ref>{{Citation |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o2zfXluLbtcC&dq=chart+pattana+Party+thailand&pg=PA7 |first=Surin |last=Maisrikrod |title=Thailands Two General Elections in 1992: Democracy Sustained |publisher=Institute of South East Asian Studies |year=1992 |page=7|isbn=9789813016521 }}</ref>

In December 1994, Korn was again appointed Minister to the Office of Prime Minister by Prime Minister [[Chuan Leekpai]], he held that position until the government lost its majority in 1995.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_50.htm Assembly L] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126195458/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_50.htm |date=2012-01-26 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> In [[Chavalit Yongchaiyudh]]'s coalition government, Korn held the position of Deputy Prime Minister and [[Ministry of Industry (Thailand)|Minister of Industry]] from 1996 to 1997.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_52.htm Assembly LII] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014117/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_52.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref> In 1998, Korn took over the chairmanship of the National Development Party from Chatichai. In October of that year, he was made Deputy Prime Minister again under Chuan Leekpai, holding the [[Ministry of Public Health (Thailand)|public health portfolio]] additionally.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_53.htm Assembly LIII] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110821105143/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_53.htm |date=2011-08-21 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref>

In the succeeding cabinet of [[Thaksin Shinawatra]], Korn was again Deputy Prime Minister from March 2002 to November 2003, when Thaksin dropped the National Development Party from his coalition. Thereupon Korn defected to the Prime Minister's [[Thai Rak Thai Party]].<ref>{{Citation |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_33MsnXELzIC&dq=%22chart+pattana%22&pg=PA32 |first=Michael Kelly |last=Connors |chapter=Thaksin's Thailand: Thai Politics in 2003-04 |title=Thailand's Economic Recovery |publisher=Institute of Southeast Asian Studies |year=2006 |page=32|isbn=9789812303523 }}</ref> He was called up to the cabinet as [[Ministry of Science and Technology (Thailand)|Minister of Science and Technology]] again in March 2004, serving until August 2005.<ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_54.htm Assembly LIV] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014148/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_54.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref><ref>[http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_55.htm Assembly LV] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605014222/http://www.cabinet.thaigov.go.th/eng/cab_55.htm |date=2011-06-05 }}, The Cabinet, retrieved 22 March 2012</ref>

In 2007, Korn left Thai Rak Thai for the [[Pracharaj Party|Royalist People's Party]] (Pracharaj) of [[Sanoh Thienthong]], became deputy leader, but resigned from the party in October of the same year, to re-join the Thai Nation Party after 15 years.<ref>{{Citation |title=Mr. Korn quits Pracharaj to join Chart Thai |publisher=NNT National News Bureau of Thailand |date=31 October 2007 |url=http://thainews.prd.go.th/en/news.php?id=255010310016 |accessdate=22 March 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715184908/http://thainews.prd.go.th/en/news.php?id=255010310016 |archive-date=15 July 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Other offices==
Korn was the president of the [[International Badminton Federation]] (IBF).<ref name="APECF">[http://www.apecf.org/en/leadership/korn_dabbaransi.html Co-Chairman: Korn Dabbaransi – Former Deputy Prime Minister of Thailand], Asia Pacific Exchange & Cooperation Foundation, retrieved on 22 March 2012</ref> He has been the chairman of the [[Thai-Chinese Friendship Association]] since 2002.<ref>{{Citation |first=Sun |last=Guangyong |title=Thai diplomat: CPC serves people  |newspaper=People's Daily Online |date=22 June 2011 |url=http://english.people.com.cn/90001/90780/7417149.html |accessdate=22 March 2012}}</ref>

Naathapit Lamsam | partner = | relatives = | signature = | website = | footnotes = }} '''Banthoon Lamsam '''({{langx|th|บัณฑูร ล่ำซำ}}; {{RTGS|''Banthun Lamsam''}}, or nicknamed '''Pan''' (ปั้น);Matichon Daily Newspaper. Year 35 No.12444. Thursday April 5, 2012. ISSN 1686-8188. page 17 {{zh|t=伍萬通}}; born 15 January 1953 (2496 [[Buddhist calendar|BE]])) is a Thai business executive and the successor to the family business, Lamsam. He is the son of [[Bancha Lamsam]] and Thanphuying Sam-aungvarn Lamsam (maiden name Devakula; half-sister of M.R. [[Pridiyathorn Devakula]]). The [[Lamsam family]] is one of the wealthiest and most powerful families in Thailand.{{cite web|url=http://library.uru.ac.th/webdb/images/sakulthai13.htm|title=สกุลไทย (Sakul Thai Magazine). ชีวิตและงานของ บัณฑูร ล่ำซำ กรรมการผู้จัดการและประธานเจ้าหน้าที่บริหารธนาคารกสิกรไทย (Life and Work of Bantoon Lamsam, President and CEO of KBank).|access-date=September 1, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080102235821/http://library.uru.ac.th/webdb/images/sakulthai13.htm|archive-date=January 2, 2008|url-status=dead}} Bantoon is Lamsam 5th generation and heading family's banking and insurance flagship. He is currently the Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of [[Kasikornbank]], the top financial service provider group in Thailand. == Early life == Banthoon Lamsam was born on 15 January 1953, son of Bancha Lamsam and [[Thanphuying]] Sam-aungvarn Lamsam (maiden name [[Mom Rajawongse]] Sam-aungvarn Devakula; daughter of Prince [[Priditheppong Devakula]] and Mom Rajawongse Sa-ang Pramoj). Bantoon has two younger sisters. Bantoon is a grandson of [[Choti Lamsam]] who founded [[Kasikornbank]] in 1945 as Thai Farmers Bank. Banthoon graduated from [[Saint Gabriel's College, Bangkok]] and [[Srinakharinwirot University Prasarnmit Demonstration School]]. He studied at [[Phillips Exeter Academy]] from 1967 to 1971{{Cite web |url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2005/11/07/entertainment/data/entertainment_19080450.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2015-11-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117023309/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2005/11/07/entertainment/data/entertainment_19080450.html |archive-date=2015-11-17 |url-status=dead }} before going on to earn a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from [[Princeton University]] and a masters of business administration (MBA) from [[Harvard Business School]] (HBS). After graduation, he spent two years with the military's Directorate of Joint Intelligence in the Ministry of Defence. In 1979, Banthoon joined Thai Farmers Bank (later changed to Kasikornbank) in the international banking department, where he was promoted to first vice president in 1986. In 1987 he moved to the domestic banking department as a senior vice president. In 1992, Banthoon was nominated president as of Thai Farmers Bank (TFB).{{Cite web|url = http://www.kasikornbank.com/picture1/BoardofDirecter/Documents/BANTHOON_EN.pdf|title = Bantoon Lamsam, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, Kasikornbank|access-date = September 26, 2014|website = Kasikorn }} After the [[1997 Asian financial crisis]] (known as วิกฤตต้มยำกุ้ง, literally translated as [[Tom Yam|Tom Yam Kung]] crisis), he was the first to introduce the term "reengineering" to Thailand's banking industry. The Lamsam family became a minority shareholder of Kasikornbank. Banthoon Lamsam is an important contributor to the [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democratic Party]]. Banthoon was skeptical of the country's economic policies during [[Thaksin Shinawatra|Pol. Lt. Col Thaksin Shinawatra]]'s term as the prime minister of Thailand, and it was rumored that he had been approached by the Democratic Party for the position of the party leader in 2004.{{cite web|url=http://www.thairath.co.th/content/432603|title=Thairath Online. เปิดประวัติผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิ 'ซุปเปอร์บอร์ด รสก.' เป็นใครมาจากไหน?.|date=27 June 2014 |access-date=July 24, 2014}} In 2002, Banthoon became president and CEO of TFB. In 2003, he changed the logo and name of the bank from Thai Farmers Bank (TFB) to the current name, Kasikornbank (KBank), improvising Chinese characters style into the logo, "K". In 2010, after Dr. Prasarn Trairatvorakul, then the president of KBank, left to become the Governor of the [[Bank of Thailand]], Banthoon assumed the role of both president and CEO of KBank. He also instituted a senior executive position called "domain coordinator" and nominated four executive vice presidents to assume the positions of business domain, risk domain, infrastructure domain, and resource domain. Two of these executives later became the presidents of KBank and the other two became board directors. In May 2013, Banthoon published a 608-page novel, ''Sinaeha Montra Lanna'', which he wrote in 13 months. The publisher printed 20,000 copies in the first two months.รายงานพิเศษ มติชนสุดสัปดาห์ (Matichon Weekend Special Report). Volume 33, No. 1716. 5–11 July 2013. ISSN 1686-8196{{RP|86}} Banthoon Lamsam's hobbies are playing the saxophone and canoeing. He is also feng shui believer.{{Cite news|url = https://www.forbes.com/profile/banthoon-lamsam/|title = #21 Banthoon Lamsam, Thailand's 50 Richest|date = June 2014|work = Forbes|access-date = 26 September 2014}} == Current profession == * Chairman of the Board (2013) and Chief Executive Officer (since 1991), KASIKORNBANK PLC * Director of Pukha Holdings, Pukha Realty, Pukha Go, Pukha Nanfa Hotel * Chairman and Manager, Mahamakuta Rajavidyalaya Foundation under Royal Patronage{{cite web|url=https://thaipublica.org/2011/10/phra-wannarat-buntoon/|title=THAIPUBLICA. สนทนาธรรมกับ "สมเด็จพระวันรัต – บัณฑูร ล่ำซำ". |date=2 October 2011 |access-date = July 25, 2014}} * Treasurer, [[Wat]] Bovoranives Vihara and Wat Nyanasamvararam Varamahavihara Buddhist Monasteries{{cite web|url=http://www.kasikornbank.com/EN/Investors/ShareholderServices/GeneralMeeting/NoticeOfMeeting/Annex03_E.pdf|title=Annex 3, AGM #101 Notice of Meeting, April 3, 2013}} {{cite web|url=http://www.kasikornbank.com/EN/AboutUs/BoardOfDirectors/Pages/CEO.aspx |title=Kasikornbank's Board of Directors. |access-date = July 25, 2014}} == Work experience == 1977 (เนื่องในโอกาสพระราชพิธีฉัตรมงคล วันที่ ๕ พฤษภาคม ๒๕๕๐ จำนวน ๑๒๒ ราย), เล่ม ๑๒๔, ตอน ๖ ข, ๕ พฤษภาคม พ.ศ. ๒๕๕๐, หน้า ๑] * 2003 - Tatiya Chunlachomklao Wiset, The Most Illustrious Order of Chula Chom He studied at [[Phillips Exeter Academy]] from 1967 to 1971{{Cite web |url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2005/11/07/entertainment/data/entertainment_19080450.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2015-11-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117023309/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2005/11/07/entertainment/data/entertainment_19080450.html |archive-date=2015-11-17 |url-status=dead }} before going on to earn a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from [[Princeton University]] and a masters of business administration (MBA) from [[Harvard Business School]] (HBS). After graduation, he spent two years with the military's Directorate of Joint Intelligence in the Ministry of Defence. In 1979, Banthoon joined Thai Farmers Bank (later changed to Kasikornbank) in the international banking department, where he was promoted to first vice president in 1986. In 1987 he moved to the domestic banking department as a senior vice president. In 1992, Banthoon was nominated president as of Thai Farmers Bank (TFB).{{Cite web|url = http://www.kasikornbank.com/picture1/BoardofDirecter/Documents/BANTHOON_EN.pdf|title = Bantoon Lamsam, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, Kasikornbank|access-date = September 26, 2014|website = Kasikorn }} After the [[1997 Asian financial crisis]] (known as วิกฤตต้มยำกุ้ง, literally translated as [[Tom Yam|Tom Yam Kung]] crisis), he was the first to introduce the term "reengineering" to Thailand's banking industry. The Lamsam family became a minority shareholder of Kasikornbank. Banthoon Lamsam is an important contributor to the [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democratic Party]]. Banthoon was skeptical of the country's economic policies during [[Thaksin Shinawatra|Pol. Lt. Col Thaksin Shinawatra]]'s term as the prime minister of Thailand, and it was rumored that he had been approached by the Democratic Party for the position of the party leader in 2004.{{cite web|url=http://www.thairath.co.th/content/432603|title=Thairath Online. เปิดประวัติผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิ 'ซุปเปอร์บอร์ด รสก.' เป็นใครมาจากไหน?.|date=27 June 2014 |access-date=July 24, 2014}} In 2002, Banthoon became president and CEO of TFB. In 2003, he changed the logo and name of the bank from Thai Farmers Bank (TFB) to the current name, Kasikornbank (KBank), improvising Chinese characters style into the logo, "K". In 2010, after Dr. Prasarn Trairatvorakul, then the president of KBank, left to become the Governor of the [[Bank of Thailand]], Banthoon assumed the role of both president and CEO of KBank. He also instituted a senior executive position called "domain coordinator" and nominated four executive vice presidents to assume the positions of business domain, risk domain, infrastructure domain, and resource domain. Two of these executives later became the presidents of KBank and the other two became board directors. In May 2013, Banthoon published a 608-page novel, ''Sinaeha Montra Lanna'', which he wrote in 13 months. The publisher printed 20,000 copies in the first two months.รายงานพิเศษ มติชนสุดสัปดาห์ (Matichon Weekend Special Report). Volume 33, No. 1716. 5–11 July 2013. ISSN 1686-8196{{RP|86}} Banthoon Lamsam's hobbies are playing the saxophone and canoeing. He is also feng shui believer.{{Cite news|url = https://www.forbes.com/profile/banthoon-lamsam/|title = #21 Banthoon Lamsam, Thailand's 50 Richest|date = June 2014|work = Forbes|access-date = 26 1383122985.content:
{{Short description|Thai politician (born 1986)}} {{Infobox officeholder | name = Akanat Promphan | native_name = {{nobold|เอกนัฏ พร้อมพันธุ์}} | image = Akanat Promphan November 22, 2024.jpg | caption = Akanat in November, 2024 | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1986|01|12|mf=y}} | birth_place = [[Bangkok]], Thailand | party = [[Bhumjaithai Party|Bhumjaithai]] (since 2025) | other_party = [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democrat]] (2011–2022)
[[United Thai Nation Party|United Thai Nation]] (2022–2024) | spouse = | profession = | education = [[St John's College, Oxford]] (BS, MS) | office = [[Ministry of Energy (Thailand)|Minister of Energy]] | term_start = 30 March 2026 | term_end = | successor = | prime_minister = [[Anutin Charnvirakul]] | predecessor = Atthaphon Rerkpiboon | office2 = [[United Thai Nation Party|Secretary-General of the United Thai Nation Party]] | office1 = [[Ministry of Industry (Thailand)|Minister of Industry]] | predecessor1 = [[Pimpatra Wichaikul]] | prime_minister1 = [[Paetongtarn Shinawatra]] | successor1 = Thanakorn Wangboonkongchana | term_start1 = 3 September 2024 | term_end1 = 19 September 2025 | term_start2 = 3 August 2022 | term_end2 = 16 September 2025 | predecessor2 = [[Thandee Hongrattanauthai]] | office3 = Member of the House of Representatives | term_start3 = 3 July 2011 | term_end3 = 8 December 2013 | constituency3 = Bangkok 29 | successor3 = Supaporn Kongwutpanya | relatives = [[Suthep Thaugsuban]] (stepfather) }} '''Akanat Promphan''' ({{langx|th|เอกนัฏ พร้อมพันธุ์}}, {{RTGS|Ekanat Phromphan}}; born 12 January 1986) is a Thai politician and [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democrat]] [[Parliament of Thailand|MP]] who served as [[Private Secretary]] to his stepfather Deputy Prime Minister [[Suthep Thaugsuban]] in the government of [[Abhisit Vejjajiva]] and as a spokesman for the [[People's Democratic Reform Committee]] protest movement.{{Cite web |date=2024-09-04 |title=Meet Akanat Promphan, Thailand's new industry minister |url=https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40041183 |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=nationthailand |language=en-US}} ==Early life and education== Akanat was born on 12 January 1986 in [[Bangkok]] as the second son of Pornthep Techapaibul and Srisakul Promphan, who later divorced. His father, Pornthep, once served as a deputy minister in the government of [[Chuan Leekpai]], while his mother, sister of veteran Democrat politician [[Niphon Promphan]], eventually remarried [[Suthep Thaugsuban]], who served as [[Deputy Prime Minister of Thailand]] from 2008 to 2011.{{cite news|title=When women become the talk behind politics|url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/02/politics/politics_30096924.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304172654/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/02/politics/politics_30096924.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2009|accessdate=15 September 2015|work=[[The Nation (Thailand)|The Nation]]|date=2 March 2009}}{{cite news|last1=Sinlapalavan|first1=Budsarakham|title=Fast-tracked to fame|url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/15/opinion/opinion_30097933.php|accessdate=15 September 2015|work=[[The Nation (Thailand)|The Nation]]|date=15 March 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064640/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/15/opinion/opinion_30097933.php|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} He attended [[Saint Gabriel's College, Bangkok]] until he was 10, after which he studied in Australia and then at [[Charterhouse School]] in the United Kingdom. He read engineering, economics and management at [[St John's College, Oxford]], receiving a bachelor's and a master's degree. ==Political career== Akanat entered politics shortly after graduating from Oxford, becoming private secretary to his stepfather, Suthep, then Deputy Prime Minister. Akanat was subsequently elected a [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democrat]] Member of Parliament representing Bangkok in the [[2011 Thai general election|2011 general elections]]. At 25, he was the youngest MP elected that year. He and other members of his family received acclaim for his work during the [[2011 Thailand floods]], where he delivered food and other supplies to aid kitchens in Bangkok and Southern Thailand.{{cite news|title=All for one, one for all|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/print/383605/|accessdate=15 September 2015|work=[[Bangkok Post]]}} In June 2013 he resigned from Parliament, to help lead the [[People's Democratic Reform Committee]] dedicated to ousting the government of [[Yingluck Shinawatra]], and served as the organisation's spokesman. After the [[2014 Thai coup d'état|removal of the Yingluck government and coup d'état in 2014]], Akanat joined Suthep in being ordained as a monk for a year. In 2022 Akanat resigned from Democrat Party and became secretary-general of the [[United Thai Nation Party]] on 3 August 2022. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Promphan, Akanat}} [[Category:1986 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Alumni of St John's College, Oxford]] [[Category:Ministers of industry of Thailand|Akanat Promphan]] [[Category:Paetongtarn cabinet|Akanat Promphan]] {{Thailand-politician-stub}}

[[United Thai Nation Party|United Thai Nation]] (2022–2024) | spouse = | profession = | education = [[St John's College, Oxford]] (BS, MS) | office = [[Ministry of Energy (Thailand)|Minister of Energy]] | term_start = 30 March 2026 | term_end = | successor = | prime_minister = [[Anutin Charnvirakul]] | predecessor = Atthaphon Rerkpiboon | office2 = [[United Thai Nation Party|Secretary-General of the United Thai Nation Party]] | office1 = [[Ministry of Industry (Thailand)|Minister of Industry]] | predecessor1 = [[Pimpatra Wichaikul]] | prime_minister1 = [[Paetongtarn Shinawatra]] | successor1 = Thanakorn Wangboonkongchana | term_start1 = 3 September 2024 | term_end1 = 19 September 2025 | term_start2 = 3 August 2022 | term_end2 = 16 September 2025 | predecessor2 = [[Thandee Hongrattanauthai]] | office3 = Member of the House of Representatives | term_start3 = 3 July 2011 | term_end3 = 8 December 2013 | constituency3 = Bangkok 29 | successor3 = Supaporn Kongwutpanya | relatives = [[Suthep Thaugsuban]] (stepfather) }} '''Akanat Promphan''' ({{langx|th|เอกนัฏ พร้อมพันธุ์}}, {{RTGS|Ekanat Phromphan}}; born 12 January 1986) is a Thai politician and [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democrat]] [[Parliament of Thailand|MP]] who served as [[Private Secretary]] to his stepfather Deputy Prime Minister [[Suthep Thaugsuban]] in the government of [[Abhisit Vejjajiva]] and as a spokesman for the [[People's Democratic Reform Committee]] protest movement.{{Cite web |date=2024-09-04 |title=Meet Akanat Promphan, Thailand's new industry minister |url=https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40041183 |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=nationthailand |language=en-US}} ==Early life and education== Akanat was born on 12 January 1986 in [[Bangkok]] as the second son of Pornthep Techapaibul and Srisakul Promphan, who later divorced. His father, Pornthep, once served as a deputy minister in the government of [[Chuan Leekpai]], while his mother, sister of veteran Democrat politician [[Niphon Promphan]], eventually remarried [[Suthep Thaugsuban]], who served as [[Deputy Prime Minister of Thailand]] from 2008 to 2011.{{cite news|title=When women become the talk behind politics|url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/02/politics/politics_30096924.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304172654/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/02/politics/politics_30096924.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2009|accessdate=15 September 2015|work=[[The Nation (Thailand)|The Nation]]|date=2 March 2009}}{{cite news|last1=Sinlapalavan|first1=Budsarakham|title=Fast-tracked to fame|url=http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/15/opinion/opinion_30097933.php|accessdate=15 September 2015|work=[[The Nation (Thailand)|The Nation]]|date=15 March 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064640/http://www.nationmultimedia.com/2009/03/15/opinion/opinion_30097933.php|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} He attended [[Saint Gabriel's College (Thailand)|Saint Gabriel's College]] until he was 10, after which he studied in Australia and then at [[Charterhouse School]] in the United Kingdom. He read engineering, economics and management at [[St John's College, Oxford]], receiving a bachelor's and a master's degree. ==Political career== Akanat entered politics shortly after graduating from Oxford, becoming private secretary to his stepfather, Suthep, then Deputy Prime Minister. Akanat was subsequently elected a [[Democrat Party (Thailand)|Democrat]] Member of Parliament representing Bangkok in the [[2011 Thai general election|2011 general elections]]. At 25, he was the youngest MP elected that year. He and other members of his family received acclaim for his work during the [[2011 Thailand floods]], where he delivered food and other supplies to aid kitchens in Bangkok and Southern Thailand.{{cite news|title=All for one, one for all|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/print/383605/|accessdate=15 September 2015|work=[[Bangkok Post]]}} In June 2013 he resigned from Parliament, to help lead the [[People's Democratic Reform Committee]] dedicated to ousting the government of [[Yingluck Shinawatra]], and served as the organisation's spokesman. After the [[2014 Thai coup d'état|removal of the Yingluck government and coup d'état in 2014]], Akanat joined Suthep in being ordained as a monk for a year. In 2022 Akanat resigned from Democrat Party and became secretary-general of the [[United Thai Nation Party]] on 3 August 2022. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Promphan, Akanat}} [[Category:1986 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Alumni of St John's College, Oxford]] [[Category:Ministers of industry of Thailand|Akanat Promphan]] [[Category:Paetongtarn cabinet|Akanat Promphan]] {{Thailand-politician-stub}}
