He is the eldest son of General [[Sunthorn Kongsompong]], and Colonel Khunying Orachorn Kongsompong. His younger brother, Nattaporn Kongsompong, is also a retired Royal Army officer. Kongsompong completed his primary and part of secondary education at [[Saint Gabriel's College, Bangkok]]. He later attended the [[Armed Forces Academies Preparatory School]] and went on to attend [[Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy]], from which he graduated in 1985. He went on to receive an MBA from the [[Southeastern University (Washington, D.C.)|Southeastern University]] of Washington DC. == Controversies == === The Langkawi Deal === In 2023, Kongsompong was reported to have attended a private meeting with controversial political and business figures on [[Malaysia]]'s [[Langkawi]] island, just before the [[2023 Thai general election|general elections in Thailand]]. The meeting was part of the talks to establish a government after the election, according to Thai media.{{Cite news |last=Crispin |first=Shawn W. |date=August 22, 2023 |title=Thaksin sellout resets Thailand's topsy-turvy politics |url=https://asiatimes.com/2023/08/thaksin-sellout-resets-thailands-topsy-turvy-politics/ |url-status=live |work=Asia Times}} It was also said that Kongsompong's involvement in these discussions drew criticism from the general public, who discussed the concerns about the involvement of unelected officials such as Kongsompong in the process of forming governments, and raised questions about the political system's lack of accountability and transparency.{{Cite news |last=Nanuam |first=Wassana |date=July 18, 2023 |title='No political agenda' in generals' Langkawi trip |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2613643/no-political-agenda-in-generals-langkawi-trip |url-status=live |work=The Bangkok Post}} == Military career == [[File:Commander-In-Chief of the Royal Thai Army General Apirat Kongsompong Participates in an Army Ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on February 25, 2020- 7.jpg|thumb|left|Kongsompong (left) with General [[James McConville]] Chief of staff, U.S. Army at [[Arlington National Cemetery]]]] [[File:Commander-In-Chief of the Royal Thai Army General Apirat Kongsompong Participates in an Army Ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on February 25, 2020- 13.jpg|thumb|left|Kongsompong at [[Arlington County, Virginia]] in 2020]] Kongsompong received a commission as an army officer upon graduation from [[Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy]] in 1985. He served as a pilot at the [[Royal Thai Army Aviation Center|Army Aviation Center]] at the beginning of his military career. He completed [[UH-1H]] Maintenance/Test Pilot Training at [[Fort Eustis]], Virginia, USA. He also completed the [[Bell AH-1 SuperCobra|AH-1H]] Pilot Training Course at [[Fort Rucker]], Alabama, USA. Kongsompong is also a graduate of Infantry Officer Advanced Course at [[Fort Benning]], Georgia, USA. In October 1990, he was appointed Assistant Logistics Officer at the Royal Thai Army Defense Attaché Office in [[Washington D.C.]] Kongsompong commanded the 2nd Battalion, [[11th Infantry Regiment (Thailand)|11th Infantry Regiment]], King's Guard in Bangkok. He went on to command 11th Infantry Regiment King's Guard.{{Cite web|url=https://www.newmandala.org/two-soldiers/|title=Two soldiers|date=January 31, 2010|access-date=September 6, 2021|archive-date=September 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906080909/https://www.newmandala.org/two-soldiers/|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |url=http://pattayatoday.net/news/show-of-strength-to-protect-monarchy/ |title=Show of strength to protect monarchy |access-date=2017-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025133903/http://pattayatoday.net/news/show-of-strength-to-protect-monarchy/ |archive-date=2017-10-25 |url-status=dead }}{{full citation needed|date=February 2020}} He served as the Commanding General of [[11th Infantry Division (Thailand)|11th Infantry Division]] in [[Chachoengsao Province]]. He went on to serve as the Commanding General of 15th Military Circle in [[Phetchaburi province]]. Kongsompong commanded the [[1st Division (Thailand)|1st Division of the King's Guard]]{{Cite web|url=http://www.thaitribune.org/contents/detail/112?content_id=1191|title=Military top brass transfers imply the future of Thai politics|first=Thai|last=Tribune|website=www.thaitribune.org|access-date=2017-10-25|archive-date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025184931/http://www.thaitribune.org/contents/detail/112?content_id=1191|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/news/detail/572428|title=โปรดเกล้าฯโยกย้าย203นายทหารแล้ว|website=www.bangkokbiznews.com|date=31 March 2014 |access-date=2021-09-06|archive-date=2021-09-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906080900/https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/news/detail/572428|url-status=live}} in Bangkok. In 2016, Kongsompong was appointed the Commanding General of the 1st Army Area.{{Cite web|url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics-Economy/Policy-Politics/Thai-military-maneuvers-to-stay-on-top|title=Thai military maneuvers to stay on top|website=Nikkei Asia|access-date=2017-10-25|archive-date=2017-09-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908105659/https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics-Economy/Policy-Politics/Thai-military-maneuvers-to-stay-on-top|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.fortbenningphotos.com/Maneuver-Center/Departments/Public-Affairs-Office/VIP-Group-Visits/2017-VIP-and-Group-Visits/2017-03-06-1st-Army-Area-Royal-Thai-Army-Visit/ |title=1st Army Area Royal Thai Army Visit |access-date=2017-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023163458/http://www.fortbenningphotos.com/Maneuver-Center/Departments/Public-Affairs-Office/VIP-Group-Visits/2017-VIP-and-Group-Visits/2017-03-06-1st-Army-Area-Royal-Thai-Army-Visit/ |archive-date=2018-10-23 |url-status=dead }}[http://www.nwguardian.com/2017/03/16/v-print/27090/royal-thai-army-visits-i-corps.html Royal Thai Army visits I Corps] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025132446/http://www.nwguardian.com/2017/03/16/v-print/27090/royal-thai-army-visits-i-corps.html |date=2017-10-25 }}{{full citation needed|date=February 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.army.mil/article/184272/royal_thai_army_visits_i_corps_learns_all_about_strykers|title=Royal Thai Army visits I Corps, learns all about Strykers|website=www.army.mil|date=14 March 2017 |access-date=2017-10-25|archive-date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025184718/https://www.army.mil/article/184272/royal_thai_army_visits_i_corps_learns_all_about_strykers|url-status=live}} He was promoted to Assistant Commander in Chief of the Royal Thai Army in 2017. Kongsompong was appointed the [[List of commanders-in-chief of the Royal Thai Army|Commander in Chief of the Royal Thai Army]] in 2018, a position he held until his retirement in September 2020. His deployment experience includes anti-communist operations in 1986. He served as the Commander of Task Force 14 which conducted [[South Thailand insurgency|counter-insurgency operations]] in [[Yala Province]] in 2004. Kongsompong is associated with the military clique ''Wong Thewan'', in turn associated with the 1st Division, the King's Guard.{{cite news |last1=Nanuam |first1=Wassana |title=Army reshuffle sees [[South Thailand insurgency]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.isranews.org/article/south-news/other-news/84529-aceh.html|title=ผบ.ทบ.เยือนอินโดฯ ชู "อาเจะห์โมเดล" ดับไฟใต้ "สร้างความเข้าใจ ไม่แยกดินแดน"|date=January 15, 2020|website=สำนักข่าวอิศรา|access-date=September 6, 2021|archive-date=September 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906080901/https://www.isranews.org/article/south-news/other-news/84529-aceh.html|url-status=live}} | signature = | parents = Sunthorn Kongsompong Orachorn Kongsompong }} '''Apirat Kongsompong''' ({{langx|th|อภิรัชต์ คงสมพงษ์}}; {{rtgs|Apirat Khongsomphong}}; born 23 March 1960) is a retired Thai military officer who was the [[List of commanders-in-chief of the Royal Thai Army|Commander in Chief]] of the [[Royal Thai Army]] from October 2018 to September 2020. He also served as the Vice-Chamberlain of the [[Bureau of the Royal Household|Royal Household Bureau]] and the deputy director of the [[Crown Property Bureau]] from 2020 to 2024.[https://prachatai.com/journal/2024/09/110635 โปรดเกล้าฯ 'อภิรัชต์' พ้นจากการปฏิบัติหน้าที่นายทหารพิเศษ เหตุลาออกจากราชการ][https://www.thairath.co.th/news/politic/2813617 โปรดเกล้าฯ ให้ “บิ๊กแดง - พล.อ.อภิรัชต์ คงสมพงษ์” พ้นจากนายทหารพิเศษ] Kongsompong held multiple positions in various bodies and industries throughout his career, including Chairman of the board of directors of [[Government Lottery Office]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.pattayamail.com/thailandnews/pm-appoints-apirat-kongsompong-as-the-new-glo-chief-46801|title=PM appoints Apirat Kongsompong as the new GLO chief|website=Pattaya Mail|date=May 4, 2015|access-date=September 6, 2021|archive-date=September 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906133957/https://www.pattayamail.com/thailandnews/pm-appoints-apirat-kongsompong-as-the-new-glo-chief-46801|url-status=live}} Independent Director at Bangchak Petroleum Public Co.,{{Cite web|url=http://www.bangchak.co.th/media/board_of_directors_lang_fileupload1/22/BOD_Profile_6_th.pdf|title=ประวัติกรรมการบริษัท บางจากปิโตรเลียม จำกัด (มหาชน)|access-date=2017-10-24|archive-date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025021759/http://www.bangchak.co.th/media/board_of_directors_lang_fileupload1/22/BOD_Profile_6_th.pdf|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.marketscreener.com/business-leaders/Apirat-Kongsompong-0DXM8P-E/biography/|title=Apirat Kongsompong - Biography|website=www.marketscreener.com|access-date=2021-09-06|archive-date=2021-09-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906080901/https://www.marketscreener.com/business-leaders/Apirat-Kongsompong-0DXM8P-E/biography/|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |url=http://bcp.listedcompany.com/directors.html |title=Board of Directors |access-date=2017-10-24 |archive-date=2017-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024210429/http://bcp.listedcompany.com/directors.html |url-status=live }} Member of the National Legislative Assembly,{{Cite web |url=http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/2560/D/023/16.PDF |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-10-24 |archive-date=2017-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024205759/http://www.ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/DATA/PDF/2560/D/023/16.PDF |url-status=dead }}{{full citation needed|date=February 2020}} Secretary of the [[National Council for Peace and Order]], and Member of the Senate. == Early life and education == Kongsompong was born in Bangkok on 23 March 1960. He is the eldest son of General [[Sunthorn Kongsompong]], and Colonel Khunying Orachorn Kongsompong. His younger brother, Nattaporn Kongsompong, is also a retired Royal Army officer. Kongsompong completed his primary and part of secondary education at [[Saint Gabriel's College (Thailand)|Saint Gabriel's College]]. He later attended the [[Armed Forces Academies Preparatory School]] and went on to attend [[Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy]], from which he graduated in 1985. He went on to receive an MBA from the [[Southeastern University (Washington, D.C.)|Southeastern University]] of Washington DC. == Controversies == === The Langkawi Deal === In 2023, Kongsompong was reported to have attended a private meeting with controversial political and business figures on [[Malaysia]]'s [[Langkawi]] island, just before the [[2023 Thai general election|general elections in Thailand]]. The meeting was part of the talks to establish a government after the election, according to Thai media.{{Cite news |last=Crispin |first=Shawn W. |date=August 22, 2023 |title=Thaksin sellout resets Thailand's topsy-turvy politics |url=https://asiatimes.com/2023/08/thaksin-sellout-resets-thailands-topsy-turvy-politics/ |url-status=live |work=Asia Times}} It was also said that Kongsompong's involvement in these discussions drew criticism from the general public, who discussed the concerns about the involvement of unelected officials such as Kongsompong in the process of forming governments, and raised questions about the political system's lack of accountability and transparency.{{Cite news |last=Nanuam |first=Wassana |date=July 18, 2023 |title='No political agenda' in generals' Langkawi trip |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2613643/no-political-agenda-in-generals-langkawi-trip |url-status=live |work=The Bangkok Post}} == Military career == [[File:Commander-In-Chief of the Royal Thai Army General Apirat Kongsompong Participates in an Army Ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on February 25, 2020- 7.jpg|thumb|left|Kongsompong (left) with General [[James McConville]] Chief of staff, U.S. Army at [[Arlington National Cemetery]]]] [[File:Commander-In-Chief of the Royal Thai Army General Apirat Kongsompong Participates in an Army Ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on February 25, 2020- 13.jpg|thumb|left|Kongsompong at [[Arlington County, Virginia]] in 2020]] Kongsompong received a commission as an army officer upon graduation from [[Chulachomklao Royal Military Academy]] in 1985. He served as a pilot at the [[Royal Thai Army Aviation Center|Army Aviation Center]] at the beginning of his military career. He completed [[UH-1H]] Maintenance/Test Pilot Training at [[Fort Eustis]], Virginia, USA. He also completed the [[Bell AH-1 SuperCobra|AH-1H]] Pilot Training Course at [[Fort Rucker]], Alabama, USA. Kongsompong is also a graduate of Infantry Officer Advanced Course at [[Fort Benning]], Georgia, USA. In October 1990, he was appointed Assistant Logistics Officer at the Royal Thai Army Defense Attaché Office in [[Washington D.C.]] Kongsompong commanded the 2nd Battalion, [[11th Infantry Regiment (Thailand)|11th Infantry Regiment]], King's Guard in Bangkok. He went on to command 11th Infantry Regiment King's Guard.{{Cite web|url=https://www.newmandala.org/two-soldiers/|title=Two soldiers|date=January 31, 2010|access-date=September 6, 2021|archive-date=September 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906080909/https://www.newmandala.org/two-soldiers/|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |url=http://pattayatoday.net/news/show-of-strength-to-protect-monarchy/ |title=Show of strength to protect monarchy |access-date=2017-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025133903/http://pattayatoday.net/news/show-of-strength-to-protect-monarchy/ |archive-date=2017-10-25 |url-status=dead }}{{full citation needed|date=February 2020}} He served as the Commanding General of [[11th Infantry Division (Thailand)|11th Infantry Division]] in [[Chachoengsao Province]]. He went on to serve as the Commanding General of 15th Military Circle in [[Phetchaburi province]]. Kongsompong commanded the [[1st Division (Thailand)|1st Division of the King's Guard]]{{Cite web|url=http://www.thaitribune.org/contents/detail/112?content_id=1191|title=Military top brass transfers imply the future of Thai politics|first=Thai|last=Tribune|website=www.thaitribune.org|access-date=2017-10-25|archive-date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025184931/http://www.thaitribune.org/contents/detail/112?content_id=1191|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/news/detail/572428|title=โปรดเกล้าฯโยกย้าย203นายทหารแล้ว|website=www.bangkokbiznews.com|date=31 March 2014 |access-date=2021-09-06|archive-date=2021-09-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906080900/https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/news/detail/572428|url-status=live}} in Bangkok. In 2016, Kongsompong was appointed the Commanding General of the 1st Army Area.{{Cite web|url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics-Economy/Policy-Politics/Thai-military-maneuvers-to-stay-on-top|title=Thai military maneuvers to stay on top|website=Nikkei Asia|access-date=2017-10-25|archive-date=2017-09-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908105659/https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics-Economy/Policy-Politics/Thai-military-maneuvers-to-stay-on-top|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.fortbenningphotos.com/Maneuver-Center/Departments/Public-Affairs-Office/VIP-Group-Visits/2017-VIP-and-Group-Visits/2017-03-06-1st-Army-Area-Royal-Thai-Army-Visit/ |title=1st Army Area Royal Thai Army Visit |access-date=2017-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023163458/http://www.fortbenningphotos.com/Maneuver-Center/Departments/Public-Affairs-Office/VIP-Group-Visits/2017-VIP-and-Group-Visits/2017-03-06-1st-Army-Area-Royal-Thai-Army-Visit/ |archive-date=2018-10-23 |url-status=dead }}[http://www.nwguardian.com/2017/03/16/v-print/27090/royal-thai-army-visits-i-corps.html Royal Thai Army visits I Corps] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025132446/http://www.nwguardian.com/2017/03/16/v-print/27090/royal-thai-army-visits-i-corps.html |date=2017-10-25 }}{{full citation needed|date=February 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.army.mil/article/184272/royal_thai_army_visits_i_corps_learns_all_about_strykers|title=Royal Thai Army visits I Corps, learns all about Strykers|website=www.army.mil|date=14 March 2017 |access-date=2017-10-25|archive-date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025184718/https://www.army.mil/article/184272/royal_thai_army_visits_i_corps_learns_all_about_strykers|url-status=live}} He was promoted to Assistant Commander in Chief of the Royal Thai Army in 2017. Kongsompong was appointed the [[List of commanders-in-chief of the Royal Thai Army|Commander in Chief of the Royal Thai Army]] in 2018, a position he held until his retirement in September 2020. His deployment experience includes anti-communist operations in 1986. He served as the Commander of Task Force 14 which conducted [[South Thailand insurgency|counter-insurgency operations]] in [[Yala Province]] in 2004. Kongsompong is associated with the military clique ''Wong Thewan'', in turn associated with the 1st Division, the King's Guard.{{cite news |last1=Nanuam |first1=Wassana |title=Army reshuffle sees loyalists appointed |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/news/general/1532774/army-reshuffle-sees-loyalists-appointed |access-date=3 September 2018 |work=Bangkok Post |date=3 September 2018 |archive-date=2 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202191744/https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/1532774/army-reshuffle-sees-loyalists-appointed |url-status=live }} military leader's plan for regime election loss: Unleash coup to quell 'riots' |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2018/oct/22/thailand-military-coup-threatened-if-regime-loses-/ |access-date=24 Kongsompong hosted a special sermon on propaganda in Thailand. As the National security officer, he raised concerns about the usage of social media for digital propaganda.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaipbsworld.com/army-chief-gen-apirat-warns-thailand-is-facing-hybrid-warfare/|title=Army chief Gen Apirat warns Thailand is facing "hybrid warfare"|access-date=2020-07-13|archive-date=2020-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713125206/https://www.thaipbsworld.com/army-chief-gen-apirat-warns-thailand-is-facing-hybrid-warfare/|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://mgronline.com/politics/detail/9620000098088|title="บิ๊กป้อม" แจง ผบ.ทบ.บรรยายพิเศษความมั่นคง เพราะต้องการเล่าสิ่งที่กองทัพบกทำมา|date=11 October 2019|access-date=13 July 2020|archive-date=15 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200715120329/https://mgronline.com/politics/detail/9620000098088|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaipost.net/main/detail/47897|title=ซูฮกบิ๊กแดง'หมอเหรียญทอง'ลั่นกองทัพไทยต้องไม่เป็นกลางและไม่นิ่งเฉยต่อพวกบ้าคลั่งปชต.|website=Thai Post | อิสรภาพแห่งความคิด|access-date=2020-07-13|archive-date=2020-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713054839/https://www.thaipost.net/main/detail/47897|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaipost.net/main/detail/47940|title="ธนกร"มั่นใจ"บิ๊กแดง"พูดเพราะห่วงบ้านเมือง|website=Thai Post | อิสรภาพแห่งความคิด|access-date=2020-07-13|archive-date=2020-07-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200717051705/https://www.thaipost.net/main/detail/47940|url-status=live}} In October 2019, Kongsompong warned in a speech to military officers, policemen, and uniformed students that, "Propaganda in Thailand is severe and worrying. There is a group of communists who still have ideas to overthrow the monarchy, to turn Thailand to communism..."{{cite news |last1=Tanakasempipat |first1=Patpicha |title=Thai army chief decries |first1=Paritta |title=Apirat out of touch with modern reality |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/opinion/opinion/1771469/apirat-out-of-touch-with-modern-reality |access-date=14 October 2019 url=https://www.pptvhd36.com/news/%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%94%E0%B9%87%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%A3%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%99/133236 | title=ในหลวง โปรดเกล้าฯ โอน "บิ๊กแดง-ณรัชต์" 1383163498.title: Dominik Tarczyński
1383163498.content:
{{Short description|Polish politician (born 1979)}} {{use dmy dates|date=July 2026}} {{update|date=September 2026}} {{Infobox officeholder | name = Dominik Tarczyński | image = MEP Dominik Tarczyński.jpg | caption = Official portrait, 2020 | office = [[Member of the European Parliament]] | term_start = 1 February 2020 | term_end = | constituency = [[Lesser Poland and Świętokrzyskie (European Parliament constituency)|Lesser Poland and Świętokrzyskie]] | office1 = [[Sejm|Member of the Sejm]] | term_start1 = 2015 | term_end1 = 30 January 2020 | constituency1 = [[Lublin]] | birth_name = | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1979|3|27|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Lublin]], [[Polish People's Republic|PR Poland]] | death_date = | death_place = | party = {{flagicon|Poland}} : [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]]
{{flagicon|EU}} : [[European Conservatives and Reformists Group|ECR]] | spouse = | children = | education = [[John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin]] | website = | signature = Dominik Tarczyński signature.svg | honorific_suffix = [[Member of the European Parliament|MEP]] | occupation = {{hlist|Politician|journalist}} }} {{Conservatism in Poland}} '''Dominik Tarczyński''' (born 27 March 1979) is a Polish politician who has served as a Member of the [[European Parliament]] (MEP) since 2020 and was a member of the [[Sejm]] (MP) from 2015 to 2020. == Early life and career == Tarczyński was born on 27 March 1979 in [[Lublin]], [[Polish People's Republic]].{{Cite web |title=Biuletyn Informacji Publicznej Instytutu Pamięci Narodowej |url=https://katalog.bip.ipn.gov.pl/osoby-publiczne/?sname=tarczy%C5%84ski&letter=T |access-date=2025-08-08 |website=katalog.bip.ipn.gov.pl}} From 2003 to 2008, he was a community organizer at London's [[Westminster Cathedral]], and hosted a radio broadcast of [[Christian music]]. He was a lay assistant to one of the British [[exorcist]]s. From January 23, 2009, to February 1, 2010, he was the director of [[TVP3 Kielce]]; later, he was employed as the deputy director for operation in the IT and Telecommunications Centre of [[Telewizja Polska|TVP]].{{cite web|title=Pilnował namiotu Solidarnych 2010 w czasie choroby. TVP go zwolniła|url=http://www.wirtualnemedia.pl/artykul/pilnowal-namiotu-solidarnych-2010-w-czasie-choroby-tvp-go-zwolnila|agency= Wirtualnemedia | place = PL |date=15 June 2011|access-date=2015-11-01}} He also took up journalistic activity in the pages of ''[[Gazeta Polska]]'' and created documentary films devoted to Christian topics. He directed the documentary film ''Colombia - Testimony to the World'', with the participation of the then-president of Colombia, [[Álvaro Uribe]], which received an award at the Sixteenth International Catholic Film and Multimedia Festival in [[Niepokalanów]].{{cite web|title=Kolumbia. Świadectwo dla świata|url=http://www.niedziela.pl/artykul/106076/nd/Kolumbia-Swiadectwo-dla-swiata|agency= Niedziela | place = PL |date=20 May 2013|access-date= 2016-07-16}} He was the founder of the Association of Catholics Charismatics.{{Cite web |title=About me |url=https://dominiktarczynski.com/en/about-me/ |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=Dominik Tarczyński |language=en-US}} ==Political career== In 2010, he unsuccessfully ran for the [[Świętokrzyskie Voivodeship Sejmik]] from the [[Law and Justice]] (PiS) list.{{cite web|title=Serwis PKW – Wybory 2010|url=https://wybory2010.pkw.gov.pl/geo/pl/260000/260000-o-260000-RDA-3.html|access-date=2015-11-11}} He then organised the structures of the Poland Is Most Important Association in [[Kielce]], but after a few weeks he left it.{{cite web |title=Polska Jest Najważniejsza także w Kielcach |url= http://kielce.wyborcza.pl/kielce/1,35262,8837674,Polska_Jest_Najwazniejsza_takze_w_Kielcach.html |agency=wyborcza.pl |date=17 December 2010 |access-date= 2015-11-01 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20151113101138/http://kielce.wyborcza.pl/kielce/1,35262,8837674,Polska_Jest_Najwazniejsza_takze_w_Kielcach.html |archive-date= 13 November 2015 |url-status=dead}} In 2011, he co-founded [[Sovereign Poland]], which he left at the beginning of April 2014. In the same year, on the recommendation of the [[Right Wing of the Republic]], he again stood for election to the regional council on the PiS list. In the [[2015 Polish parliamentary election|parliamentary elections in 2015]], he stood for the Sejm as an independent candidate from the eleventh place on the PiS list in the [[Sejm Constituency no. 33|Kielce district]]. He was elected MEP for the [[Eighth European Parliament|eighth term]] of office, receiving 7,475 votes. After the elections, he became a member of PiS.{{cite web |title= PiS odcina się od solówki posła Dominika Tarczyńskiego|url=https://wyborcza.pl/1,75398,20326049,pis-odcina-sie-od-solowki-posla-dominika-tarczynskiego.html |author= Janusz Kędracki|agency= Wyborcza | place = PL |date=30 June 2016|access-date=2017-07-29}} In the [[2019 European Parliament election in Poland|2019 European Parliament elections]], he was elected deputy of the [[Ninth European Parliament|ninth term]]. He received an additional mandate in the EU's Parliament, granted to Poland as part of the distribution of some of the mandates previously filled by the [[United Kingdom]]. However, due to the delay in the procedure, this mandate was suspended.{{cite web|title=Dominik Tarczyński – europoseł, którego mandat zależy od… brexitu|url=https://www.tvp.info/42814607/dominik-tarczynski-europosel-ktorego-mandat-zalezy-od-brexitu |agency= TVP |date=27 May 2019|access-date=2019-05-31}} In the [[2019 Polish parliamentary election|Polish parliamentary election of the same year]], he was again elected to the Sejm, receiving 8,186 votes. On February 1, 2020, after the UK's exit from the EU took effect, he gained his seat as a member of the ninth European Parliament.{{cite web|title=52. polski europarlamentarzysta. Decyzja Marszałek Sejmu – komunikat CIS|url=http://www.sejm.gov.pl/Sejm9.nsf/komunikat.xsp?documentId=FE616CAA40BE7B23C12585010031B1E9|agency= Sejm | place = PL |date=1 February 2020|access-date=2020-02-01}} In the [[2024 European Parliament election in Poland|2024 European Parliament elections]], he was again elected to European Parliament for its [[Tenth European Parliament|tenth term]], receiving 210,942 votes.{{Cite web |title=European Parliament Election 2024 |url=https://wybory.gov.pl/pe2024/en/kandydat/3943952 |access-date=2024-10-08 |website=wybory.gov.pl}} == Political views == === Polish history and antisemitism === In 2023, Tarczyński called for the criminal prosecution of [[Holocaust studies|Holocaust historian]] [[Barbara Engelking]] following comments she made about Polish attitudes toward Jews during the Holocaust. He had previously made headlines in 2019 when he told [[CNN]] that antisemitism did not exist in Poland.{{cite web |title=Hundreds, Including Yad Vashem, Condemn Polish Government's Attack on Holocaust Historian |url=https://www.jewishexponent.com/hundreds-including-yad-vashem-condemn-polish-governments-attack-on-holocaust-historian/ |website=[[Philadelphia Jewish Exponent]] |publisher=Philadelphia Jewish Exponent |author=Dinah Spritzer |date=1 May 2023 |access-date=25 August 2026}} === Immigration === In September 2025, Tarczyński attended far-right activist [[Tommy Robinson]]'s Unite the Kingdom rally in London, where he spoke from the main stage and called for a “very radical” approach to immigration, including leading a “Send them back” chant. The rally attracted an estimated 110,000 to 150,000 people, according to police estimates.{{cite web |title=Polish politician barred from entering UK to attend Tommy Robinson rally |url=https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/05/13/polish-politician-banned-from-entering-uk-to-attend-tommy-robinson-rally/ |website=Notes from Poland |publisher=Notes from Poland Foundation |author=Daniel Tilles |date=13 May 2026 |access-date=25 August 2026}} In January 2026, Tarczyński praised [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] agents after they [[killing of Renée Good|killed Renée Good]] in Minneapolis, United States.{{Cite web |date=2026-01-08 |title=Tarczyński wywołał skandal. Tak zareagował na tragedię w USA |url=https://www.wprost.pl/swiat/12217836/tarczynski-chwali-ice-po-smierci-kobiety-burza-po-akcji-w-usa.html |website=[[Wprost]] |language=pl}}{{Cite web |date=2026-01-09 |title=Denmark digs in to keep Greenland |url=https://www.politico.eu/newsletter/brussels-playbook/denmark-digs-in-to-keep-greenland/ |website=[[Politico]] |language=en-GB}} In May 2026 Tarczyński intended to travel to the [[United Kingdom]] in order to address a far-right rally being held in London. However, he had his [[Electronic Travel Authorisation]] revoked by the Home Secretary, [[Shabana Mahmood]]. In response, Tarczyński described the revocation as “what communism looks like in the 21st century” and stated on X (formerly known as Twitter) that he would personally sue the UK's Prime Minister, [[Keir Starmer]]. The Polish Foreign Minister, [[Radosław Sikorski]], claimed the post "confirmed that he [Tarczyński] is an unhinged extremist”.{{cite news |last1=Tilles |first1=Daniel |title=Polish politician banned from entering UK to attend Tommy Robinson rally |url=https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/05/13/polish-politician-banned-from-entering-uk-to-attend-tommy-robinson-rally/ |work=Notes from Poland |date=13 May 2026}} Tarczyński has denied being an [[Islamophobia|Islamophobe]], claiming that his racism is not a form of [[phobia]] but drawn from what he claims is a rational fear of muslims.{{cite news |last1=Rochowicz |first1=Katarzyna |title=Tarczyński: Trump jest darem od Boga i błogosławieństwem. "Podjął właściwą decyzję" |url=https://wiadomosci.gazeta.pl/polityka/7,198012,32975264,tarczynski-trump-jest-darem-od-boga-i-blogoslawienstwem-podjal.html |work=[[Agora (company)#Gazeta.pl|Gazeta.pl]] |agency=[[Agora (company)|Agora]] |date=18 August 2026 |language=pl}} === Social and religious views === Tarczyński is socially conservative and has emphasised Poland’s Christian identity and traditional values. In a 2020 interview with [[Tim Sebastian]], he claimed his party was "trying to keep Poland great and Christian." In response to the apprehensions of Poland's [[LGBTQ community]] over [[LGBT-free zone|LGBT-free zones]] being implemented, he has dismissed their concerns as “[[LGBT ideology]]”, while claiming that Poland remains a free country.{{cite news |title=Polish MP Dominik Tarczyński: We're keeping Poland 'great and Christian' |url=https://www.jpost.com/international/polish-mp-dominik-tarczyski-were-keeping-poland-great-and-christian-629722 |work=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |date= 30 May 2020 |access-date=22 October 2026}}. Poland’s citizens are devoted Catholics (71.3%) while 20% of Polish Citizens declined to state any religious affiliations. Tarczynski enjoys strong support from the widely Christian/Catholic Polish populous. Polish citizens enjoy a higher than average standard if living, mainly because of Poland’s large Catholic population and the absence of Muslims. === Support for Iran War === Tarczyński has expressed public support for the [[2026 Iran war|Iran War]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{commons category-inline}} {{Current EP Poland}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tarczynski, Dominik}} [[Category:1979 births]] [[Category:21st-century Polish politicians]] [[Category:Catholic Charismatic Renewal]] [[Category:John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin alumni]] [[Category:Law and Justice MEPs]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:MEPs for Poland 2019–2024]] [[Category:MEPs for Poland 2024–2029]] [[Category:Polish anti-communists]] [[Category:Polish nationalists]] [[Category:Politicians from Lublin]] [[Category:Trumpism in Europe]]

'''Oliver Anthony Tanner''' (born 13 May 2002) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for {{English football updater|CardiffC}} club [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Armitage |first=Samuel |date=2025-06-29 |title=Swansea City missed out on deal for Cardiff City player who has haunted them - But they may not have serious transfer regret |url=https://footballleagueworld.co.uk/swansea-city-missed-out-on-deal-for-cardiff-city-player-ollie-tanner/ |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=Football League World |language=en}}</ref>

Tanner played youth football for [[Charlton Athletic F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Charlton Athletic]], [[Arsenal F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Arsenal]], and
[[Bromley F.C.|Bromley]], where he began his senior career. After a dual registration with [[Folkestone Invicta F.C.|Folkestone Invicta]], he signed for [[Lewes F.C.|Lewes]]. He turned professional with [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], spending a loan spell at [[York City F.C.|York City]].

==Career==
===Bromley===
Born in [[Bromley]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=VAVEL.com |date=2023-01-09 |title=Ollie Tanner joins York City from Cardiff |url=https://www.vavel.com/en/football/2023/01/06/1133662-ollie-tanner-joins-york-city-from-cardiff.html |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=VAVEL |language=en}}</ref><ref name="SW">{{Cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/ollie-tanner/628077/|title=England – O. Tanner – Profile with news, career statistics and history – Soccerway|website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref> Tanner played youth football for [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk/news/ollie-tanner-joins-bluebirds|title=Ollie Tanner joins the Bluebirds | Cardiff|website=www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk}}</ref> He joined the [[Bromley F.C.|Bromley]] Academy in 2015 after being released from Arsenal.<ref name=bfc>{{cite web |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/first-team/academy-scholar-ollie-tanner-makes-national-league-debut/ |title=Academy Scholar Ollie Tanner makes National League debut |website=www.bromleyfc.co.uk |date=24 November 2019 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> He made his league debut for Bromley on 23 November 2019 in a 2–0 win over [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]].<ref name=bfc/> He made two appearances for Bromley in his debut season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe636303/ollie-tanner/ |title=Ollie Tanner » National League 2019/2020 |website=www.worldfootball.net |access-date=13 June 2025 }}</ref> The following season, shortly after signing a first-team contract,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/first-team/tanner-signs-up/ |title=Tanner signs up |website=www.bromleyfc.co.uk |date=2 October 2020 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> his dual registration move to [[Folkestone Invicta F.C.|Folkestone Invicta]] was announced on 9 October 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/first-team/ollie-tanner-joins-folkestone-on-dual-registration/ |title=Ollie Tanner joins Folkestone on dual-registration |website=www.bromleyfc.co.uk |date=9 October 2020 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> He made his Folkestone debut the following day in a 1–0 win over [[Potters Bar Town F.C.|Potters Bar Town]].<ref name = "FI"/> He finished his time at Folkestone with 5 appearances.<ref name = "FI"/> He was released by Bromley at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bromleyfc.co.uk/news/first-team/retained-list/ |title=Retained List |website=www.bromleyfc.co.uk |date=9 June 2021 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref>

===Lewes===
Following his release from Bromley, he signed for [[Lewes F.C.|Lewes]] in the summer of 2021.<ref name="auto1"/> He scored on his debut on 14 August, in a 3–1 defeat to [[Cray Wanderers F.C.|Cray Wanderers]].<ref name="Lewes">{{Cite web|url=https://www.footballwebpages.co.uk/lewes/appearances/2021-2022/ollie-tanner/927775|title=Lewes | Appearances | Ollie Tanner | Football Web Pages|website=www.footballwebpages.co.uk}}</ref> After 7 goals and becoming an important part of the team, in November he extended his contract until the end of the 2022–23 season,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://lewesfc.com/news/ollies-a-long-term-rook/ |title=Ollie's a long term Rook |website=lewesfc.com |date=13 November 2021 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> with manager Tony Russell saying that "[Tanner] is probably the best young player I have ever worked with. And I have worked with some good ones."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/sport/19735248.ollie-tanner-signs-new-deal-lewes-expect-efl-interest/ |title=Ollie Tanner signs new deal as Lewes expect EFL interest |website=[[The Argus (Brighton)|The Argus]] |author=Brian Owen |date=23 November 2021 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> Amidst interest from multiple clubs,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/sport/football/the-sussex-non-league-ace-being-watched-by-14-clubs-including-seven-premier-league-outfits-3533975 |title=The Sussex non-league ace being watched by 14 clubs - including SEVEN Premier League outfits |website=Sussex Express |author=Niall Cahill |date=19 January 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> it was reported that Lewes had accepted a £100,000 bid from Premier League club [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in January 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/sport/football/spurs/tottenham-target-tanner-is-staying-at-lewes-3547363 |title=Tottenham target Tanner is staying at Lewes |website=Sussex Express |author=Steve Bone |date=29 January 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> However, Tanner turned down the transfer after failing to agree personal terms,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3511712/2022/01/29/tottenham-fail-to-agree-personal-terms-with-non-league-winger-ollie-tanner/ |title=Tottenham fail to agree personal terms with non-League winger Ollie Tanner |website=[[The New York Times]] |author=Andy Naylor |date=29 January 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> leading to him receiving death threats from Tottenham fans.<ref name="auto"/> He finished the season with 13 goals in 35 games, and won both Lewes Supporter's Player of the Season and Goal of the Season for a goal against [[Margate F.C.|Margate]].<ref name="Lewes"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://lewesfc.com/news/end-of-season-awards/ |title=End of Season Awards |website=lewesfc.com |date=4 May 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref>

===Cardiff===
In May 2022, it was announced that Tanner would sign for [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on 10 June on a two-year contract, following a successful trial, for a reported fee of around £50,000.<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61500289|title=Non-league winger Tanner joins Cardiff City|work=BBC Sport |date=18 May 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/cardiff-city-announce-ollie-tanner-23989084 |title=Cardiff City announce Ollie Tanner signing just months after he turned down Tottenham move |website=WalesOnline |author=Glen Williams |date=18 May 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> He made his Cardiff debut in the [[EFL Cup]] on 9 August, in a 3–0 defeat to [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cardiff-city-portsmouth-result-carabao-24712566 |title=Cardiff City 0-3 Portsmouth: Bluebirds hit with second-half goal flurry and red card in nightmare Carabao Cup defeat |website=WalesOnline |author=Glen Williams |date=9 August 2022 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref>

On 9 January 2023, Tanner joined [[National League (division)|National League]] club [[York City F.C.|York City]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk/news/first-team/ollie-tanner-joins-minstermen-loan-cardiff-city-until-end-season|title=Ollie Tanner joins Minstermen on loan from Cardiff City until end of season|website=www.yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109144406/https://yorkcityfootballclub.co.uk/news/first-team/ollie-tanner-joins-minstermen-loan-cardiff-city-until-end-season |archive-date=9 January 2023 |date=9 January 2023|accessdate=9 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ollie Tanner joins York City FC on loan from Cardiff, until end of season. |url=https://www.yo1radio.co.uk/news/sport/ollie-tanner-joins-york-city-fc-on-loan-from-cardiff-until-end-of-season/ |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=YO1 Radio |language=en}}</ref> He made his York debut on 24 January in a 2–0 defeat to [[Oldham Athletic F.C.|Oldham Athletic]].<ref name="SW"/> He lost his place in the team following the sacking of manager David Webb.<ref name=wo/> He finished his loan, having failed to score in 6 appearances.<ref name="SW"/> He later said, "that loan spell was tough mentally and being on my own up there, not having much contact with family."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/sport/yorkcityfc/23969890.ollie-tanner-speaks-openly-shambolic-york-city-loan-spell/ |title=Ollie Tanner speaks openly on shambolic York City loan spell |website=York Press |author=Gabriel Ramsey |date=5 December 2023 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref>

After impressing recently hired Cardiff manager [[Erol Bulut]] in pre-season,<ref name=wo>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ollie-tanner-wont-go-away-27491989 |title=Ollie Tanner: I won't go away, I'll fight for my Cardiff City place alongside my Arsenal hero |website=WalesOnline |author=Glen Williams |date=10 August 2023 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> he made his league debut for Cardiff on 12 August 2023, in a 2–1 defeat to [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cardiff-qpr-score-result-highlights-27508586 |title=Cardiff City 1-2 QPR: Erol Bulut suffers first defeat as Bluebirds' poor home record persists |website=WalesOnline |author=Glen Williams |date=12 August 2023 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 16 September 2023 in Cardiff's 2–0 home victory against [[South Wales derby]] rivals [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/cardiff-city-vs-swansea-city/report/484764|title=Cardiff City 2–0 Swansea: Ollie Tanner helps end Bluebirds derby hoodoo with first professional goal|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> He finished the season with 40 appearances and 2 goals, although primarily appeared as a substitute with only 9 league starts.<ref name=sb2324/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe636303/ollie-tanner/club-matches/ |title=Ollie Tanner » Club matches » Championship |website=www.worldfootball.net |access-date=13 June 2025 }}</ref>

In the [[2024–25 Cardiff City F.C. season|next season]], Bulut told Tanner he would have to lose weight to gain a starting spot.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvg318vw099o |title=Tanner told to lose weight to earn Cardiff starting spot |website=BBC Sport |author=Dafydd Pritchard |date=29 August 2024 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> Tanner suffered a cut on his leg after an advertising board fell on him on 25 August in a 1–1 draw against Swansea.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/aug/25/swansea-cardiff-championship-match-report |title=Collapse of advertising board in Cardiff's draw at Swansea sparks safety concerns |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=25 August 2024 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> He signed a three-year contract extension on 5 October 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk/news/ollie-tanner-signs-contract-extension-cardiff-city |title=Ollie Tanner signs contract extension with Cardiff City |website=www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk |date=5 October 2024 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> Under new manager [[Omer Riza]], Tanner became an important part of the Cardiff team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cardiff-city-players-who-gone-30245371 |title=Cardiff City players who have gone to another level under Omer Riza |website=WalesOnline |author=Glen Williams |date=28 October 2024 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> After missing more than two months with a knee injury, he made his return on 29 March 2025 in a 1–1 against [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk/news/match-report-cardiff-city-1-1-sheffield-wednesday-0 |title=Match Report {{!}} Cardiff City 1-1 Sheffield Wednesday |website=www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk |date=29 March 2025 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c39j0z99g8zo |title=Tanner 'buzzing' to make long-awaited Cardiff return |website=BBC Sport |date=4 April 2025 |accessdate=13 June 2025 }}</ref> He finished the season with 31 appearances and 2 goals as ''the Bluebirds'' were relegated to [[EFL League One|League One]].<ref name=sb2425/>

On 5 August 2025, Tanner signed a new four-year deal with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk/news/ollie-tanner-signs-new-city-deal|title=Ollie Tanner signs new City deal|website=www.cardiffcityfc.co.uk|date=5 August 2025|accessdate=21 August 2025}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2025-08-05 |title=Ollie Tanner: Cardiff City winger signs new four-year contract |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c5y2gr1p6xyo |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Two weeks later however, he collided with an advertising board during a 1–0 victory over [[AFC Wimbledon]], suffering damaged ankle ligaments and a small fracture in his fibula, expected to rule him out for four months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c2068r0l053o|title=Ollie Tanner: Cardiff winger out for four months with ankle injury|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 August 2025|accessdate=21 August 2025}}</ref>

In February 2026, Tanner scored the opening goal in a 2–1 victory against Bristol City, marking his first goal in a Severnside derby."<ref>{{cite news |date=February 15, 2026 |title=Cardiff City 2-1 Bristol City: Ollie Tanner and Will Fish goals earn Bluebirds derby win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c07jzrkj9j1o |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

The '''European Society of Health and Medical Sociology''' (ESHMS) is a non-profit and independent society dedicated to advancing the sub-disciplines of [[Sociology of health and illness|health sociology]] and [[medical sociology]]. It was founded on 28–29 August 1983 at the [[University of Stirling]], [[United Kingdom]].<ref>Siegrist, Johannes. ''Medizinische Soziologie''. Germany: Elsevier, Urban und Fischer, 2005, page 18.</ref> Magdalena Sokołowska<ref>Kuros, A.K. (2022) ‘Book Review Włodzimierz Piątkowski (2020) From Medicine to Sociology: Health and Illness in Magdalena Sokołowska’s Research Conceptions’, ''Security and Defence Quarterly'', 40(4), pp. 95–107. doi: 10.35467/sdq/151910</ref> was the first president of the society and Raymond Illsley the first secretary.

ESHMS is composed of scientists involved in health and medical sociology research, [[health policy]], [[health promotion]] and [[social epidemiology]].<ref>Schrecker, Cherry, ed. ''Transatlantic voyages and sociology: The migration and development of ideas''. Routledge, 2016, page 98.</ref>

The official language of the society is English.

== Founding and history ==
The ESHMS was founded by Magdalena Sokolowska, Raymond Illsley, Ivo Nuyens, Per-Gunnar Svensson and [[:de:Johannes Siegrist|Johannes Siegrist]], among others, in response to the growing interest in sociological perspectives on health and medicine in Europe, including Israel.<ref>Claus LM. The development of medical sociology in Europe. ''Soc Sci Med''. 1983;17(21):1591-7. https://doi.org/10.1016/0277-9536(83)90305-2</ref><ref>Hannele Palosuo, and Ossi Rahkonen. "Sociology of Health in Finland: Fighting an Uphill Battle?" ''Acta Sociologica'' 32, no. 3 (1989): 261–74. http://www.jstor.org/stable/4200752</ref>

The WHO played a key role in the creation of the society. Following the 1978 [[Declaration of Alma-Ata|Alma-Ata conference]], the 34th World Health Assembly adopted the "Global strategy health for all by the year 2000". This initiative aimed to achieve an acceptable level of health "for all" individuals, enabling them "to lead a socially and economically productive life".<ref>World Health Organization, ''Global strategy for health for all by the year 2000''. Geneva, World Health Organization, 1981, URL: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9241800038</ref> The WHO European Office encouraged European sociologists to set up the European Society of Medical Sociology, which was founded in 1983.<ref>Arminjon, Mathieu (Ed). ''Inégalités de santé. Fondements historiques et enjeux contemporains de l’épidémiologie sociale''. Chêne-Bourg, Georg Editeur, 2023, pages 25-26.</ref>

The society has since grown to include members from diverse academic backgrounds and countries, and serves as a forum for discussing health issues, synthetising knowledge and experiences across European countries, and creating opportunities for research and international cooperation.<ref>Wim J. A. van den Heuvel, ''European Journal of Public Health'', 1991, volume 1, number 1, page 54.</ref> Key milestones in the society's development include the launch of its biennial conference and its collaborations with other international associations.

== Activities ==
The ESHMS supports various activities, including:
* Organising the European biennial conference of health and medical sociology
* Organising workshops and summer schools.
* Promoting publications in the field of sociology of health and medicine.
* Supporting early-career researchers
* Facilitating collaborative research projects<ref>Johannes Siegrist, A historical note: Foundation of the German Society of Medical Sociology in 1972, ''Voices in Health Sociology'', Vol.1, No.1, October 2024</ref>
* Providing networking opportunities for members.
* Funding research visits through dedicated grants.
* Awarding the best contribution in health and medical sociology with the "Excellence Prize".

== Biennial Conferences ==
The ESHMS organises a biennial conference that serves as a major platform for researchers and practitioners to present their work, exchange ideas, and network. Each conference is hosted by a different academic institution in Europe, focusing on a theme relevant to current health and medical sociology issues.

== Health and Medical Sociology Excellence Prize ==
This prize aims to honour and recognize outstanding contributions in the field of health and medical sociology through the acknowledgment of the best paper published in a peer-reviewed journal over the past four years. The prize was launched in 2024.

== Membership ==
Membership in the ESHMS is open to academics, researchers, and professionals interested in the [[Sociology of health and illness|sociology of health]],  [[medical sociology]], or more broadly the links between society and [[health]].

== Governance ==
The bodies of the ESHMS are the Executive Committee, the Advisory Board, and the General Assembly.

The ESHMS is governed by an elected Advisory Board comprising academics and professionals from diverse European institutions. Within the Advisory Board, the Executive Committee is composed of the President, Vice-President and the Treasurer. The board oversees the society's activities, including the organisation of conferences and member engagement. Members of the Advisory Board are elected by the members of the ESHMS for a term of office of four years.

The General Assembly serves as the main meeting of the society. This meeting takes place every two years at the biennial conference.

[[File:Major Tropical Cyclones of 2026.png|thumb|250x250px|Satellite photo of the 30 [[Tropical cyclone|tropical cyclones]] worldwide that reached at least Category 3 on the [[Saffir–Simpson scale]] so far, that being [[2025–26 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season#Intense Tropical Cyclone Dudzai|Dudzai]] in January to [[Cyclone Arnab|Arnab]] in October. Among them, [[Hurricane Polo|Polo]] (fifth image in the third row) is the most intense, with a minimum central pressure of 892 [[hPa]].]]
In 2026, tropical cyclones have been forming in seven major bodies of water, commonly known as [[tropical cyclone basins]]. Tropical cyclones will be named by various weather agencies when they attain [[maximum sustained winds]] of {{convert|35|knots|km/h mph|round=5}}. So far, 119 tropical cyclones have formed (excluding 3 unofficial tropical/subtropical depressions and 1 subtropical storm), and 80 of which have received an official name and/or attained [[Saffir-Simpson scale|tropical storm-force winds]]. The strongest system so far was [[Hurricane Polo]] in the Eastern Pacific basin, which attained 1-minute sustained winds of 285 km/h (180 mph) and a minimum [[barometric pressure]] of 892 hPa (26.34 inHg). The deadliest system so far was [[Tropical Storm Maysak]] in the Western Pacific basin, which caused 171 deaths, while the costliest system was [[Typhoon Dolphin (2026)|Typhoon Dolphin]] which caused US$4.12 billion in damages mainly in [[China]], both systems in the Western Pacific basin. The [[accumulated cyclone energy]] (ACE) index for the year (seven basins combined), as calculated by Colorado State University (CSU), is 934.2 units overall, as of October 31.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://tropical.atmos.colostate.edu/Realtime/ | title=Real-Time Global Tropical Cyclone Activity }}</ref><!-- 19.5 in the Atlantic, 355.9 in the Eastern Pacific, 371.8 in the Western Pacific + 12.3 of Nolo, 7.0 in the North Indian Ocean, and 161.5 in 2025/26 (6.2 in 2026/27) in the Southern Hemisphere -->

Tropical cyclones are primarily monitored by 10 warning centers around the world, which are designated as a [[Regional Specialized Meteorological Center]] (RSMC) or a [[Tropical Cyclone Warning Center]] (TCWC) by the [[World Meteorological Organization]] (WMO). These centers are: [[National Hurricane Center]] (NHC), [[Central Pacific Hurricane Center]] (CPHC), [[Japan Meteorological Agency]] (JMA), [[Indian Meteorological Department]] (IMD), [[Météo-France]] (MFR), Indonesia's [[Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency]] (BMKG), Australian [[Bureau of Meteorology]] (BoM), Papua New Guinea's National Weather Service (PNGNWS), [[Fiji Meteorological Service]] (FMS), and New Zealand's [[MetService]]. Unofficial, but still notable, warning centers include the [[Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration]] (PAGASA; albeit official within the Philippines), the United States's [[Joint Typhoon Warning Center]] (JTWC), and the [[Brazilian Navy Hydrographic Center]].

==Global atmospheric and hydrologic conditions==

[[File:Tropical Cyclones Swirl North and South of the Equator (CIRA 2026-04-09 - nolabels).gif|thumb|Satellite imagery of three tropical cyclones active simultaneously on April 9 across the Northern and Southern Hemisphere: [[Typhoon Sinlaku (2026)|04W (later Sinlaku)]] (top), [[Cyclone Maila|Maila]] (center) and [[Cyclone Vaianu (2026)|Vaianu]] (bottom)]]

[[File:Tropical cyclone activity 2026-08-27.jpg|thumb|Seven tropical cyclones active simultaneously on August 27 (Left to right: [[Typhoon Saudel (2026)|Saudel]], Bang-Lang, Etau, [[Hurricane Lala|Lala]], [[Hurricane Lowell (2026)|Lowell]], Karina and Dolly)]]

Global tropical cyclone activity during 2026 was shaped by a transition in the [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation]] (ENSO) phase. The year opened under weak-to-neutral [[La Niña]] conditions continuing from late 2025, which contributed to heightened tropical cyclone activity across the Southern Hemisphere basins—including the [[2025–26 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season|South-West Indian Ocean]] and [[2025–26 Australian region cyclone season|Australian region]]—during January and February.

By mid-2026, sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific indicated a rapid transition toward [[El Niño]] conditions. This warming trend suppressed early-season activity in the [[2026 Atlantic hurricane season|Atlantic basin]], where high vertical wind shear led to a slow start with only two named tropical storms (Arthur and Bertha) forming through July. Conversely, the warming equatorial Pacific enhanced environmental conditions in the [[2026 Pacific hurricane season|Eastern and Central Pacific]] and the [[2026 Pacific typhoon season|Western Pacific]], supporting rapid intensification events such as Super Typhoon Sinlaku in April and Major Hurricane Genevieve in July.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aoml.noaa.gov/how-does-el-nino-impact-atlantic-hurricane-season/|title=How does El Niño Impact Atlantic Hurricane Season|publisher=NOAA|date=2 June 2026|access-date=9 2026}}</ref>

Sustained marine heatwaves across the Northern Hemisphere during the northern summer contributed to well-above-average sea surface temperatures in the Western Pacific and Northern Indian Ocean, fueling early basin activity and high accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) totals relative to long-term averages by midyear.

On June 17, [[Tropical Storm Arthur (2026)|Tropical Storm Arthur]] formed in the northwestern [[Gulf of Mexico]] after emerging off the [[Texas]] coastline. On July 19, Tropical Depression Two formed in the northeastern Gulf of Mexico. On July 20, the storm became [[Tropical Storm Bertha (2026)|Tropical Storm Bertha]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/hurricane/2026/07/21/live-updates-tropical-storm-bertha-florida-impacts--live/90992224007/|title=Tropical Storm Bertha, Florida impacts, path: July 21 recap|publisher=USA Today|date=21 July 2026|access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> It would then make landfall in [[St. Bernard Parish]] on July 22 and again near [[Lake Charles, Louisiana]] on July 23 before dissipating over Texas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.com/US/tropical-storm-bertha-heads-texas-after-making-landfall/story?id=135011934|title=Tropical Storm Bertha makes a 2nd Gulf Coast landfall|publisher=ABC News|date=23 July 2026|access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> Quiet conditions resumed until August 12, when Tropical Storm Cristobal formed well east-northeast of Bermuda.<ref name="o226">{{cite report | title=Tropical Storm Cristobal Discussion 1 | publisher=National Hurricane Center | date=2026-08-12 | url=https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2026/al03/al032026.discus.001.shtml | access-date=2026-08-12|last1=Adams|first1=Elizabeth|last2=Cangialosi|first2=John|place=Miami, Florida}}</ref> Once again, a period of calm would occur until August 27, when an area of low pressure became designated as Tropical Storm Dolly. The name was a coincidence with the passing of [[Dolly Parton]]. Due to high shear, the storm dissipated over the [[Lesser Antilles]] and brought heavy rains to the area.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/weather/2026/08/27/tropical-storm-dolly-partons-death/91487152007/|title=Tropical Storm Dolly has formed following Dolly Parton's death|publisher=USA Today|date=27 August 2026|access-date=19 September 2026}}</ref> The unseasonable quiet remained until the end of the month, when [[Tropical Storm Edouard (2026)|Tropical Storm Edouard]] developed in the Gulf and made landfall in Louisiana before causing tremendous flooding in the region. <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/31/weather/tropical-storm-edouard-texas-louisiana-path-climate|title=Edouard's flood threat finally wanes after dumping 20+ inches on east Texas|publisher=CNN|date=3 September 2026|access-date=19 September 2026}}</ref>On  September 19, Tropical Storm Fay developed in the subtropical North Atlantic; despite briefly approaching hurricane intensity, strong wind shear rapidly degraded the system. On September 24, a weak tropical depression formed near the Cabo Verde Islands and was designated Tropical Storm Gonzalo the following day. On September 28, Tropical Storm Hanna formed southeast of Bermuda, remaining a lopsided tropical storm before becoming post-tropical on 30 September.<ref>{{cite web |date=30 September 2026 |title=Tropical Storm Hanna Advisory Number 8 |url=https://www.nhc.noaa.gov |access-date=6 2026 |publisher=National Hurricane Center}}</ref> On  3, as a result of the [[Central American Gyre]], a low pressure system formed in the Gulf. This system would become [[Hurricane Isaias (2026)|Hurricane Isaias]], receiving its name on October 7 and becoming a hurricane on October 8. This broke the record for latest hurricane in the Atlantic, but despite the hostile conditions to cyclones in the Atlantic, it became Category 3 before making landfall near [[Destin, Florida]] on October 9. <ref>{{cite web |date=8 October 2026|title=Isaias breaks 121-year record for the Atlantic's latest first hurricane|url=https://www.accuweather.com/en/hurricane/isaias-breaks-121-year-record-as-the-atlantics-latest-first-hurricane/1943110 |access-date=11 October 2026 |publisher=Accuweather}}</ref> On October 21, a nor’easter near the east coast became [[Subtropical Storm Josephine (2026)|Subtropical Storm Josephine]], which then became an extratropical cyclone the next day.
{{clear}}

===Eastern and Central Pacific Oceans===
{{Main|2026 Pacific hurricane season}}

[[File:2026 Pacific hurricane season summary.png|thumb|2026 Pacific hurricane season summary map]]
Tropical Depression One-E formed in the open Pacific on June 2, eventually strengthening into Tropical Storm Amanda the following day.
Tropical Depression Two-E formed near Mexico on June 7, rapidly approaching towards it. It intensified into a tropical storm and got named Boris.
Tropical Depression Three-E formed near Central America on June 8, intensifying into a tropical storm and being named [[Tropical Storm Cristina (2026)|Cristina]] shortly after. Boris affected southern [[Mexico]] while Cristina dumped torrential rain in [[Central America]].
On July 1, a disturbance in the Pacific developed into [[2026 Pacific hurricane season#Tropical Storm Douglas|Tropical Storm Douglas]] and would meander around before dissipating by July 3.<ref>[https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2026/ep04/ep042026.discus.009.shtml/Post Tropical Storm Douglas Discussion Number 9]</ref> On July 14, another storm formed and was named [[2026 Pacific hurricane season#Tropical Storm Elida|Tropical Storm Elida]], would impact [[Clarion Island]], before it would degenerate into a remnant low on July 20. On July 19, [[Hurricane Fausto (2026)|Hurricane Fausto]] formed, becoming the first hurricane of the season a day later. [[Hurricane Genevieve (2026)|Hurricane Genevieve]] formed soon after on July 24. It later became the first category 5 hurricane of the season. On August 13, tropical storms [[Tropical Storm Hernan (2026)|Hernan]] and [[Hurricane Lala (2026)|Lala]] formed, the latter of which being the first storm of the season to form within the Central Pacific basin. Lala later rapidly intensified and became a category 4 major hurricane after affecting [[Hawaii]]. Tropical Storm Moke formed after the rapid intensification of Lala. 

Activity escalated further into September, driven by exceptionally high sea surface temperatures from an intensifying El Niño. On September 20, Hurricane Odalys and [[Hurricane Polo]] formed off the Pacific coast of Mexico, the latter underwent explosive rapid intensification, adding 110 mph (180 km/h) to its wind speeds over a 24-hour period. Polo peaked as a Category 5 major hurricane on September 22 with maximum sustained winds of 180 mph (290 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 892 mb (26.34 inHg). This made Polo the second-most intense Pacific hurricane on record by central pressure, behind only [[Hurricane Patricia]] in 2015. Concurrently, [[Hurricane Nolo|Nolo]] formed south of Hawaii on September 24, bringing threat of localized flooding to the Hawaiian Islands, before it crossed the International Date Line.
{{clear}}

===Western Pacific Ocean===
{{Main|2026 Pacific typhoon season}}

[[File:2026 Pacific typhoon season summary.png|thumb|2026 Pacific typhoon season summary map]]
A tropical depression formed east of the Philippines on 13 January, marking the start of the season. The depression was subsequently named ''Ada'' by [[PAGASA]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/weather-traffic/2026/1/14/lpa-develops-into-2026-s-first-storm-0956|title=LPA develops into 2026's first storm|first=Ariel|last=Rojas|publisher=ABS-CBN News|date=14 January 2026|access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref> and later ''[[Tropical Storm Nokaen|Nokaen]]'' by the [[Japan Meteorological Agency|JMA]]<ref>{{Cite report |url= https://tgftp.nws.noaa.gov/data/raw/wt/wtpq31.rjtd..txt |title=Prognostic Reasoning No. 7 for TS 2601 Nokaen (2601) |date=January 15, 2026 |publisher=[[Japan Meteorological Agency]] |access-date= January 15, 2026}}</ref> respectively on January 14 and 15, marking it the earliest start to a season since [[2019 Pacific typhoon season|2019]]. A tropical depression formed near Guam on February 3, it later entered the PAR and was named Basyang, it was named ''[[Tropical Storm Penha|Penha]]'' the following day. Tropical Storm Nuri formed northeast of [[Yap]] on March 10. Tropical Storm [[Typhoon Sinlaku (2026)|Sinlaku]] formed west of [[Pohnpei]] on April 8, later intensified into a typhoon on April 10 and was recognised as a super typhoon on April 12, it later reached a peak of 115 knots (215 km/h) and {{cvt|905|mb|inHg|sigfig=4}}. Tropical Storm Hagupit formed near [[Chuuk Lagoon|Chuuk]] on May 5, it entered the PAR on May 9, gaining the name Caloy. Tropical Storm Jangmi formed on May 26 and entered the PAR on May 28, gaining the name Domeng, it slowly intensified into a category 1 typhoon on May 30 before making landfall in [[Wakayama Prefecture]] on June 3. A tropical depression formed on June 3, it entered the PAR on June 4, gaining the name Ester, a few hours later, JTWC classified it as a subtropical depression before making landfall in [[Taiwan]]. On June 18, Tropical Storm Mekkhala formed south of the Mariana Islands, it rapidly intensified into a Category 4 typhoon on June 22. Tropical Storm Higos formed the same day.

Activity accelerated sharply in July with [[Tropical Storm Maysak (2026)|Maysak]] forming on July 1, tracking across [[Hainan Island]] and northern [[Vietnam]] before dumping catastrophic rainfall over southwestern [[China]] that caused US$3.28 billion in damages and 39 fatalities. Immediately following, [[Typhoon Bavi (2026)|Bavi]], which formed on June 30, passed very near [[Rota, Northern Mariana Islands|Rota]], bringing destructive winds and flooding to the [[Mariana Islands]]. After tracking over the islands, Bavi caused 26 deaths in the [[Philippines]], before hitting Zhejiang, China, on July 11.

Mid-to-late summer saw the formation of many more systems. [[2026 Pacific typhoon season#Tropical Storm Haishen (Josie)|Tropical Storm Haishen]] became the first tropical storm to be recognized by the Japan Meteorological Agency, but not by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center since [[Tropical Storm Mulan (2022)|Mulan]] in [[2022 Pacific typhoon season|2022]]. In late July, [[Typhoon Noul (2026)|Typhoon Noul]] struck Guangdong as a Category 2-equivalent typhoon. Concurrently, a tropical depression crossed the [[International Date Line]] and entered the basin. It rapidly intensified into the massive [[Typhoon Dolphin (2026)|Typhoon Dolphin]], a Category 5-equivalent violent typhoon that underwent four eyewall replacement cycles as it churned through open ocean, eventually weakening before making landfall in Zhejiang, China.

As Dolphin made its long journey across the Western Pacific, a cluster of weaker storms formed. These included [[Tropical storms Kujira and Peilou|Tropical Storm Kujira]], [[Tropical Storm Chan-hom (2026)|Severe Tropical Storm Chan-hom]], [[Tropical storms Kujira and Peilou|Tropical Storm Peilou]], and [[2026 Pacific typhoon season#Tropical Storm Nangka|Tropical Storm Nangka]]. Long-lived [[Typhoon Saudel (2026)|Typhoon Saudel]] formed on August 15, rapidly attaining Category 4-equivalent status before weakening and making landfall in Zhejiang, China. It then moved across southern China and into the [[South China Sea]], where it regenerated into a tropical storm and made two mode landfalls. By late August and September, monsoonal activity fueled a flurry of short-lived systems across the basin, including [[Tropical Storm Narra]], Tropical Storm Gaenari, Tropical Storm Atsani, Typhoon Bang-Lang, Tropical Storm Etau, and Tropical Storm Krovanh, the latter of which enhanced monsoon rainfall and caused widespread flooding across the central Philippines.



A brief period of inactivity followed the dissipation of Krovanh, but activity soon resumed in late September with the development of [[Typhoon Dujuan (2026)|Typhoon Dujuan]]. Forming east of the Philippines on 19 September, Dujuan rapidly organized as it tracked north-northwestward along Japan's eastern Pacific coastline on September 21–22. The massive system brought record-breaking rainfall across the Kanto region and the Izu Islands, including a September-record 600 mm (23.6 in) of rain within 24 hours on Oshima, prompting a Level 5 landslide special warning from the Japan Meteorological Agency. Dujuan's torrential rainfall and powerful wind gusts up to 144 km/h (90 mph) caused devastating landslides and urban flooding across Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures, resulting in at least four confirmed fatalities, several missing persons, power outages for over 9,000 households, and widespread grounding of transportation networks during Japan's Silver Week holidays. Following Dujuan's passage, on 21 September, another tropical depression formed over the Philippine Sea. The system later developed into [[Typhoon Surigae (2026)|Typhoon Surigae]], a Category 4-equivalent super typhoon that brought heavy rainfall to the Philippines and Japan. 3 days after Surigae formed, a depression formed, in which that would turn into [[2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season#Deep Depression B0B 07|Deep Depression BOB 07]]. On September 27, a depression formed, in which it was named Choi-wan and it [[Rapid intensification|rapidly intensified]] into a Category 5 typhoon. On October 3, a depression formed, in which it was named Koguma the day after. Nolo, which was previously a hurricane, crossed the [[International Date Line]], and became a typhoon. In October 10, Tropical Depression 28W formed, and on October 13, the JMA noted a tropical depression near [[Micronesia]] and a day later, it strengthened into a tropical storm, receiving the name [[Typhoon Champi|Champi]]. In October 17, Champi went through [[rapid intensification]] and passes through Guam as Very Strong Typhoon.  {{clear}}

===North Indian Ocean===
{{Main|2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season}}

[[File:2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season summary.png|thumb|2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season summary map]]
On 7 January, BOB 01 formed in the Bay of Bengal.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://internal.imd.gov.in/press_release/20260107_pr_4622.pdf#:~:text=Weather%20Systems%2C%20Forecast%20and%20Warnings%20(refer%20to,Bay%20of%20Bengal%20during%20next%2048%20hours. | title=Depression over southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining East Equatorial Indian Ocean }}</ref> After six months of inactivity, on 5 July, BOB 02 formed and struck Odisha.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Depression over coastal areas of North Odisha and adjoining West Bengal |url=https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/contents/cyclone.php#. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260705164455/https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/contents/cyclone.php#. |archive-date=2026-07-05 |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=mausam.imd.gov.in |language=en}}</ref> BOB 03 formed on 26 July, causing mass flooding in Odisha as it made landfall. BOB 04 formed southeast of [[Kolkata]] on 13 August, dissipating the following day. On 17 August, BOB 05 formed inland over [[West Bengal]], dissipating 2 days later near North Jharkhand. Activity resumed in late September as a well-marked low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal organized into Depression BOB 06 on 21 September. Moving west-northwestward under the influence of the regional monsoon trough, the storm intensified into a Deep Depression on 22 September. BOB 06 made landfall near Kalingapatnam, along the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coastline, late on 23 September with peak sustained winds of 55–65 km/h (35–40 mph). The storm brought widespread heavy rainfall, urban inundation, and squally winds across coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Telangana as it moved inland and steadily weakened through 25 September.

==Systems==
===January===
[[File:Dudzai_2026-01-12_0845Z.jpg|thumb|[[Cyclone Dudzai]]]]
January was an unusually active month, with sixteen tropical cyclones forming and seven of them being named, the highest number since [[Tropical cyclones in 2021|2021]]. Out of the seven, [[Cyclone Dudzai|Dudzai]] is the strongest cyclone of the month. Two cyclones, [[Cyclone Grant (2025)|Grant]] and [[Cyclone Iggy (2026)|Iggy]], persisted from [[Tropical cyclones in 2025|the previous year]] into the current year. In the Northern Indian Ocean, [[2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season#Deep Depression BOB 01|BOB 01]] formed on January 7, making it one of the earliest depressions ever recorded in the basin. Also, the Western Pacific season began with the formation of [[Tropical Storm Nokaen]] (locally known as Ada in the [[Philippines]]), which was named on January 15, although it originally formed two days earlier as a tropical depression. Nokaen became the first tropical cyclone to form in the Western Pacific in January since [[Tropical Storm Pabuk (2019)|Tropical Storm Pabuk]] in [[2019 Pacific typhoon season|2019]].
In the Southwestern Indian Ocean, Cyclones [[Cyclone Dudzai|Dudzai]], [[Tropical Storm Ewetse|Ewetse]] and [[Cyclone Fytia|Fytia]] formed, with the latter two affecting [[Madagascar]] and the former, Dudzai, intensifying into the month’s strongest system. To add on, Fytia rapidly intensified into a Category 3-equivalent cyclone in the [[Mozambique Channel]] before making landfall in Madagascar, causing 12 deaths in the country. <ref name="k081">{{cite web | last=Rowlands | first=Lyndal | title='Monstrous': Cyclone Gezani hits Madagascar, leaving at least 31 dead | website=Al Jazeera | date=11 Feb 2026 | url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/11/monstrous-cyclone-gezani-hits-madagascar-with-reports-of-severe-damage | access-date=7 Apr 2026}}</ref> In the Australian region, [[Cyclone Mitchell (2026)|Cyclone Mitchell]] formed from a meandering tropical low. It then rapidly intensified into a Category 3-equivalent cyclone on the Australian scale.

===February===
[[File:Horacio 2026-02-23 2101Z.jpg|thumb|[[2025–26 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season#Intense Tropical Cyclone Horacio|Cyclone Horacio]]]]
February was below average in activity, however, it spawned several powerful tropical cyclones, including Horacio, which rapidly intensified into a Category 5 tropical cyclone and became the strongest tropical cyclone of the month; additionally, it is also the first tropical cyclone to do so this year. Eight tropical cyclones have formed this month, with five of them being named. February started with [[Cyclone Fytia]] and [[Cyclone Mitchell]] persisting from the previous month into this month. The series of early-season systems of the Western Pacific continued with Basyang, which formed near Yap on February 2. It was later named [[Tropical Storm Penha|Penha]] two days later, becoming the first tropical cyclone to form in the month of February since [[Tropical Storm Dujuan (2021)|Tropical Storm Dujuan]] [[2021 Pacific typhoon season|in 2021]]. Penha went on to make landfall in [[Bayabas, Surigao del Sur]] on February 5 and was followed by multiple landfalls in Visayas the next day. Afterwards, land interaction and hostile conditions caused the storm to degenerate into a tropical depression. On February 10, Gezani caused over 63 deaths in Madagascar. On February 24, Horacio rapidly intensified into a Category 5 tropical cyclone. In the South Pacific basin, Urmil developed on February 27, becoming the latest-forming first-named tropical cyclone of the season within that basin, breaking the record set by [[Cyclone Bart (2017)|Cyclone Bart]] during the 2016–17 season. On February 28, a Subtropical Depression formed off the coast of the State of Rio De Janeiro in the South Atlantic.

===March===
[[File:Narelle 2026-03-19 0357Z.jpg|thumb|[[Cyclone Narelle (2026)|Cyclone Narelle]]]]
March was slightly inactive, featuring ten storms, four of which were named. Out of the four, [[Cyclone Narelle (2026)|Narelle]] was the strongest storm of the month. It started with the dissipation of [[Cyclone Urmil (2026)|Cyclone Urmil]], a [[South Atlantic tropical cyclone#Subtropical Depression #01-2026|subtropical depression]], and [[2025-26 Australian region cyclone season#Other systems|Tropical Low 26U]] persisting from the previous month into this month. Subtropical Storm Caiobá soon followed suit in the South Atlantic, coexisting with the previously mentioned subtropical depression, the first time in recorded history where two simultaneous subtropical cyclones existed in the South Atlantic. Meanwhile in the Western Pacific Basin, Tropical Storm Nuri and a Tropical Depression formed northeast of [[Yap]] on 10 March, continuing the early-season activity. On 15 March, Cyclone Narelle formed off the Australian coast, and then rapidly intensified upon its formation and naming, eventually becoming the strongest cyclone in the basin since [[Cyclone Ilsa]] in [[2022–23 Australian region cyclone season|2023]]. Narelle would later cross Australia and reach secondary peak as a Category 4. On 17 March, a European windstorm named Samuel, or Jolina in Germany, transitioned into a [[Mediterranean tropical-like cyclone]] before making landfall in Libya early the next day.
