In 2000, 140.2 million personal computers were shipped, at an estimated value of $226 billion. Worldwide shipments of personal computers surpassed the 100-million mark in 1999, growing to 113.5 million units from 93.3 million units in 1998.{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jan-24-fi-57038-story.html |title=Dell Passes Compaq as Top PC Seller in U.S |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=13 January 2009 |first=Nona |last=Yates |date=24 January 2000 |archive-date=27 December 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111227142110/http://articles.latimes.com/2000/jan/24/business/fi-57038 |url-status=live }} In 1999, Asia had 14.1 million units shipped.{{citation |url=http://www.zdnetasia.com/news/hardware/0,39042972,13025480,00.htm |title=Economic recovery bumps AP 1999 PC shipments to record high |publisher=zdnetasia.com |access-date=13 January 2009 }}{{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} As of June 2008, the number of personal computers in use worldwide hit one billion,{{cite web|title=Worldwide PC use to reach 1 billion by 2008: report|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/worldwide-pc-use-to-reach-1-billion-by-2008-report-1.666962|publisher=CBC News|access-date=12 June 2007|archive-date=23 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140823181604/http://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/worldwide-pc-use-to-reach-1-billion-by-2008-report-1.666962|url-status=live}} while another billion is expected to be reached by 2014. Mature markets like the United States, [[Western Europe]] and Japan accounted for 58% of the worldwide installed PCs. The [[emerging market]]s were expected to double their installed PCs by 2012 and to take 70% of the second billion PCs. About 180 million computers (16% of the existing installed base) were expected to be replaced and 35 million to be dumped into landfill in 2008. The whole installed base grew 12% annually.{{cite press release|url=http://www.gartner.com/it/page.jsp?id=703807 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081204005841/http://www.gartner.com/it/page.jsp?id=703807 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 December 2008 |title=Gartner Says More than 1 Billion PCs in Use Worldwide and Headed to 2 Billion Units by 2014 |publisher=[[Gartner]] |date=23 June 2008 |access-date=14 October 2010}}{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/technologyNews/idUSL2324525420080623 |title=Computers in use pass 1 billion mark: Gartner |publisher=Reuters |author=Tarmo Virki |date=23 June 2008 |access-date=14 October 2010 |archive-date=19 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090919051207/http://www.reuters.com/article/technologyNews/idUSL2324525420080623 |url-status=live }} Based on [[International Data Corporation]] (IDC) data for Q2 2011, for the first time China surpassed US in PC shipments by 18.5 million and 17.7 million respectively. This trend reflects the rising of emerging markets as well as the relative stagnation of mature regions. Besides the regular computer manufacturers, companies making especially rugged versions of computers have sprung up, offering alternatives for people operating their machines in extreme weather or environments.{{cite web |url=http://www.ruggedpcreview.com/2_leaders.html |title=Rugged PC leaders |author=Conrad H. Blickenstorfer |publisher=Ruggedpcreview.com |access-date=14 October 2010 |archive-date=25 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425055712/http://www.ruggedpcreview.com/2_leaders.html |url-status=live }} In 2011, [[Deloitte]] consulting firm predicted that, [[smartphone]]s and [[tablet computer]]s as computing devices would surpass the PCs salesTablets, smartphones to outsell PCs https://news.yahoo.com/s/afp/20110210/tc_afp/itinternettelecomequipmentmobileconsumerproduct {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110305125634/http://news.yahoo.com/s/afp/20110210/tc_afp/itinternettelecomequipmentmobileconsumerproduct |date=5 March 2011 }} (as has happened since 2012). As of 2013, worldwide sales of PCs had begun to fall as many consumers moved to tablets and smartphones. Sales of 90.3 million units in the fourth quarter of 2012 represented a 4.9% decline from sales in the fourth quarter of 2011.{{cite news|title=Gartner Says Declining Worldwide PC Shipments in Fourth Quarter of 2012 Signal Structural Shift of PC Market|url=http://www.gartner.com/it/page.jsp?id=2301715|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130115050601/https://www.gartner.com/it/page.jsp?id=2301715|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 January 2013|access-date=18 January 2013|newspaper=Gartner.Com|date=14 January 2013|type=Press release}} Global PC sales fell sharply in the first quarter of 2013, according to IDC data. The 14% year-over-year decline was the largest on record since the firm began tracking in 1994, and double what analysts had been expecting.{{cite news|title=Feeble PC industry stumbles to steep sales drop during first quarter as Windows makeover flops |agency=Associated Press |work=[[Washington Times]] |date=10 April 2013 |url=https://articles.washingtonpost.com/2013-04-10/business/38436022_1_pc-sales-pc-market-traditional-pc |access-date=11 April 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130419022401/http://articles.washingtonpost.com/2013-04-10/business/38436022_1_pc-sales-pc-market-traditional-pc |archive-date=19 April 2013}} The decline of Q2 2013 PC shipments marked the fifth straight quarter of falling sales.{{cite web |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/business/news/steve-ballmers-retirement-leaves-microsoft-in-a-replacement-crisis-700543/ |title=Steve Ballmer's retirement leaves Microsoft in a replacement crisis |date=24 August 2013 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |agency= Bloomberg News |first1=Ian |last1=King |first2=Sarah |last2=Frier |first3=Dina |last3=Bass |access-date=25 August 2013 |archive-date=24 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130824194335/http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/business/news/steve-ballmers-retirement-leaves-microsoft-in-a-replacement-crisis-700543/ |url-status=dead }} "This is horrific news for PCs", remarked an analyst. "It's all about mobile computing now. We have definitely reached the tipping point." Data from [[Gartner]] showed a similar decline for the same time period. China's [[Lenovo Group]] bucked the general trend as strong sales to first-time buyers in the developing world allowed the company's sales to stay flat overall. [[Windows 8]], which was designed to look similar to tablet/smartphone software, was cited as a contributing factor in the decline of new PC sales. "Unfortunately, it seems clear that the Windows 8 launch not only didn't provide a positive boost to the PC market, but appears to have slowed the market," said IDC Vice President Bob O'Donnell.{{cite news|title=PC Sales Still in a Slump, Despite New Offerings|author=Nick Wingfield|date=10 April 2013|work=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/11/technology/data-show-steep-decline-in-pc-shipments.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 April 2013|archive-date=11 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130411005435/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/11/technology/data-show-steep-decline-in-pc-shipments.html|url-status=live}} In August 2013, Credit Suisse published research findings that attributed around 75% of the operating profit share of the PC industry to Microsoft (operating system) and Intel (semiconductors).{{cite web|title=The Apple Vs. Samsung Title Fight for Mobile Supremacy|url=http://www.thefinancialist.com/the-apple-vs-samsung-title-fight-for-mobile-supremacy/|work=The Financialist|publisher=Credit Suisse|access-date=13 August 2013|date=8 August 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130814130300/http://www.thefinancialist.com/the-apple-vs-samsung-title-fight-for-mobile-supremacy/|archive-date=14 August 2013}} According to IDC, in 2013 PC shipments dropped by 9.8% as the greatest drop-ever in line with consumers trends to use mobile devices.{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2014/03/04/idc-pc-shipments-2013/ |title=PC shipments faced their steepest-ever drop in 2013 |author=John Fingas |date=4 March 2014 |access-date=8 September 2017 |archive-date=25 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625170553/https://www.engadget.com/2014/03/04/idc-pc-shipments-2013/ |url-status=live }} In the second quarter of 2018, PC sales grew for the first time since the first quarter of 2012. According to research firm Gartner, the growth mainly came from the business market while the consumer market experienced decline.{{cite news|last=Warren|first=Tom|date=13 July 2018|title=PC sales are growing for the first time in six years|url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/7/13/17567760/pc-sales-growth-idc-gartner-july-2018|work=[[The Verge]]|access-date=14 July 2018|archive-date=13 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713183423/https://www.theverge.com/2018/7/13/17567760/pc-sales-growth-idc-gartner-july-2018|url-status=live}} In 2020, as the result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] with more people working at home and learning remotely, PC sales grew by 26.1% compared to previous years according to [[International Data Group|IDC]].{{Cite web |title=PC Sales Remain on Fire as Fourth Quarter Shipments Grow 26.1% Over the Previous Year, According to IDC |url=https://www.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prUS47274421 |access-date=24 July 2022 |website=IDC: The premier global market intelligence company |archive-date=30 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211230151858/https://www.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prUS47274421 |url-status=dead }} According to Canalys, 2020 was the highest growth rate for the PC market since 2011.{{Cite web |last=Kunert |first=Paul |title=Laptops are on fire! In a good way (if you're selling). PC sales race to highest growth rate since 2011 |url=https://www.theregister.com/2020/10/12/pc_sales_up_2020/ |access-date=24 July 2022 |website=www.theregister.com |language=en |archive-date=24 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220724094134/https://www.theregister.com/2020/10/12/pc_sales_up_2020/ |url-status=live }} This upward trend continued into 2021, with global PC shipments reaching over 340 million units, the highest since 2012, representing a 14.6% year-over-year growth.{{Cite web |last=Rubino |first=Daniel |date=12 January 2022 |title=Report: Record-breaking 341 million PCs shipped in 2021, highest since 2012, with 'digital acceleration' for 2022 |url=https://www.windowscentral.com/canalys-pc-market-2021-report |access-date=5 May 2025 |website=Windows Central}} [[Notebook computer|Notebooks]] and mobile workstations led the charge, with shipments growing 16% to reach 275 million units, while desktops and desktop workstations increased 7% to reach 66 million units.{{Cite web |last=www.ETTelecom.com |title=Global PC shipments hit 341 mn units in 2021, largest since 2012 - ET Telecom |url=https://telecom.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/global-pc-shipments-hit-341-mn-units-in-2021-largest-since-2012/88866568 |access-date=5 May 2025 |website=ETTelecom.com}} Major vendors such as [[Lenovo]], [[HP Inc.|HP]], [[Dell]], and [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] all saw significant increases in sales.{{Cite news |title=PC shipments jumped 15% to 341 million units in 2021 |url=https://www.theregister.com/2022/01/12/canalys_pc_2021/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241016012509/https://www.theregister.com/2022/01/12/canalys_pc_2021/ |archive-date=16 October 2024 |access-date=5 May 2025 |url-status=live }} The market saw increased demand not only from consumers and students but also from businesses investing in hybrid work infrastructure. However, by late 2022, the market began to stabilize as demand cooled down and supply chain challenges, including chip shortages, began to ease. Worldwide shipments of desktop and laptop computers fell by 19.5% in the third quarter of 2022 compared with the year-ago period, marking the steepest decline Gartner has documented in more than two decades of tracking the market.{{Cite web |date=11 October 2022 |title=Global PC sector suffers worst drop as China chip curbs loom |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/tech-news-technology/global-pc-sector-suffers-worst-drop-as-china-chip-curbs-loom-8202229/ |access-date=5 May 2025 |website=The Indian Express}} After a period of volatility, the global PC market began to stabilize in 2023. According to IDC, worldwide PC shipments during the fourth quarter of 2024 grew 1.8% year-over-year, reaching 68.9 million units.{{Cite web |title=The PC Market Closed out 2024 with Slight Growth and Mixed Views on What 2025 Will Bring, according to IDC |url=https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prUS53061925 |access-date=5 May 2025 |website=IDC: The premier global market intelligence company}} Canalys reported a 3.2% annual growth in the first quarter of 2024, totaling 57.2 million units, with notebook shipments increasing by 4.2%.{{Cite web |title=Canalys Newsroom - Global PC shipments up 3% in first quarter of 2024 |url=https://www.canalys.com/newsroom/global-pc-market-q1-2024 |access-date=5 May 2025 |website=www.canalys.com}} In the first quarter of 2025, global PC shipments experienced a significant uptick, growing 9.4% year-over-year to 62.7 million units. This surge was partly attributed to manufacturers accelerating shipments to the U.S. ahead of newly implemented tariffs under President Donald Trump's trade policies. Lenovo maintained its lead in the global PC market, shipping 15.2 million units with an 11% growth, followed by HP with 12.8 million units (6% growth), Dell with 9.5 million units (3% growth), and Apple with 6.5 million units, marking a 22% increase.{{Cite web |title=Canalys Newsroom - Worldwide PC shipments up 9% in Q1 2025 but tariffs threaten future market performance |url=https://canalys.com/newsroom/worldwide-pc-shipments-q1-2025 |access-date=5 May 2025 |website=www.canalys.com |language=en}} The integration of [[artificial intelligence]] (AI) capabilities into PCs emerged as a significant trend during this period. ===Average selling price=== Selling prices of personal computers steadily declined due to lower costs of production and manufacture, while the capabilities of computers increased. In 1975, an Altair kit sold for around only {{US$|400}}, but required customers to solder components into circuit boards; peripherals required to interact with the system in alphanumeric form instead of blinking lights would add another {{US$|long=no|2000}}, and the resultant system was of use only to hobbyists.Marvin B. Sussman ''Personal Computers and the Family'' [[Routledge]], 1985 {{ISBN|0-86656-361-X}}, p. 90. At their introduction in 1981, the {{US$|1795}} price of the [[Osborne 1]] and its competitor [[Kaypro]] was considered an attractive price point; these systems had text-only displays and only floppy disks for storage. By 1982, [[Michael Dell]] observed that a personal computer system selling at retail for about {{US$|3000}} was made of components that cost the dealer about {{US$|long=no|600}}; typical gross margin on a computer unit was around {{US$|long=no|1000}}.Kateri M. Drexler ''Icons of business: an encyclopedia of mavericks, movers, and shakers, Volume 1'', [[Greenwood Publishing Group]], 2007, {{ISBN|0-313-33863-9}}, p. 102 The total value of personal computer purchases in the US in 1983 was about {{US$|long=no|4 billion}}. By late 1998, the average selling price of personal computer systems in the United States had dropped below {{US$|long=no|1000}}.[http://www.pcworld.com/article/9150/average_pc_price_drops_below_1000.html Nancy Weil, ''Average PC Price drops below {{US$|long=no|1000}}''], ''[[PC World]]'' December 1998. Retrieved 17 November 2010. {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011152403/http://www.pcworld.com/article/9150/average_pc_price_drops_below_1000.html |date=11 October 2011 }} For [[Microsoft Windows]] systems, the [[average selling price]] (ASP) showed a decline in 2008/2009, possibly due to low-cost [[netbook]]s, drawing {{US$|long=no|569}} for [[desktop computer]]s and $689 for [[laptop]]s at U.S. retail in August 2008. In 2009, ASP had further fallen to {{US$|long=no|533}} for desktops and to {{US$|long=no|602}} for notebooks by January and to {{val|p=$|540| and |560}} in February.{{cite web |url=http://www.eweek.com/c/a/Windows/Netbooks-Are-Destroying-the-Laptop-Market-and-Microsoft-Needs-to-Act-Now-863307/ |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20090417001909/http://www.eweek.com/c/a/Windows/Netbooks-Are-Destroying-the-Laptop-Market-and-Microsoft-Needs-to-Act-Now-863307/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 April 2009 |title=Netbooks Are Destroying the Laptop Market and Microsoft Needs to Act Now |publisher=[[eWeek]] |author=Joe Wilcox |date=16 April 2009 |access-date=14 October 2010 }} According to research firm [[NPD Group|NPD]], the average selling price of all Windows portable PCs has fallen from {{US$|long=no|659}} in October 2008 to {{US$|long=no|519}} in October 2009.{{cite web |url=http://www.cio.com/article/509556/Falling_PC_Prices_Pit_Microsoft_Against_PC_Makers |title=Falling PC Prices Pit Microsoft Against PC Makers |author=Shane O'Neill |date=2 December 2009 |access-date=14 October 2010 |archive-date=12 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312212746/http://www.cio.com/article/509556/Falling_PC_Prices_Pit_Microsoft_Against_PC_Makers |url-status=dead }} ==Environmental impact== {{Main|Computer recycling}} External costs of environmental impact are not fully included in the selling price of personal computers.{{cite web|last1=Mattison|first1=Richard|title=The true cost of personal computers|url=https://www.greenbiz.com/blog/2012/10/03/true-cost-personal-computers|website=GreenBiz|publisher=GreenBiz Group Inc.|access-date=28 September 2016|date=3 October 2012|archive-date=2 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161002102420/https://www.greenbiz.com/blog/2012/10/03/true-cost-personal-computers|url-status=live}} Personal computers have become a large contributor to the 50 million tons of discarded electronic waste generated annually, according to the [[United Nations Environment Programme]]. To address the [[electronic waste]] issue affecting developing countries and the environment, [[Extended producer responsibility|extended producer responsibility (EPR)]] acts have been implemented in various countries and states.{{cite journal|last1=Nash|first1=Jennifer|last2=Bosso|first2=Christopher|title=Extended Producer Responsibility in the United States: Full Speed Ahead?|journal=Journal of Industrial Ecology|date=2013|volume=17|issue=2 – RPP–2013–04|pages=175–185|url=http://www.hks.harvard.edu/var/ezp_site/storage/fckeditor/file/pdfs/centers-programs/centers/mrcbg/publications/awp/Nash_Bosso_2013-10.pdf|access-date=23 August 2014|doi=10.1111/j.1530-9290.2012.00572.x|s2cid=154297251|archive-date=26 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826114146/http://www.hks.harvard.edu/var/ezp_site/storage/fckeditor/file/pdfs/centers-programs/centers/mrcbg/publications/awp/Nash_Bosso_2013-10.pdf|url-status=dead}} In the absence of comprehensive national legislation or regulation on the export and import of electronic waste, the [[Silicon Valley Toxics Coalition]] and BAN (Basel Action Network) teamed up with electronic recyclers in the US and Canada to create an e-steward program for the orderly disposal of electronic waste.{{cite web |title=Basel Action Network (BAN) : California's Santa Clara County Commits to Highest Standard of Responsible E-Waste Recycling |url=http://old.ban.org/ban_news/2010/101014_santa_clara_county_commits.html |website=old.ban.org |publisher=Basel Action Network |access-date=20 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726185346/http://old.ban.org/ban_news/2010/101014_santa_clara_county_commits.html |archive-date=26 July 2020 |date=14 October 2010}} Some organizations {{who|date=September 2025}} oppose EPR regulation, and claim that manufacturers naturally move toward reduced material and energy use.{{citation 1383163941.title: Switzerland in the Eurovision Song Contest 1957
1383163941.content:
{{Short description|none}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2019}}
{{Infobox song contest national year
| Year = 1957
| Broadcaster = [[Swiss Broadcasting Corporation]] (SRG SSR)
| Country = Switzerland
| Selection process = {{lang|de|Internationaler Schlagerwettbewerb}} ''1957''
| Selection date = 11 February 1957
| Song = {{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}
| Artist = [[Lys Assia]]
| Writer = {{Unbulleted list|[[Géo Voumard]]|[[Émile Gardaz]]}}
| Final result = 8th, 5 votes
}}

Switzerland was represented at the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1957]] with the song "{{lang|fr|L'enfant que j'étais|i=no}}", composed by [[Géo Voumard]], with lyrics by [[Émile Gardaz]], and performed by [[Lys Assia]]. The Swiss participating broadcaster, the [[Swiss Broadcasting Corporation]] (SRG SSR), selected its entry through a national final. Assia had already represented Switzerland at the {{escyr|1956||previous contest}} performing both Swiss entries, and winning with "{{lang|fr|[[Refrain (Lys Assia song)|Refrain]]|i=no}}".

==Before Eurovision==
=== {{lang|de|Internationaler Schlagerwettbewerb 1957}} ===
The [[Swiss Broadcasting Corporation]] (SRG SSR) held a national final to select its entry for the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1957]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=27 January 1957 |title=Das schwarze Brett: Europäischer Schlagerwettbewerb 1957 |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |page=24 |language=de |issue=4 |oclc=638310336}}</ref> Songwriters who applied for the selection were required to have Swiss citizenship or to have been residing in Switzerland for at least ten years and could submit up to three songs.<ref name="da rules">{{cite news |date=8 November 1956 |title=IIe Concours international de la Chanson |trans-title=2nd International Song Contest |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/324701/view?page=21 |access-date=27 July 2025 |work=Radio Je vois tout |location= |page=2085 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=34 |issue=45}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news |date=2 November 1956 |title=Europäischer Schlagerwettbewerb 1957 |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=TGW19561102-01.2.17.9 |access-date=30 July 2025 |work={{ill|Berner Tagwacht|de}} |page=4 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=64 |issue=268 |oclc=1367998098}}</ref> SRG SSR opened a submission window in autumn 1956, with the deadline on 5 January 1957.<ref name="da rules" /><ref name=":4" /> The broadcaster received 109 songs (69 in German, 22 in French, and 18 in Italian<ref name="langsubs">{{Cite web |title=Schweizer Ausscheidung - Finale Suisse - Finale Svizzera 1957 |url=https://vorstadtmusic.ch/1957.html |access-date=22 January 2025 |website=Vorstadt Music & Records}}</ref>) from 75 songwriters.<ref name=":0" />

The internal jury in [[Bern]] were tasked with choosing at most twenty songs<ref name="da rules"/> and ultimately selected eleven songs to compete in the selection.<ref name="bern">{{cite news |title=Concours National — Grand Prix Eurovision 1957 de la Chanson européene |trans-title=National Competition — Eurovision Grand Prix 1957 |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/325498/view?page=18&p=separate& |access-date=27 July 2025 |date=24 January 1957 |location= |page=18 |language=fr |work=Radio Je vois tout |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]]}}</ref><ref name="composer it"/>

The national final, entitled ''Internationaler Schlagerwettbewerb 1957'', was held on 11 February 1957 at 21:00 [[Central European Time|CET]] (20:00 [[Coordinated Universal Time|UTC]]) at the Embassysaal in [[Badrutt's Palace Hotel]], [[St. Moritz]].<ref name="composer it">{{cite news |title=Sarà scelta lunedi la più bella canzone svizzera |trans-title=The most beautiful Swiss song will be chosen on Monday |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=xbtXhJoB2WlOfa--QAJ4 |access-date=22 January 2025 |work=Eco di Locarno |date=9 February 1957 |location=[[Locarno]], Switzerland |page=3 |language=it |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}}}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite news |date=10 February 1957 |title=Télé-Suisse |work=Télévision Programme Magazine |page=23 |language=fr |volume=3 |issue=68 |oclc=472721214}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=10 February 1957 |title=Montag 11. Februar 1957 |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |pages=VI–VII |language=de |issue=6 |oclc=638310336}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=9 February 1957 |title=Anlässe dieser Tage |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=EDP19570209-01.2.6 |access-date=30 July 2025 |work={{ill|Engadiner Post|de}} |page=2 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=66 |issue=17 |issn=1661-0105 |oclc=806846627}}</ref> It was broadcast on [[Schweizer Fernsehen|German-]] and [[Télévision Suisse Romande|French-speaking Swiss Television]] as well as on the radio stations [[Radio SRF 1|Beromünster]], [[La Première (Switzerland)|Sottens]], and [[RSI Rete Uno|Monte Ceneri]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":14">{{Cite news |date=10 February 1957 |title=Fernseh-Programme |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |page=XXX |language=de |issue=6 |oclc=638310336}}</ref> The director was [[Franco Marazzi]].<ref name=":9" /> The program was presented by |date=17 February 1957 |title=Das schwarze Brett: Schlagertage in St. Moritz |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |page=24 |language=de |issue=7 |oclc=638310336}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite news |date=5 |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=66 |issue=15 |issn=1661-0105 |oclc=806846627}}</ref><ref name="heidi" /> The artists were accompanied by [[Radiotelevisione svizzera|RSI]]'s orchestra Radiosa under the musical direction of [[Fernando Paggi]].<ref name="heidi">{{cite news |last= |first= |date=12 February 1957 |title=Per una canzone «nazionale» |trans-title=For a "national" song |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=-r1ihpoB2WlOfa--GSDY |access-date=22 January 2025 |work=[[Giornale del Popolo]] |location=[[Lugano]], Switzerland |page=2 |language=it |via={{ill|Sistema |access-date=22 January 2025 |work=Libera Stampa |location=[[Lugano]], Switzerland |page=2 |language=it |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}} |volume=45 |issue=37 |oclc=732473625}}</ref><ref The eleven entries were performed by [[Lys Assia]], Jo Roland and Gianni Ferraresi, with Lys Assia performing five songs, Jo Roland three, and Gianni Ferraresi also three songs.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":5" /> Three entries were sung in German, four in French, and four in Italian.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Villani |first=Silvano |date=12 February 1957 |title=Trasmesso alla televisione: il Festival svizzero della canzone |work=[[Corriere della Sera]] |page=6 |language=it |volume=82 |issue=37 |oclc=1371227030}}</ref> The running order was decided by a draw.<ref name="stm jury" /> The act.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 March 1957 |title=Melodischer Kampf um einen grossen Preis |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |pages=12–13 |language=de |issue=9 |oclc=638310336}}</ref> 

Four regional juries, located in [[Basel]] (representing radio [[Radio SRF 1|Beromünster]]), [[Geneva]] (for radio [[La Première (Switzerland)|Sottens]]), [[Lugano]] (for radio [[RSI Rete Uno|Monte Ceneri]]), and St. Moritz (representing Swiss Television), decided the winner.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="stm jury" /><ref name=":2" /> Each jury consisted of ten members, with each jury member giving one vote to their favourite song.<ref name="all da scores" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite news |date=14 February 1957 |title='L'enfant que j'étais' canzone svizzera 1957 |trans-title='L'enfant que j'étais' Swiss song of 1957 |url=https://aqp.sbt.ti.ch/viewer?id=zrtXhJoB2WlOfa--SQIx |access-date=24 September 2025 |work=L'Eco di Locarno |language=it |volume=32 |issue=19 |page=2 |via={{ill|Sistema bibliotecario ticinese|it}}}}</ref><ref name="stm jury" /> The jury members from St. Mortiz were present within the location of the final, while the remaining juries delivered their votes in their respective cities.<ref name="all da scores" /> The ten jurors from Geneva consisted of Marius Berthet (jury president), Jean-Pierre Allenbach, Robert Burnier, {{ill|Raymond Colbert (radio personality)|lt=Raymond Colbert|fr}}, Jo Excoffier, Frank Guibat, Lisette Martin, Robert Pibouleau, Clairette Sacchi, and [[Julien-François Zbinden]].<ref name="stm jury">{{Cite magazine |date=7 February 1957 |title=Le Grand Prix Européen de la Chanson |trans-title=The European Song Grand Prix |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/325512/view?page=24&p=separate& |access-date=23 July 2025 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=24 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=35 |issue=6}}</ref> In the Luganese jury, Bruno Pagnamenta was the jury president.<ref name=":12" /> The juries gave their votes via telephone.<ref name=":10" />

Following the voting, three songs tied for first place with 8 votes each: "{{lang|fr|La Vie|i=no}}" and "{{lang|fr|Avec vingt sous|i=no}}", sung by Jo Roland, and "{{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}", performed by Lys Assia.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=3 March 1957 |title=Melodischer Kampf um einen grossen Preis |work=Schweizer Radio-Zeitung |pages=12–13 |language=de |issue=9 |oclc=638310336}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> After all three songs had been performed once more, a revote of the tying entries took place to decide the winner.<ref name="results claim 2"/> The winner was the song "{{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}", composed by [[Géo Voumard]], with lyrics by [[Émile Gardaz]], arranged by Mario Robbiani, and performed by [[Lys Assia]].<ref name="all da scores" /><ref name=":2" /> The songwriters Gardaz and Voumard had already won both the national final and the Eurovision Song Contest for {{esccnty|Switzerland|y=1956|t=Switzerland in 1956}}, in both |language=fr}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite book |last=O'Connor |first=John Kennedy |title=The Eurovision Song Contest: The Official History |publisher=Carlton |year=2010 |isbn=978-1-84732-521-1 |edition=Updated |location=London |pages=8–9 |oclc=699877063}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite news |date=13 February 1957 |title=Cronaca Ticinese: Saranno ancora gli autori del fortunato 'Refrain' a ===Releases and archives===
"{{lang|fr|L'Enfant que j'étais|i=no}}" by [[Lys Assia]] was first recorded and released on a single under the same title in 1957.<ref name="lal">{{cite AV media |last=Assia |first=Lys |title=L'enfant Que J'étais |type=Vinyl |language=fr |publisher=[[Telefunken]] |id=U 55 039 }}</ref> In 1998, the song was featured in a CD compilation titled "{{lang|de|Concours Eurovision De La Chanson 1956-1998: Schweizer Beiträge|i=no}}", which compiled every Swiss Eurovision entry at the time.<ref name="vorstadt">{{cite AV media |last= |first= |title=Concours Eurovision De La Chanson 1956-1998: Schweizer Beiträge |type=CD |language=de |publisher=Vorstadt Records |id=VRS 990 001-2 }}</ref>

Jo Roland released "{{lang|fr|La Vie|i=no}}" and by "{{lang|fr|Avec vingt sous|i=no}}" in his debut single, titled after the former song, in 1957.<ref name="jrl">{{cite AV media |last=Roland |first=Jo |title=La Vie |type=Vinyl |language=fr |publisher=[[Decca Records|Decca]] |id=18 438 }}</ref><ref name="jo">{{Cite magazine |date=25 October 1962 |title=Un Oscar qui s'apelle: Jo Roland |trans-title=An Oscar named: Jo Roland |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/322510/view?page=5&p=separate& |access-date=1 November 2026 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=5 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume= |issue=}}</ref> Gianni Ferraresi would release "{{lang|it|Bellissima|i=no}}" two years later.<ref name="gfb">{{cite AV media |last=Ferraresi |first=Gianni |title=Bellissima |type=Vinyl |language=it |publisher={{ill|Music (casa discografica)|it|lt=Music}} |id=EPM 10141 }}</ref>

Studio recordings of all competing entries have been preserved in the [[Swiss National Sound Archives]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Canzoni presentate al festival svizzero della canzone a Saint Moritz (DAT12995) |url=https://www.fonoteca.ch/cgi-bin/oecgi4.exe/inet_fnbasedetail?REC_ID=89781.027&LNG_ID=ENU |access-date=9 March 2026 |website=Swiss National Sound Archives (catalog) |publisher=[[Swiss National Sound Archives]] |place=[[Lugano]] |id=DAT12995}}</ref>

== At Eurovision ==
[[File:Lys Assia (1957).jpg|thumb|[[Lys Assia]] represented Switzerland in the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1957]]]]

At the Eurovision Song Contest 1957 in [[Frankfurt]], the Swiss entry was performed tenth and last in the running order, following {{esccnty|Denmark|y=1957}}.<ref name="1957results">{{cite web |title=Final of Frankfurt 1957 – Eurovision Song Contest |url=https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220517112718/https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final |archive-date=17 May 2022 |access-date=3 June 2022 |publisher=European Broadcasting Union}}</ref> The Swiss entry was conducted at the contest by the event's musical director [[Willy Berking]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Thorsson |first=Leif |title=Melodifestivalen genom tiderna: de Svenska uttagningarna och de internationella finalerna |last2=Verhage |first2=Martin |publisher=Premium |year=2006 |isbn=91-89136-29-2 |edition=2nd |location=Stockholm |page=350 |language=sv |oclc=185355414}}</ref> At the close of voting, Switzerland had received five votes in total; the country finished shared eight among the ten participants.<ref name="1957final">{{cite web |title=Frankfurt 1957 |url=https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final |publisher=Eurovision Song Contest |access-date=28 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327160227/https://eurovision.tv/event/frankfurt-1957/final/results/switzerland |archive-date=27 March 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="1957detailed"/>

The contest was broadcast in Switzerland on French-speaking [[Télévision Suisse Romande|TSR]] with commentary by [[Robert Beauvais]], on [[SRF 1|German-speaking television]], as well as on radio [[Radio SRF 1|Beromünster]] and [[RTS Première|Sottens]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 March 1957 |title=Radio Beromünster + UKW |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=WVF19570301-02.2.20 |access-date=3 August 2025 |work=Walliser Volksfreund |page=3 |language=de |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=38 |issue=17 |oclc=806848191}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2 March 1957 |title=Radio Sottens |url=https://www.e-newspaperarchives.ch/?a=d&d=LGE19570302-01.2.12 |access-date=3 August 2025 |work=[[La Gruyère (newspaper)|La Gruyère]] |page=3 |language=fr |via=[[e-newspaperarchives.ch]] |volume=76 |issue=26 |issn=2296-2409 |oclc=806828885}}</ref><ref name=":14" /> Excerpts were broadcast on 11 March 1957 at 20:00 CET on the second program of radio [[RSI Rete Uno|Monte Ceneri]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 March 1957 |title=Lundi 11 mars: Second programme |url=https://www.scriptorium.ch/zoom/325528/view?page=29 |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Radio Je vois tout |page=29 |language=fr |via=[[Scriptorium (website)|Scriptorium]] |volume=35 |issue=10}}</ref>

=== Voting ===
Each participating broadcaster assembled a ten-member jury panel.<ref name=":13">{{Cite journal |date=January–February 1957 |title=Grand Prix Eurovision 1957 de la Chanson européenne |journal=Bulletin de l'U.E.R. |language=fr |publisher=[[European Broadcasting Union]] |volume=8 |issue=41 |page= |pages=109–113 |oclc=473721192}}</ref> Every jury member could give one vote to their favourite song.<ref name=":13" />

The '''Ekumeku Movement''' consisted of a series of uprisings against the rising power of the [[Royal Niger Company]] of the [[British Empire]] by Anioma Igbo people. The British penetration of [[Nigeria]] met with various forms of resistance throughout the country. In the south, the British had to fight many wars.

'''Žarko Puhovski''' (born 15 December 1946) is a [[Croatia]]n professor, political analyst, philosopher and intellectual, former president of the [[Croatian Helsinki Committee]].

==Biography==
Puhovski was born in [[Zagreb]] on 15 December 1946. He was born to a [[Jews|Jewish]] mother although he has never been an active Jew.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jta.org/2002/05/21/lifestyle/croatian-paper-demands-jews-blast-israel |title=Croatian paper demands Jews blast Israel |author=Vlasta Kovač |date=21 May 2002 |work=jta.org |publisher=[[Jewish Telegraphic Agency]] |accessdate=7 January 2019}}</ref>

Puhovski received attention at an early age, when he became the president of his [[Gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]] as a member of the committee of the Alliance of Socialist Youth. He was expelled from the [[League of Communists of Croatia]] for a paper on sex and contraception, but was subsequently reinstated by [[Miko Tripalo]], the secretary of the City Committee of the League of Communists.<ref name="VL">{{cite web |title=Zarko Puhovski |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/enciklopedija/zarko-puhovski-18129 |website=Večernji list |date=12 January 2006}}</ref>

After studying [[physics]] for two years he headed to [[Germany]], but returned to Zagreb in 1968 enrolling at the Faculty of Political Sciences. In December 1969 he was appointed as the editor-in-chief of the ''Omladinski tjednik'' ("Youth weekly"), taking only 4 months to be discharged. The newspapers he edited were banned for insulting the President of the Republic.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}} He graduated in 1973, and became an assistant at the Institute of Philosophy of the [[University of Zagreb]]. Since 1975, he has been teaching political philosophy at the Faculty of Philosophy.<ref name="FFZG">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ffzg.unizg.hr/filoz/nastavnici/zarko-puhovski/|title=Filozofski fakultet u Zagrebu|website=ffzg.unizg.hr|publisher=Faculty of Philosophy, University of Zagreb}}</ref> As a professor he held guest lectures at the Universities of [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Berlin]], [[Johann Wolfgang Goethe University Frankfurt am Main|Frankfurt]], [[University of London|London]], [[University of Brighton|Brighton]], [[University of Klagenfurt|Klagenfurt]] and [[University of Valencia|Valencia]]. He is a member of The [[Ethikon Institute]] in [[Los Angeles]].<ref name="FFZG"/> He is the scientific director of the [[European University Center for Peace Studies]] in [[Stadtschlaining]], [[Austria]].<ref name="FFZG"/>

In 1971 he was a witness for the trial of Croatian student leaders [[Dražen Budiša]] and [[Ivan Zvonimir Čičak]].<ref name="VL" />

In 1988, he co-founded of the first alternative Yugoslav political organisation UJDI (''Udruženje za Jugoslavensku demokratsku inicijativu'', "[[Association for Yugoslav Democratic Initiative]]").<ref name="VL" />

He was an active member of the [[Croatian Helsinki Committee]] (HHO), since its inception in 1993, serving as its President from 2000 to 2007.<ref name="VL" />

He served as an editor in various periodicals: ''[[Ideje]]'' (1970–1973); ''[[Kulturni radnik]]'' (1971–1982); ''[[Praxis (magazine)|Praxis]]'' (1973–1975); ''[[Teka (magazine)|Teka]]'' (1975); ''[[Filozofska istraživanja]]'' (1980–1986). He translated numerous books and studies from [[German language|German]] and [[English language|English]], published about two hundred works in political philosophy, [[ethics]], philosophy of [[culture]], [[jurisprudence]] and [[social sciences]].<ref name="FFZG" />

He was awarded with European Club of Rectors Extraordinary Award for Peace and against Xenophobia 1993.

==Works==
Some of his major works include:<ref name="VL" />
* ''Interes i zajednica'' (1975)
* ''Kontekst kulture'' (1979)
* ''Povijest i revolucija'' (1980)
* ''Um i društvenost'' (1989)
* ''Socijalistička konstrukcija zbilje'' (1990)
* ''Leksikon temeljnih pojmova politike'' (1990)
* ''Politics and Economics of Transition'' (1993)

1383163602.title: Names of Georgia
1383163602.content:
{{Short description|Etymologies}}
{{for|the etymology of the US state|List of state and territory name etymologies of the United States}}
{{History of Georgia (country)}}
{{Georgians}}
'''Georgia''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=en-us-Georgia.ogg|ˈ|dʒ|ɔr|dʒ|ə}} {{respell|JOR|jə}}) is the [[Western world|Western]] [[exonym]] for [[Georgia (country)|the country]] in the [[Caucasus]] natively known as '''Sakartvelo''' ({{lang-ka|საქართველო}} {{IPA|ka|sakʰaɾtʰʷelo||Pronunciation audio-Georgia-KA.oga}}). The Armenian exonym is '''Vrastan''' ({{langx|hy|Վրաստան}} {{IPA|hy|vəɾɑsˈtɑn|}}); predominantly [[Islam|Muslim]] nations refer to it as '''Gurjistan''' or  its many similar variations; while in mostly [[Slavic languages|Slavic]] languages it is '''Gruziya''' and its derivatives.

The first mention of the name [[Spelling|spelled]] as "Georgia" was recorded in [[Italian language|Italian]] on the ''[[mappa mundi]]'' of [[Pietro Vesconte]] dated AD 1320.<ref>[[Rouben Galichian]] (2007) Countries South of the Caucasus in Medieval Maps: Armenia, Georgia and Azerbaijan. pp. 188—189</ref> In early appearances in the Latin world, the name was not always written in the same transliteration, the first consonant originally being spelt with ''J'', as '''Jorgia'''.<ref>Boeder; et al. (2002). Philology, typology and language structure. Peter Lang. p. 65. {{ISBN|978-0820459912}}</ref>

Both [[endonym and exonym]] for the country are derived from the same [[state formation|state-forming]] core and central Georgian region of [[Kartli]] ({{lang-ka|ქართლი}} {{IPA|ka|ˈkʰaɾtʰli||Kartli.ogg}}; known as [[Kingdom of Iberia|Iberia]] to the [[Classical antiquity|Classical]] and [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] sources) around which the early medieval cultural and political unity of the [[Georgians]] was formed.

All exonyms are likely derived from {{transliteration|fa|gorğān}} ({{wikt-lang|fa|گرگان}}), the [[Persian language|Persian]] designation of the Georgians, evolving from [[Parthian language|Parthian]] {{transliteration|xpr|wurğān}} ({{lang|xpr|[[wikt:𐭅𐭓𐭊𐭍|𐭅𐭓𐭊𐭍]]}}) and [[Middle Persian]] {{transliteration|pal|[[Sasanian Iberia|wiručān]]}} ({{wikt-lang|pal|𐭥𐭫𐭥𐭰𐭠𐭭}}), rooting out from [[Old Persian]] {{transliteration|peo|vrkān}} ({{wikt-lang|peo|𐎺𐎼𐎣𐎠𐎴}}) meaning "the land of the [[wolf|wolves]]". This is also reflected in [[Old Armenian]] {{transliteration|xcl|virk}} ({{wikt-lang|xcl|վիրք}}), it being a source of [[Ancient Greek]] {{transliteration|grc|ibēríā}} ({{wikt-lang|grc|Ἰβηρία}}), that entered [[Latin]] as {{wikt-lang|la|Hiberia}}. The transformation of {{transliteration|peo|vrkān}} into {{transliteration|fa|gorğān}} and alteration of '''''v''''' into '''''g''''' was a phonetic phenomenon in the [[word formation]] of [[Proto-Aryan]] and ancient [[Iranian languages]]. All exonyms are simply phonetic variations of the same root ''vrk/varka'' ({{wikt-lang|peo|𐎺𐎼𐎣}}) meaning [[wolf]].<ref>[[Elguja Khintibidze|Khintibidze, Elguja]] (1998), The Designations of the Georgians and Their Etymology, pp. 85-86-87, [[Tbilisi State University]] Press, {{ISBN|5-511-00775-7}}</ref>

The full, official name of the country is simply "Georgia", as specified in the [[Constitution of Georgia (country)|Georgian constitution]] which reads "''Georgia'' is the name of the state of Georgia."<ref>{{citation|chapter=Article 2.1|title=Constitution of Georgia|publisher=Legislative Herald of Georgia|chapter-url=https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/30346?publication=35|quote=‘Georgia’ is the name of the state of Georgia.}}</ref> Before the 1995 constitution came into force the country's name was the ''Republic of Georgia''. Since 2005<ref>Mikaberidze, Alexander (2015) Historical Dictionary of Georgia (2 ed.). p.4, Rowman & Littlefield, {{ISBN|978-1-4422-4146-6}}</ref> the [[Georgian Government]] has worked actively to remove the Russian-derived exonym ''Gruziya'' from usage around the world.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2015/04/15/national/politics-diplomacy/government-changing-official-pronunciation-georgia/#.VZL3n1J2yEm |title=Government changing official pronunciation of Georgia |newspaper=The Japan Times |date=April 15, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150418002238if_/http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2015/04/15/national/politics-diplomacy/government-changing-official-pronunciation-georgia/#.VTGj4ej7Q2w |archive-date=2015-04-18 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Endonym ==
[[File:Georgian passport.jpg|thumb|The front cover of a [[Georgian passport]] showing the [[official name]] of the country in [[Georgian language|Georgian]] as {{transliteration|ka|Sakartvelo}} and English as ''Georgia''.]]
The native Georgian name for the country is {{transliteration|ka|Sakartvelo}} ({{lang|ka|საქართველო}}). The word consists of two parts. Its root, {{transliteration|ka|kartvel-i}} ({{lang|ka|ქართველ-ი}}), first attested in the [[Old Georgian]] [[Umm Leisun inscription|inscription of Umm Leisun]] in [[Jerusalem]], originally referred to an inhabitant of the core central Georgian region of [[Kartli]] – [[Kingdom of Iberia (antiquity)|Iberia]] of the [[Classical antiquity|Classical]] and [[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] sources. By the early 9th century, the meaning of "Kartli" was expanded to other areas of medieval Georgia held together by religion, culture, and language. The Georgian [[circumfix]] ''sa''-X-''o'' is a standard geographic construction designating "the area where X dwell", where X is an [[ethnonym]].<ref name="Rapp">Rapp, Stephen H. (2003), ''Studies in Medieval Georgian Historiography: Early Texts And Eurasian Contexts'', pp. 419-423. Peeters Publishers, {{ISBN|90-429-1318-5}}</ref>

The earliest reference to "Sakartvelo" occurs in the {{circa|800}} [[Georgian Chronicles|Georgian chronicle]] by [[Juansher Juansheriani]].

{{Text and translation
|language=ka
|და ვითარცა შევლო ყრუმან კლისურა, რომელი მას ჟამსა იყო საზღვარი საბერძნეთისა და საქართველოსა, და შემუსრა ქალაქი აფშილეთისა ცხუმი. და მოადგა ციხესა ანაკოფისასა.
|And when that deaf man [i.e. ''[[Umayyad]] [[Caliph]]'' [[Marwan II]] (Georgians named him as "Marwan the Deaf" during his [[Marwan ibn Muhammad's invasion of Georgia|invasion of Georgia]])] destroyed Klisura, which was the border of ''[[Saberdzneti]]'' and '''''Sakartvelo''''', and he destroyed the city of [[Tskhumi]] of Apshileti, and came over the [[Anacopia Fortress]].<ref>Rapp, Stephen H. (2003) Corpus scriptorum christianorum orientalium: Subsidia, Studies in Medieval Georgian Historiography: Early Texts and Eurasian Contexts, Peeters Publishers, pp. 425-426</ref>
|Life of King of Kings [[Vakhtang Gorgasali]]}}

Within the next 200 years, this designation was reconfigured so that it came to signify the all-Georgian realm which came into existence with the political [[Unification of the Georgian realm|unification of Kartli and Apkhazeti]] under [[Bagrat III of Georgia|Bagrat III]] in 1008. However, it was not until the early 13th century that the term fully entered regular official usage.<ref name="Rapp"/>

The memory and dream of a united Georgia – Sakartvelo – persisted even after the political catastrophe of the 15th century when the [[Kingdom of Georgia]] [[Triarchy and collapse of the Kingdom of Georgia|fell apart]] to form three separate kingdoms: [[Kingdom of Kartli|Kartli]], [[Kingdom of Kakheti|Kakheti]], and [[Kingdom of Imereti|Imereti]], and five principalities: [[Samtskhe-Saatabago]], [[Principality of Mingrelia|Mingrelia]], [[Principality of Guria|Guria]], [[Principality of Svaneti|Svaneti]], and [[Principality of Abkhazia|Abkhazia]]. Thus, the later kings did not relinquish the titles of the all-Georgian monarchs whose legitimate successors they claimed to be. The idea of all-Georgian unity also dominated history-writing of the early 18th-century Georgian scholar and a member of the [[Bagrationi dynasty|royal family]], Prince [[Prince Vakhushti of Kartli|Vakhushti]], whose ''[[Description of the Kingdom of Georgia]]'' (''agtsera sameposa sakartvelosa'') had a noticeable influence on the latter-day conception of Sakartvelo. Although Georgia was politically divided among competing kingdoms and principalities during Vakhushti's lifetime, the scholar viewed the past and present of these breakaway polities as parts of the history of a single nation.<ref name="Rapp"/>

Georgia fell under successive [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]], [[Persian Empire|Iranian]] ([[Safavid Iran|Safavid]], [[Afsharid Iran|Afsharids]], [[Qajar dynasty|Qajars]]), and [[Russian Empire|Russian]] rule during the 15th to 19th centuries. It was re-united as the short-lived  [[Democratic Republic of Georgia]] ({{lang|ka|საქართველოს დემოკრატიული რესპუბლიკა}} {{transliteration|ka|sakartvelos demokratiuli respublika}}) on May 26, 1918, transformed into the [[Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic]] ({{lang|ka|საქართველოს საბჭოთა სოციალისტური რესპუბლიკა}} {{transliteration|ka|sakartvelos sabchota socialisturi respublika}}) in  1921, and eventually gaining independence as the Republic of Georgia ({{lang|ka|საქართველოს რესპუბლიკა}} {{transliteration|ka|sakartvelos respublika}}) on November 14, 1990. 
According to the 1995 [[Constitution of Georgia (country)|constitution]], the nation's official name is {{lang|ka|საქართველო}} {{transliteration|ka|sakartvelo}}.<ref name="const">[http://www.parliament.ge/files/68_1944_951190_CONSTIT_27_12.06.pdf Constitution of Georgia. Chapter 1. Article 1.3]. [[Parliament of Georgia]]. Retrieved on June 28, 2009</ref>

In other [[Kartvelian languages]], like [[Mingrelian language|Mingrelian]], Georgia is referred as {{lang|xmf|საქორთუო}} {{transliteration|xmf|sakortuo}}, in [[Laz language|Laz]] it's {{lang|lzz|ოქორთურა}} {{transliteration|lzz|okortura}}, when in [[Svan language|Svan]] it uses the same name as Georgian does, {{lang|sva|საქართველო}} {{transliteration|sva|sakartvelo}}. This same root is also adopted in [[Abkhaz language|Abkhaz]] and Georgia is referred as {{wikt-lang|ab|Қырҭтәыла}} {{transliteration|ab|Kyrţtwyla}} (i.e. Sakartvelo).

== Exonyms ==
{{multiple image
|align     = right
|direction = vertical
|image1    = Inscription Iviron on a stele.jpg

|image4    = Gorgania on Fra Mauro map.jpg

|width6    =

|caption6  = '''Iberia''' and '''Georgia''', detail from ''[[The Ambassadors (Holbein)|The Ambassadors]]'', painting of [[Hans Holbein the Younger]], 1533.
|image7    = Fedor chertezh.jpeg
|width7    = 
|alt7      =
|caption7  = "Map of Russia" commissioned by [[Feodor II of Russia]] and published by [[Hessel Gerritsz]] in [[Amsterdam]] mentions "Iveria sive '''Grusinæ''' Imperium" i.e. Iberia or the Empire of Georgia.
}}

===Iberia===
{{see also|Kingdom of Iberia (antiquity)|Hyrcania}}
One theory on the etymology of the name Iberia, proposed by [[Giorgi Melikishvili]], was that it was derived from the contemporary [[Armenian language|Armenian]] designation for Georgia, {{transliteration|hy|Virkʿ}} ({{lang|hy|Վիրք}}, and {{transliteration|hy|Ivirkʿ}} {{lang|hy|Իվիրք}} and {{transliteration|hy|Iverkʿ}} {{lang|hy|Իվերք}}), which itself was connected to the word Sver (or Svir), the [[Kartvelian languages|Kartvelian]] designation for Georgians.<ref name="SAE">{{in lang|hy}} [[Suren Yeremyan|Yeremyan, Suren T]]. ''«Իբերիա»'' (Iberia). [[Soviet Armenian Encyclopedia]]. vol. iv. Yerevan, Armenian SSR: [[Armenian Academy of Sciences]], 1978, p. 306.</ref> The letter "s" in this instance served as a prefix for the root word "Ver" (or "Vir"). Accordingly, in following [[Ivane Javakhishvili]]'s theory, the ethnic designation of "Sber", a variant of Sver, was derived the word "Hber" ("Hver") (and thus Iberia) and the Armenian variants, Veria and Viria.<ref name="SAE"/>

The [[Armenian language|Armenian]] name of Georgia is  {{wikt-lang|hy|Վրաստան}} {{transliteration|hy|Vrastan}}, {{wikt-lang|hy|Վիրք}} {{transliteration|hy|Virk}} (i.e. ''Iberia''). Ethnic [[Georgians]] are referred in Armenian as {{lang|hy|Վրացիներ}} ({{transliteration|hy|Vratsiner}}) literally meaning ''Iberians''.

===Georgia===
The European "Georgia" probably stems from the [[Persian language|Persian]] designation of the Georgians – {{transliteration|fa|gurğ}} ({{lang|fa|گرج}}), {{transliteration|fa|ğurğ}} – which reached the [[Western Europe]]an crusaders and pilgrims in the [[Holy Land]] who rendered the name as ''Georgia'' (also ''Jorgania'', ''Giorginia'', etc.) and, erroneously,<ref>[http://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/georgia-i GEORGIA i. The land and the people]</ref> explained its origin by the popularity of [[St. George]] ([[Tetri Giorgi]]) among the Georgians. This explanation is offered, among others, by [[Jacques de Vitry]] and Franz Ferdinand von Troilo.<ref>[[Grigol Peradze|Peradze, Gregory]]. "The Pilgrims' derivation of the name Georgia". ''Georgica'', Autumn, 1937, nos. 4 & 5, 208-209</ref> 
Another theory, popularized by the likes of [[Jean Chardin]], semantically linked "Georgia" to Greek {{lang|grc|γεωργός}} ("tiller of the land"). The supporters of this explanation sometimes referred to classical authors, in particular [[Pliny the Younger|Pliny]] and [[Pomponius Mela]]. The "Georgi" mentioned by these authors (Pliny, IV.26, VI.14; Mela, ''De Sita Orb''. i.2, & 50; ii.1, & 44, 102.) were merely agricultural tribes, so named to distinguish them from their unsettled and pastoral neighbors on the other side of the river [[Panticapaeum|Panticapea]] (in [[Taurica]]).<ref>Romer, Frank E.  (ed., 1998), ''Pomponius Mela's Description of the World'', p. 72. [[University of Michigan Press]], {{ISBN|0-472-08452-6}}</ref>
In the 19th century, [[Marie-Félicité Brosset]] favored the derivation of the name Georgia from that of the river [[Mtkvari]] via Kuros-Cyrus-Kura-Djurzan.<ref name="Allen-32">[[William Edward David Allen|Allen, William Edward David]] (1932), A History of the Georgian People: From the Beginning Down to the Russian Conquest in the Nineteenth Century, p. 369. Taylor & Francis, {{ISBN|0-7100-6959-6}}</ref>

According to several modern scholars, "Georgia" seems to have been borrowed in the 11th or 12th century from the [[Syriac language|Syriac]] {{transliteration|syr|gurz-ān}}/{{transliteration|syr|gurz-iyān}} and [[Arabic language|Arabic]] {{transliteration|ar|ĵurĵan}}/{{transliteration|ar|ĵurzan}}, derived from the [[New Persian]] {{transliteration|fa|gurğ}}/{{transliteration|fa|gurğān}}, itself stemming from the [[Middle Persian]] {{transliteration|pal|[[Sasanian Iberia|waručān]]}} of unclear origin, but resembling the eastern trans-[[Caspian Sea|Caspian]] toponym [[Gorgan]], which comes from the [[Old Persian]] {{transliteration|peo|varkâna-}}, "land of the wolves". This might have been of the same etymology as the [[Old Armenian|Armenian]] {{transliteration|hy|Virk'}} ({{lang|hy|Վիրք}}) and a source of the Greco-Roman rendition {{lang|la|Iberi}} ({{lang|grc|Ἴβηρες}}), the ethnonym already known to them as a designation of the [[Iberians|Iberian peoples]] of the [[Iberian Peninsula]].<ref>[[David Marshall Lang|Lang, David Marshall]] (1966), ''The Georgians'', pp. 5-6. Praeger Publishers</ref><ref>Khintibidze, Elguja (1998), ''The Designations of the Georgians and Their Etymology'', pp. 29-30. [[Tbilisi State University]] Press, {{ISBN|5-511-00775-7}} ([http://www.kartvfund.org.ge/anewtheory.htm A New Theory on the Etymology of the Designations of the Georgians (Excerpt from the book)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930020807/http://www.kartvfund.org.ge/anewtheory.htm |date=2007-09-30 }}) ([https://web.archive.org/web/20161230094932/http://kartvfund.org.ge/index.php?act=page&id=33.58&lang=en Google Cache])</ref>

===Gruziya===
The [[Russian language|Russian]] exonym Gruziya ({{lang-rus|Грузия|p=ˈɡruzʲɪjə|a=Ka-Gruziya.oga}}) is also of Persian origin, from [[Persian language|Persian]] {{wikt-lang|fa|گرجستان}} {{transliteration|fa|Gorjestân}} (Turkish {{wikt-lang|tr|Gürcistan}}, [[Ossetian language|Ossetian]]: {{wikt-lang|os|Гуырдзыстон}} {{transliteration|os|Gwyrdzyston}}, Mongolian {{wikt-lang|mn|Гүрж}} {{transliteration|mn|Gürj}}).

The Russian name first occurs in the travel records of [[Ignaty Smolnyanin]] as {{transliteration|ru|gurzi}} ({{lang|ru|гурзи}}) (1389).

{{Text and translation
|language=ru|
А въ церковь ту влѣзщи, ино направѣ '''Гурзійскаа''' служба, '''Гурзіи''' служатъ.
|There is a church and there is a  '''''Gurz''''' [i.e. Georgian] [[liturgy]], '''''Gurzis''''' [i.e. Georgians] serve there.
|Travels in Jerusalem}}

[[Afanasy Nikitin]] calls Georgia as {{transliteration|ru|gurzynskaya zemlya}} ({{lang|ru|Гурзыньская земля}}, "Gurzin land") (1466–72).<ref>{{in lang|ru}} [[Max Vasmer|Vesmer, MAx]] (trans. [[Oleg Trubachyov|Trubachyov, Oleg]], 1987),  «Этимологический словарь русского языка» (''Etymological Dictionary of the Russian Language''), vol. 1, p. 464. Progress: Moscow ([http://starling.rinet.ru/cgi-bin/response.cgi?basename=%5Cusr%5Clocal%5Cshare%5Cstarling%5Cmorpho%5Cvasmer%5Cvasmer&first=3021&morpho=1&root=/usr/local/share/starling/morpho Online version])</ref>

{{Text and translation
|language=ru|Да Севастѣи губѣ, да '''Гурзынской земли''' добро обилію всѣм; да Торская земля обилна.
|And in Sevastia, and in the '''''Gurzin land''''' [i.e. Georgian land] everything is in abundance, and Torsk land [i.e. Turkish land] is abundant.
|[[A Journey Beyond the Three Seas]]}}

As a result of permutation of sounds "Gurz" transformed into "Gruz" and eventually "Gruz-iya". The Russian name was brought into several [[Slavic languages]] (Belarusian, Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Macedonian, Polish, Serbian, Slovak, Slovenian, Ukrainian) as well as other languages historically in contact with the [[Russian Empire]] and/or the [[Soviet Union]] (such as Latvian, Lithuanian, Estonian, Hungarian, Yiddish, Kyrgyz, Turkmen, Uyghur, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese).<ref name="civil270611">{{Cite web|url=http://civil.ge/eng/article.php?id=23673|title=Tbilisi Wants to Be Referred as 'Georgia' Not 'Gruzya'|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200216151904/https://old.civil.ge/eng/article.php?id=23673|archive-date=2020-02-16|website=Civil Georgia|date=June 27, 2011}}</ref>

====Abandoning the name====
In August 2005, the Georgian ambassador to Israel [[Lasha Zhvania]] asked that the Hebrew speakers refer to his country as {{transliteration|he|Georgia}} {{lang|he|{{Script/Hebrew|גאורגיה}}}} and abandon the name {{transliteration|he|Gruzia}}. The name entered the contemporary [[Hebrew]] as {{lang|he|{{Script/Hebrew|גרוזיה}}}} ({{transliteration|he|Gruz-ia}}). It coexisted with the names {{lang|he|{{Script/Hebrew|גאורגיה}}}} ({{transliteration|he|Gheorghia}} with two hard ''g'''s) and {{lang|he|{{Script/Hebrew|גורג'יה}}}} ({{transliteration|he|Gurjia}}), when {{transliteration|he|Gruzia}} took over in the 1970s, probably due to a [[Aliyah|massive immigration]] of bilingual Georgian-Russian Jews to Israel at that time. Georgia's request was approved and now Israel refers to the country as {{transliteration|he|Gheorghia}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/hasen/pages/ShArt.jhtml?itemNo=610079 |title=Georgia on his mind: Republic's ambassador demands Hebrew name change|publisher=Haaretz.com|date=2005-08-08|access-date=2009-06-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022110634/http://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/news/georgia-on-his-mind-republic-s-ambassador-demands-hebrew-name-change-1.166281|archive-date=2012-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=여러 나라에서 자연재해 |url=http://www.rodong.rep.kp/ko/index.php?OEAyMDI0LTA2LTExLU4wMjlAMkBAQDFAMjk= |work=[[Rodong Sinmun]]}}</ref>

In June 2011, the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Georgia)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia]] said [[South Korea]] had agreed to refer to the country as {{lang|ko|조지아}} ({{transliteration|ko|Jojia}}) instead of the Russian-influenced {{lang|ko|그루지야}} ({{transliteration|ko|Geurujiya}}) and the government of Georgia was continuing talks with other countries on the issue. Although [[North Korea]] still uses {{lang|ko|그루지야}} as of 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=About us |url=http://mfa.gov.kp/article/page/about-us |website=[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (North Korea)]] |access-date=29 June 2024 |language=Korean}}</ref>

In April 2015, Japan changed the official Japanese name for Georgia from {{nihongo||グルジア|Gurujia}}, which derives from the Russian term {{transliteration|ru|Gruziya}}, to {{nihongo||ジョージア|Jōjia}}, which derives from the English term "Georgia".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/press/release/press4_002048.html|script-title=ja:国名呼称の変更（グルジア）|work=Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan|date=22 April 2015|language=ja|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829151146/https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/press/release/press4_002048.html|archive-date=29 August 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

In May 2018, Lithuania switched to {{lang|lt|Sakartvelas}}, which is derived from Georgia's original native name {{transliteration|ka|Sakartvelo}}. The new name would be an alternative for Georgia alongside the long-established {{lang|lt|Gruzija}}.<ref>[http://www.eurasianet.org/node/85301 Lithuania Moves to Stop Calling Georgia by its Russian Name]</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lithuania Adopts Sakartvelas as Alternative Name for Georgia |url=https://civil.ge/archives/240537 |access-date=23 July 2018 |work=Civil Georgia |date=3 May 2018}}</ref> Georgia had initially asked for a change in December 2009 to be called {{lang|lt|Georgija}} instead of {{lang|lt|Gruzija}}; the request was forwarded to the [[Commission of the Lithuanian Language]] and was declined at that time.<ref>Jackevičius, M. [https://www.delfi.lt/news/daily/lithuania/gruzija-nori-buti-vadinama-georgija.d?id=26304293 Gruzija nori būti vadinama "Georgija"]</ref> In 2010, then-[[Minister of Foreign Affairs of Georgia]] [[Grigol Vashadze]] during his official visit to Lithuania promised to "destroy the name Gruziya" and asked the Lithuanian authorities for a name switch.<ref>[https://lenta.ru/news/2010/05/19/gruzia/ "Георгийский" министр пообещал уничтожить "Грузию"] Lenta</ref> Lithuanian authorities made the switch for [[Independence Day of Georgia]] and described it as a "great gift to the Georgian people" when Georgia celebrated the 100th anniversary of the declaration of independence of the [[First Republic of Georgia]].<ref>[https://www.rferl.org/a/lithuania-moves-change-official-name-goeriga-sakartvelo-from-russian-name-gruzia/28759383.html Lithuania Moves To Change Official Name For Georgia To Sakartvelo From Gruzia]</ref> As a gesture of appreciation, Georgia also changed Lithuania's Russian-derived name of {{transliteration|ka|Litva}} ({{langx|ru|Литва}}) to its native {{transliteration|ka|Lietuva}}.<ref>Samantha Guthrie [http://georgiatoday.ge/news/10448/Lithuania-Gets-a-New-Name-in-Georgian Lithuania Gets a New Name in Georgian] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121215031/http://georgiatoday.ge/news/10448/Lithuania-Gets-a-New-Name-in-Georgian |date=2021-01-21 }} ''Georgia Today'', 25 May  2018</ref> Accordingly, the Embassy of Georgia in Lithuania changed its name from {{lang|lt|Gruzijos Ambasada}} to {{lang|lt|Sakartvelo Ambasada}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://1tv.ge/en/news/authentic-name-georgia-sakartvelas-officially-used-lithuanian-language/ |title=Authentic name of Georgia 'Sakartvelas' to be officially used in Lithuanian Language|date=May 3, 2018|work=Georgia First Channel|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201121143718/https://1tv.ge/en/news/authentic-name-georgia-sakartvelas-officially-used-lithuanian-language/|archive-date=21 November 2020}}</ref> However, as of 2019, the traditional name {{lang|lt|Gruzija}} was still more popular than the new name in media and on social networks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/1089256/sakartvelo-catching-on-georgia-s-historic-name-growing-in-popularity-in-lithuania|title=Sakartvelo catching on – Georgia's historic name growing in popularity in Lithuania |work=LRT|date=19 August 2019}}</ref> On December 21, 2020, the State Commission of the Lithuanian Language (VLKK) decided that the name {{lang|lt|Sakartvelas}} should be used in all official Lithuanian-language documents.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/1317371/lithuania-approves-sakartvelo-as-official-name-for-georgia|title= Lithuania approves Sakartvelo as official name for Georgia|date=11 January 2021|work=LRT English}}</ref>

In June 2019, during the [[2019 Georgian protests]], former Ukrainian president [[Petro Poroshenko]] called upon the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine]] to change {{transliteration|uk|Gruziya}} to {{transliteration|uk|Sakartvelo}}.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-06-24 |title=Порошенко закликає МЗС України "перейменувати" Грузію на Сакартвело |url=https://www.ukrinform.ua/rubric-polytics/2727263-porosenko-zaklikae-mzs-ukraini-perejmenuvati-gruziu-na-sakartvelo.html |access-date=2023-12-16 |website=www.ukrinform.ua |language=uk}}</ref>

'''Omid Alishah''' ({{langx|fa|امید عالیشاه}}; born 10 January 1992) is an Iranian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Persian Gulf Pro League]] club [[Gol Gohar Sirjan F.C.|Gol Gohar]]. He is one of the most successful player in Persepolis's history, having won five league titles, two Hazfi Cups, and three Super Cups with the team.

He signed a two-year contract with [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] on 11 June 2013 and debuted on 16 August 2013. On 23 November 2014, Alishah scored the winning goal in the [[Tehran derby]] against rival [[Esteghlal F.C.|Esteghlal]] in the 78th minute. has also played for [[F.C. Nassaji Mazandaran|Nassaji Mazandaran]], [[Naft Tehran F.C.|Naft Tehran]], [[Rah Ahan Tehran F.C.|Rah Ahan]] and [[Tractor S.C.|Tractor]]. Also, He was the [[2015–16 Persian Gulf Pro League|2015–16 PGL Top Goal Assistant]].

==Club career==

===Nassaji===

Alishah started his career at [[Nassaji Mazandaran F.C.|Nassaji]] when he was 17.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.persianleague.com/teams.html?sid=20&view=player&id=1589 |title=Persianleague.com |access-date=2013-04-02 |archive-date=2016-10-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161001160904/http://www.persianleague.com/teams.html?sid=20&view=player&id=1589 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He debuted for the club on January 7, 2010, against [[Shirin Faraz F.C.|Shirin Faraz]] when he was chosen as a starter by the coach [[Nader Dastneshan]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.abrarnews.com/sport/1388/881019/html/page11.htm#s541653 |title=Abrarnews.com |access-date=2013-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130406231941/http://abrarnews.com/sport/1388/881019/html/page11.htm#s541653 |archive-date=2013-04-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Naft Tehran===

In the 2010–11 season, Alishah joined the newly promoted IPL team [[Naft Tehran F.C.|Naft Tehran]].<ref>[http://www.goal.com/iran/news/1825/%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86/2010/07/21/2034628/%DA%AF%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B4-%DA%A9%D8%A7%D9%85%D9%84-%DA%AF%D9%84-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D9%86%D9%82%D9%84-%D9%88-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AA%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%84%D9%8A%DA%AF-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%B1 Goal.com]</ref> During his time at Naft, he failed to make any appearances for the first team. He was also a part of [[Naft Tehran F.C.|Naft Tehran U-21]] and won the [[Tehran Football Competitions|2010–11 Tehran U–21 League]].<ref>[http://www.footballtehran.com/id/269 Footballtehran.com]</ref><ref>[http://www.nioc.ir/portal/Home/ShowPage.aspx?Object=NEWS&ID=12205543-7203-4f4a-9ce3-acef196cbbdb&LayoutID=d56819c3-861b-4f26-a4af-36684d521883&CategoryID=40295507-1e70-49ec-af82-e5eeba6870bc Nioc.ir]</ref>

===Rah Ahan===
After a season at Naft, Alishah was signed up by [[Ali Daei]] for [[Rah Ahan F.C.|Rah Ahan]].<ref>[https://www.asriran.com/fa/news/175100 Asriran.com]</ref> Ali Daei moved him up the field and into a more attacking position using Alishah as a right winger/second striker instead of right back where he had been used by his previous managers. Alishah, with his blistering pace, quickly managed to find his way into the starting line-up scoring five goals in his first nine games. He had a less successful second half of the season mainly due to a [[Cruciate ligament]] injury in a match against [[S.C. Damash|Damash Gilan]] in March 2012.<ref>[https://www.mashreghnews.ir/fa/news/107331 Mashreghnews.ir]</ref> He had been far from the team till December 2012.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130412235839/http://sorinetsport.ir/Default.aspx?cat=news&g=912|title=Sorinetsport.ir}}</ref>

===Persepolis===
[[File:Omid Alishah Persepolis VS Foolad.jpg|thumb|Alishah (in red) playing for [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] against [[Foolad F.C.|Foolad]] in 2018]]
He signed a two-year contract with [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] on 11 June 2013.<ref>{{cite web
 |title       = Official: Omid Alishah joins Persepolis
 |url         = http://www1.fc-perspolis.com/news_content/main/newsId:10971
 |url-status     = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20130921054737/http://www1.fc-perspolis.com/news_content/main/newsId%3A10971
 |archivedate = 2013-09-21
}}</ref> He made his debut on 16 August 2013 in a match against [[Malavan F.C.|Malavan]], in which he scored the winning goal. He scored his second goal on 6 April 2014 in a 2–2 draw against his former team, [[Rah Ahan F.C.|Rah Ahan]]. On 23 November 2014, Alishah scored the winning goal in the [[Tehran derby]] against rival [[Esteghlal F.C.|Esteghlal]] in the 78th minute. He was sent off after receiving his second yellow card seconds after his goal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-11-24 |title=Reds Win Action-Packed Tehran Derby |url=https://financialtribune.com/articles/art-and-culture/5363/reds-win-action-packed-tehran-derby |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=Financial Tribune |language=En}}</ref>

In 2015, before the 2015–16 season, Alishah was designated as Persepolis' third captain.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-05-05 |title=این شما و این کاپیتان سوم پرسپولیس |url=https://footballi.net/news/r/350767/این-شما-و-این-کاپیتان-سوم-پرسپولیس |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=فوتبالی |language=fa}}</ref> Also, he was the [[2015–16 Persian Gulf Pro League|2015–16 PGL Top Goal Assistant]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=رده بندی بهترین پاسورهای لیگ پانزدهم |url=https://www.varzesh3.com/news/1324873 |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=ورزش سه |language=fa}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=عالیشاه بهترین پاسور لیگ و پرسپولیس |url=https://www.varzesh3.com/news/1325693 |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=ورزش سه |language=fa}}</ref>

From the 2022 season, he became the team's first captain.<ref>{{Cite web |title=بازوبند کاپیتانی پرسپولیس به چه کسی می‌رسد؟ |url=https://www.jamaran.news/بخش-%D9%88%D8%B1%D8%B2%D8%B4%DB%8C-160/1557925-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%88%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%AF-%DA%A9%D8%A7%D9%BE%DB%8C%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86%DB%8C-%D9%BE%D8%B1%D8%B3%D9%BE%D9%88%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%B3-%D8%A8%D9%87-%DA%86%D9%87-%DA%A9%D8%B3%DB%8C-%D9%85%DB%8C-%D8%B1%D8%B3%D8%AF |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=پایگاه خبری جماران |language=fa}}</ref>

In 2025, Alishah became Persepolis's all-time record appearance. He surpassed Ali Parvin's record by playing his 280th match for the team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=بازوبند کاپیتانیAlishah becomes Persepolis’s all-time record appearance holder
 |url=https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/509921/Alishah-becomes-Persepolis-s-all-time-record-appearance-holder |access-date=2025-02-19|website=تهران تایمز |language=fa}}</ref>

=== Tractor ===
In the winter of 2017, Alishah signed a two–year contract with [[Tractor S.C.|Tractor]] to spend his [[Conscription in Iran|conscription]] period at the club. Alishah returned to Persepolis before [[2018–19 Persian Gulf Pro League|2018-19]] league.<ref>{{Cite web |title=عالیشاه تسویه حساب گرفت و به پرسپولیس بازگشت + تصویر نامه- اخبار ورزشی تسنیم {{!}} Tasnim |url=https://www.tasnimnews.com/fa/news/1397/01/29/1703608 |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=خبرگزاری تسنیم {{!}} Tasnim |language=fa}}</ref>

=== Gol Gohar ===

In the summer of 2026, he joined [[Gol Gohar Sirjan F.C.|Gol Gohar Sirjan]] from Persepolis on a permanent transfer.

==International career==

===U–17===
Alishah represented [[Iran national under-17 football team|Iran U-17]] in the 3 of the four games the team played at the [[2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20091123034530/http://www.fifa.com/mm/document/tournament/competition/01/11/93/31/fu17_2009_squadlists.pdf Fifa.com]</ref>

===U–20===
He also made the squad for the unsuccessful [[2010 AFC U-19 Championship]]. Surprisingly, his involvement was highly limited under the guidance of his former U17 manager, [[Ali Doustimehr]].<ref>[http://www.varzesh3.com/news.do?itemid=27655&title=%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85_%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%85%D9%8A_%D8%AA%D9%8A%D9%85_%D9%85%D9%84%D9%8A_%D8%AC%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%86 Varzesh3.com]</ref>

===U-22===
He was invited to [[Iran national under-23 football team|Iran U-22]] by the coach [[Alireza Mansourian]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ffiri.ir/news/detail/%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B5%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%A7%D9%86-20-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%DB%8C%DA%A9%D9%86-%D8%B1%D8%A7-%D8%AF%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AA-%DA%A9%D8%B1%D8%AF/102147/news.aspx |title=Ffiri.ir |access-date=2020-04-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403130213/http://ffiri.ir/news/detail/%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B5%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%A7%D9%86-20-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%DB%8C%DA%A9%D9%86-%D8%B1%D8%A7-%D8%AF%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AA-%DA%A9%D8%B1%D8%AF/102147/news.aspx |archive-date=2015-04-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his debut against [[Qatar national under-23 football team|Qatar U-22]] and scored his first goal at the match.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ffiri.ir/national-football-team/player/%D8%A7%D9%85%DB%8C%D8%AF-%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%B4%D8%A7%D9%87/57edca5d-ac39-40d3-85ce-b4d3d3e72838/NationalTeamUnder22/detail.aspx |title=Ffiri.ir |access-date=2013-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925132521/http://www.ffiri.ir/national-football-team/player/%D8%A7%D9%85%DB%8C%D8%AF-%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%B4%D8%A7%D9%87/57edca5d-ac39-40d3-85ce-b4d3d3e72838/NationalTeamUnder22/detail.aspx |archive-date=2017-09-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Senior===

He made his debut against [[Guam national football team|Guam]] on 3 September 2015 in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualifying]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=مقدماتی جام جهانی ۲۰۱۸؛ ایران مهمان خود را گلباران کرد |url=https://www.radiofarda.com/a/f8-football/27225150.html |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=رادیو فردا |language=fa}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-08-25 |title=دعوت از ۲۳ بازیکن برای دو بازی تیم ملی ایران با گوام و هند |url=https://www.bbc.com/persian/sport/2015/08/150825_l56_iran_team_meli_call_up_gauam_india |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=BBC News فارسی |language=fa}}</ref>

== Style of play ==
[[File:Persepolis F.C. v Zob Ahan Esfahan F.C., 7 August 2020 File (15).jpg|thumb|Alishah (in red) playing for [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] against [[Zob Ahan Esfahan F.C.|Zob Ahan]] in 2020]]
Alishah has been a goal maker for the team with his high speed and scoring power.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ترکیب پرسپوليس مقابل آلومینیوم مشخص شد |url=https://www.varzesh3.com/news/1818971 |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=ورزش سه |language=fa}}</ref> He has been considered to be highly capable in all attacking positions.

== Personal life ==
As a child, he experienced [[Sport of athletics|athletics]], [[handball]], [[futsal]], and [[association football|football]]. His first professional football experience was related to Iran's under-11 national football team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-11-24 |title=امید عالیشاه از زندگی شخصی اش می گوید!/فوتبالیستی که از پدرش پول تو جیبی می گیرد!! |url=https://persianv.com/maharat/امید-عالیشاه-از-زندگی-شخصی-اش-می-گویدف.html |access-date=2022-08-06 |website=مهارت های زندگی |language=fa-IR}}</ref>

On 30 January 2026, Alishah responded to the high casualty rate of the [[2025–2026 Iranian protests]] on his [[Instagram]], saying: "Our every fiber of our being was filled with pain, wounds, and sadness. Wounds for the truths that we do not have the light of, and sadness for the loss of our beautiful youth. Condolences to the homeland, condolences to us."<ref>{{Cite web | title=امید عالیشاه، کاپیتان پرسپولیس؛ بند بند وجودمان از درد و زخم و ملال پر شد، تسلیت به وطن {{!}} Iran International | url=https://www.iranintl.com/202601304351 | access-date=2026-10-08 | website=www.iranintl.com}}</ref> On 9 February 2026, he publicly objected to being included on a list of supporters of the [[Iranian Revolution|1979 Islamic Revolution]] by the [[Ministry of Sport and Youth (Iran)|Ministry of Sport and Youth]], ahead of the Revolution's anniversary.<ref>{{Cite web | title=اعتراض ورزشکاران به سوءاستفاده از نامشان در بیانیه وزارت ورزش در حمایت از جمهوری اسلامی {{!}} Iran International | url=https://www.iranintl.com/202602090161 | access-date=2026-10-08 | website=www.iranintl.com}}</ref>
