'''Domenico Berardi''' {{postnominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|Cavaliere OMRI]]}} ({{IPA|it|doˈmeːniko beˈrardi}};<ref>See [http://www.dizionario.rai.it/poplemma.aspx?lid=64628&r=6375 Domenico] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200704052933/http://www.dizionario.rai.it/poplemma.aspx?lid=64628&r=6375 |date=4 July 2020 }} and [http://www.dizionario.rai.it/poplemma.aspx?lid=78654&r=26573 Berardi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703084627/http://www.dizionario.rai.it/poplemma.aspx?lid=78654&r=26573 |date=3 July 2020 }} in ''Dizionario d'ortografia e di pronunzia''</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dipionline.it/dizionario/ricerca?lemma=Berardi|title=Berardi|work=DiPI Online|first=Luciano |last=Canepari|access-date=8 August 2019|language=it}}</ref> born 1 August 1994) is an Italian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] or [[right winger]] for {{Italian football updater|Sassuolo}} club [[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Domenico Berardi Positions|url=https://www.footballcritic.com|website=Footballcritic|access-date=18 October 2023}}</ref> 

Berardi began his club career with Sassuolo during the [[2012–13 Serie B]] season, helping the team win the title and earn promotion to Serie A, being named the best player of the competition. His prolific performances in Serie A saw him emerge as one of Italy's most promising young footballers, and earned him the [[Bravo Award]] in 2015. He is Sassuolo's all-time top scorer, with over 150 goals in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/022d-0e94703b9c2e-f33fc15bce1d-1000--ten-claims-to-fame-sassuolo/|title=Ten claims to fame: Sassuolo|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=25 May 2016|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref>

Berardi made his senior international debut with Italy in 2018, and was a member of the squad that won [[UEFA Euro 2020]].

==Club career==

===Sassuolo===

====Youth career====
Born in [[Cariati]], [[Calabria]], Berardi joined the youth academy of [[Cosenza Calcio 1914 (2008)|Cosenza]] at the age of 13, before moving to [[U.S. Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]] at the age of 16.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calcioweb.eu/2013/05/la-meglio-gioventu-domenico-berardi/58801/|title=La Meglio Gioventu' – Domenico Berardi|publisher=CalcioWeb|first=Marco |last=Giordano|date=14 May 2013|access-date=8 September 2013|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/it/news/3785/generazione-di-fenomeni/2013/04/03/3872414/generazione-di-fenomeni-domenico-berardi-il-van-persie-della|title=Generazione di Fenomeni – Domenico Berardi, il 'Van Persie della Sila' che piace a Juventus, Napoli, Inter... e Manchester Utd|website=Goal.com|first=Paolo |last=Camedda|date=3 August 2013|access-date=8 September 2013|language=it}}</ref>

====2012–13 season====
He made his senior debut for Sassuolo in [[Serie B]] on 27 August 2012, at the age of 18, in a 3–0 away win over [[A.C. Cesena|Cesena]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2012/08/27/italy/serie-b/ac-cesena/us-sassuolo-calcio/1356701/|title=Cesena vs. Sassuolo 0 - 3|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> and scored his first professional goal five days later, in a 2–1 home win over [[F.C. Crotone|Crotone]].<ref name="SW"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2012/09/01/italy/serie-b/us-sassuolo-calcio/fc-crotone/1356719/|title=Sassuolo vs. Crotone 2 - 1|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> In 2013, he was named Best Player of the [[2012–13 Serie B|Serie B]] in the past season in the annual Gran Galà del calcio awards, after helping Sassuolo win the Serie B title, and a historic promotion to Serie A, scoring 11 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2014/01/gran-gala-del-calcio-2013-winners/ |title=Gran Gala del Calcio 2013 – Winners |date=27 January 2014 |publisher=Forza Italian Football |access-date=2 October 2016}}</ref> In June 2013, he was described as the "undoubted star of the [Sassuolo] side."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wsc.co.uk/wsc-daily/1163-june-2013/9921-sassuolo-become-smallest-town-to-reach-serie-a|title=Sassuolo become smallest town to reach Serie A|date=16 June 2013|access-date=2 September 2013|first=Scott |last=Johnson|publisher=When Saturday Comes|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140113001504/http://www.wsc.co.uk/wsc-daily/1163-june-2013/9921-sassuolo-become-smallest-town-to-reach-serie-a|archive-date=13 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2013–14 season====
On 2 September 2013, [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] confirmed via their official website that Berardi had joined the club on a co-ownership basis that saw [[Luca Marrone]] transfer in the opposite direction, both for a fee of €4.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/en/news/news/2013/juventus-complete-double-transfer-deal-with-sassuolo.php|title=Juventus complete double transfer deal with Sassuolo|publisher=Juventus.com|date=2 September 2013|access-date=1 August 2015|archive-date=21 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421083123/https://www.juventus.com/en/news/news/2013/juventus-complete-double-transfer-deal-with-sassuolo.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> Berardi remained with Sassuolo on a season-long loan deal for the [[2013–14 Serie A|2013–14]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/9ede98f4-3dec-4ec7-acb3-74b3cae17727/comunicato+02092013+accordi+con+sassuolo+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=9ede98f4-3dec-4ec7-acb3-74b3cae17727|title=Agreements with Sassuolo Calcio|date=2 September 2013|access-date=21 May 2015|publisher=Juventus FC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626113123/http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/9ede98f4-3dec-4ec7-acb3-74b3cae17727/comunicato+02092013+accordi+con+sassuolo+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=9ede98f4-3dec-4ec7-acb3-74b3cae17727|archive-date=26 June 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/juve/en/news/juventus_sassuolo_marrone_berardi|title=Juventus complete double transfer deal with Sassuolo|date=2 September 2013|access-date=2 September 2013|publisher=Juventus F.C. |last1=f. c. |first1=Juventus }}</ref> He made his [[Serie A]] debut at the age of 19, in a 1–1 away draw against [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]], on 25 September 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/09/25/italy/serie-a/ssc-napoli/us-sassuolo-calcio/1551923/|title=Napoli vs. Sassuolo 1 - 1|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> He scored his first Serie A goal from a penalty on 6 October 2013, in a 3–1 defeat to [[Parma F.C.|Parma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2013-2014/parma-sassuolo_mtc646445/live.shtml|title=Parma - Sassuolo (3 - 1)|publisher=Eurosport|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> On 20 October, he scored a penalty as Sassuolo defeated [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] 2–1 for their first Serie A win, moving them off bottom spot.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sassuolo 2–1 Bologna: Neroverdi Leapfrog Rossublu After Home Win|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2013/10/sassuolo-2-1-bologna-neroverdi-leapfrog-rossublu-after-home-win/|access-date=30 May 2014|newspaper=Forza Italian Football|date=20 October 2013}}</ref> He scored a hat-trick, including two penalties, in Sassuolo's first ever Serie A away win, 4–3 against [[Sampdoria]] on 3 November 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Berardi treble boosts Sassuolo|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/299284/report|access-date=30 May 2014|newspaper=[[Sky Sports News]]|date=3 November 2013}}</ref>

On 12 January 2014, Berardi scored all four goals in a 4–3 home win against [[A.C. Milan|AC Milan]]. In doing so, he became the second youngest player to score four goals in a single [[Serie A]] match – the youngest was the 18-year-old [[Silvio Piola]] in 1931 – and the first player to score four in a league match against Milan.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/119313/sassuolo-vs-ac-milan/report |title=Sassuolo 4–3 AC Milan: History-maker Berardi leaves Rossoneri red-faced |date=12 January 2014 |access-date=28 May 2014 |publisher=Goal.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/jan/13/domenico-berardi-milan-sassuolo-allegri-serie-a |title=Domenico Berardi's awesome foursome sinks Milan ... and Massimiliano Allegri |first=Nicky |last=Bandini |work=theguardian.com |date=13 January 2014 |access-date=28 May 2014}}</ref> On 6 May 2014, Berardi scored a first-half hat-trick in 4–3 away win at [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/us/en/report/376957/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901|title=Berardi hits treble in Sassuolo win|date=6 May 2014|access-date=6 May 2014|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/5/6/5687510/fiorentina-sassuolo-serie-a-2014-final-score-result|title=Fiorentina vs Sassuolo, final score 3–4: Berardi treble boosts Sassuolo's survival hopes|date=6 May 2014|access-date=6 May 2014|first=Shaun |last=Best|website=sbnation.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 16 goals in 29 games in the league as Sassuolo avoided relegation.<ref name="SW"/>

====2014–15 season====
In July 2014, Berardi's agent confirmed that he would remain on loan at Sassuolo for another season;<ref>{{Cite web|date=3 July 2014|title=Berardi to stay at Sassuolo|url=http://www.football-italia.net/51546/%E2%80%98berardi-stay-sassuolo%E2%80%99|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140707040219/https://football-italia.net/51546/%E2%80%98berardi-stay-sassuolo%E2%80%99|archive-date=7 July 2014|access-date=19 July 2021|website=Football Italia}}</ref> the [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership deal]] was also renewed on 20 June 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/706f4af4-9b1b-45f2-b6d6-3a410c8c240f/comunicato+20062014+accordi+sassuolo+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=706f4af4-9b1b-45f2-b6d6-3a410c8c240f|title=Agreements with Sassuolo Calcio|date=20 June 2014|access-date=21 May 2015|publisher=Juventus FC|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030184654/http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/706f4af4-9b1b-45f2-b6d6-3a410c8c240f/comunicato+20062014+accordi+sassuolo+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=706f4af4-9b1b-45f2-b6d6-3a410c8c240f|archive-date=30 October 2014}}</ref>

On 17 May 2015, he scored a hat-trick at the [[Mapei Stadium – Città del Tricolore|Mapei Stadium]] in a 3–2 win over Milan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sassuolo beat Milan amid Domenico Berardi ghost goal controversy|url=http://www.espnfc.us/italian-serie-a/match/403478/sassuolo-ac-milan/report|publisher=ESPN FC|access-date=18 May 2015|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> He finished the [[2014–15 Serie A]] season with 15 goals and 10 assists, and was one of the top assist providers in the league.<ref>{{cite web|title=Serie A 2014-15 Statistics: Assists|url=http://www.espnfc.com/italian-serie-a/12/statistics/assists|publisher=ESPN FC|access-date=1 June 2015}}</ref> He reached 30 league goals in 59 games, noted by [[UEFA]] to be quicker than the 70 matches taken for [[Lionel Messi]] to reach that milestone;<ref name=Sweden/> at the age of 20, he also became the youngest player to reach 30 Serie A goals since 1958.<ref name="Europe's next generation of stars: Berardi, Sanches, Dembele, Gabigol"/>

====2015–16 season====
On 25 June 2015, it was announced through an official statement that co-ownership was resolved in favour of Sassuolo for €10 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Calciomercato: Domenico Berardi resta in neroverde|url=http://www.sassuolocalcio.it/articles/?id=9&aid=1471/calciomercato-domenico-berardi-rimane-al-sassuolo|access-date=2 October 2016|publisher=Sassuolocalcio.it|language=it|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924094459/http://www.sassuolocalcio.it/articles/?id=9&aid=1471/calciomercato-domenico-berardi-rimane-al-sassuolo|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sassuolo sign Juventus forward outright|date=25 June 2015 |url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2015/06/sassuolo-sign-juventus-forward-outright/|access-date=2 October 2016|publisher=Forza Italian Football}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=25 June 2015|title=Sharing agreement termination of the player Domenico Berardi|url=http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/20e870c5-01d4-4078-ae86-90f9c300233a/comunicato+25062015+berardi+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=20e870c5-01d4-4078-ae86-90f9c300233a|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626130318/http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/20e870c5-01d4-4078-ae86-90f9c300233a/comunicato+25062015+berardi+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=20e870c5-01d4-4078-ae86-90f9c300233a|archive-date=26 June 2015|access-date=25 June 2015|publisher=Juventus F.C.}}</ref> It was reported that it was part of [[Simone Zaza]]'s deal to Juventus. However, Juventus also retained the option to bring Berardi back to Turin in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|date=23 June 2015|title=Il Sassuolo "lascia" Zaza e "fa suo" Berardi. La Juve può ricomprarlo nel 2016|url=http://www.tuttosport.com/news/calcio/calciomercato/2015/06/23-1916145/il_sassuolo_lascia_zaza_e_fa_suo_berardi_la_juve_puo_ricomprarlo_nel_2016/|access-date=7 July 2015|work=Tuttosport|language=it}}</ref>

Berardi opened the [[2015–16 Serie A]] season with a Man of the Match performance in a 2–1 home win over Napoli, setting up [[Antonio Floro Flores|Floro Flores]]'s goal;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Sassuolo/23-08-2015/sassuolo-napoli-2-1-hamsik-illude-poi-segnano-floro-flores-sansone-1201058381005.shtml|title=Sassuolo-Napoli 2-1. Hamsik illude, poi segnano Floro Flores e Sansone|trans-title=Sassuolo-Napoli 2-1. Hamsik deceives, then Floro Flores and Sansone score|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first=Mimmo |last=Malfitano|date=23 August 2015|access-date=24 August 2015}}</ref> however, he also picked up an injury during the match, which would reportedly rule him out for a month and a half.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/calcio/fantanews/24-08-2015/sassuolo-berardi-fuori-45-giorni-inter-ansia-icardi-1201070053110.shtml|title=Sassuolo, Berardi fuori per 45 giorni. Inter in ansia per Icardi|trans-title=Sassuolo, Berardi out for 45 days. Inter anxious for Icardi|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|date=24 August 2015|access-date=24 August 2015}}</ref> He returned to the pitch after an early recovery on 20 September 2015, coming on as a substitute in a 2–2 away draw against [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://it.eurosport.com/calcio/serie-a/2015-2016/le-pagelle-di-roma-sassuolo-2-2_sto4918968/story.shtml|title=Le pagelle di Roma-Sassuolo 2-2|publisher=Eurosport|language=it|first=Stefano |last=Silvestri|date=20 September 2015|access-date=21 September 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season from the penalty spot in a 2–1 home win over [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] on 18 October 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Sassuolo/18-10-2015/sassuolo-lazio-2-1-decidono-berardi-missiroli-non-basta-felipe-anderson-130554232712.shtml|title=Sassuolo-Lazio 2-1. Decidono Berardi e Missiroli, non basta Felipe Anderson|trans-title=Sassuolo-Lazio 2-1. Berardi and Missiroli decide the match, Felipe Anderson's goal not enough|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first=Stefano |last=Cieri|date=18 October 2015|access-date=18 October 2015}}</ref> Sassuolo finished the league season in sixth place, sealing a spot in the [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round of the 2016–17 UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84783/sassuolo-italian-success-story|title=Sassuolo: 'Italian success story'|publisher=Football Italia|date=22 May 2016|access-date=6 June 2016}}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
On 28 July 2016, Berardi made his debut in European competitions in the first leg of a third-round UEFA Europa League qualifying match against [[FC Luzern]], scoring his and Sassuolo's first ever goal in the competition from the penalty spot in a 1–1 away draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://it.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/022f-0e949fab9e86-b30c40d2a3ac-1000--sassuolo-esordio-positivo-in-europa/|title=Sassuolo, esordio positivo in Europa|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|language=it|date=28 July 2016|access-date=29 July 2016}}</ref> In the return leg on 4 August, he scored twice in a 3–0 home win which allowed Sassuolo to advance to the [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League qualifying phase and play-off round#Play-off round|play-off round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Europa-League/04-08-2016/europa-league-sassuolo-lucerna-3-0-berardi-2-gol-defrel-playoff-160600392706.shtml|title=Sassuolo-Lucerna 3-0, Berardi fa 2 gol, conquistato il playoff di Europa League|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first=Ivan |last=Palumbo|date=4 August 2016|access-date=4 August 2016}}</ref> In the first leg of the Europa League play-offs, on 18 August, Berardi scored a goal and set up another in a 3–0 home win over [[Red Star Belgrade]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/89991/berardi-'great-first-leg'|title=Berardi: 'Great first leg'|publisher=Football Italia|date=18 August 2016|access-date=18 August 2016}}</ref> On the opening match of the 2016–17 Serie A season three days later, he scored once again, from the penalty spot, to give Sassuolo a 1–0 away victory over [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/report?gameId=461297|title=Palermo 0-1 Sassuolo|publisher=ESPN FC|date=21 August 2016|access-date=22 August 2016}}</ref> On 25 August, he scored yet another goal (his sixth in five matches) in a 1–1 draw against Red Star Belgrade in the return leg of the Europa League play-offs to seal a spot for Sassuolo in the season's [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League|Europa League group stage]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Europa-League/25-08-2016/europa-league-stella-rossa-sassuolo-1-1-berardi-160922440000.shtml|title=Europa League, Stella Rossa-Sassuolo 1-1, Berardi segna ancora|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first=Pietro |last=Razzini|date=25 August 2016|access-date=26 August 2016}}</ref> On 28 August, he continued his goalscoring run, netting a goal in a 2–1 home win over [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]], becoming the youngest Italian player since the [[1994–95 Serie A|1994–95 season]] to score 40 goals in Serie A, and the second youngest player overall, behind [[Alexandre Pato]], at the age of 22 years and 27 days; he later suffered an injury during the match,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/90564/sassuolo-berardi-injury-not-serious|title=Sassuolo: Berardi injury not serious|publisher=Football Italia|date=29 August 2016|access-date=29 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/pescara/serie-160-a-160-sassuolo-pescara-2-1-berardi-segna-sempre_1115626-201602a.shtml|title=Serie A: Sassuolo-Pescara 2-1, Berardi segna sempre|publisher=Mediaset|language=it|date=28 August 2016|access-date=29 August 2016}}</ref> and it was later announced that he had suffered knee ligament damage, ruling him out for the rest of the calendar year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/96296/berardi-back-training|title=Berardi back in training|publisher=Football Italia|date=2 January 2017|access-date=8 January 2017}}</ref> After being sidelined for almost four and a half months, Berardi returned to action as a second-half substitute in a 0–0 home draw against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] on 8 January 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Sassuolo/08-01-2017/sassuolo-torino-0-0-berardi-torna-campo-4-mesi-180335122547.shtml|title=Sassuolo-Torino 0-0. Berardi torna in campo dopo 4 mesi e mezzo|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first=Andrea |last=Elefante|date=8 January 2017|access-date=8 January 2017}}</ref>

====2017–present====
On 24 August 2017, Berardi signed a five-year contract with Sassuolo.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.sassuolocalcio.it/articles/?id=9&aid=3449/domenico-berardi-rinnova-fino-a-giugno-2022|title=Domenico Berardi rinnova fino a Giugno 2022|date=24 August 2017|access-date=30 August 2017|publisher=U.S. Sassuolo Calcio|language=it|archive-date=11 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190611102835/http://www.sassuolocalcio.it/articles/?id=9&aid=3449%2Fdomenico-berardi-rinnova-fino-a-giugno-2022|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, Berardi scored a goal from a penalty in a 1–0 home win over [[Inter Milan]], in the first match of the [[2018–19 Serie A]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45242529 |title=Sassuolo 1-0 Inter Milan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2018 |access-date=26 August 2018 }}</ref> On 1 September 2019, Berardi netted a hat-trick in a 4–1 win over [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.legaseriea.it/en/serie-a/match-report/2019-20/UNICO/UNI/2/SASSAM|title=Sassuolo 4–1 Sampdoria|website=Lega Serie A|date=1 September 2019|accessdate=24 May 2021|archive-date=16 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616211230/https://www.legaseriea.it/en/serie-a/match-report/2019-20/UNICO/UNI/2/SASSAM|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 17 April 2021, Berardi scored twice as Sassuolo came from behind to beat [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] by a score of 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forzaitalianfootball.com/2021/04/centurion-berardi-forces-fiorentina-second-half-collapse/|title=CENTURION BERARDI FORCES FIORENTINA SECOND-HALF COLLAPSE|website=Forza Italian Football|date=17 April 2021|accessdate=24 May 2021}}</ref> This meant that Berardi had reached 100 goals in all competitions for the Neroverdi since debuting for the club in the Serie B in August 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forzaitalianfootball.com/2021/04/domenico-berardi-legendary-status-at-sassuolo-and-applause-for-a-career-well-spent/|title=DOMENICO BERARDI: LEGENDARY STATUS AT SASSUOLO AND APPLAUSE FOR A CAREER WELL SPENT|website=Forza Italian Football|date=19 April 2021|accessdate=24 May 2021}}</ref> On 23 May 2021, Berardi scored his 17th goal of the [[2020–21 Serie A]] season in a 2–0 win over Lazio.<ref name=scoring>{{cite web|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/en/serie-a/statistics/Gol|title=Serie A TIM {{!}} Top Scorers Table|publisher=LegaNazionale Professionisti Serie A|access-date=23 May 2021|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726232346/http://www.legaseriea.it/en/serie-a/statistics/Gol|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was Berardi's best goal-scoring season in his professional career and helped Sassuolo to an 8th place finish, missing out on [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|European competition]] on goal difference.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/158963|title=Sassuolo 2-0 Lazio: Not enough for Neroverdi|website=Football Italia|date=23 May 2021|accessdate=24 May 2021}}</ref>

On 18 March 2022, Berardi scored twice in a 4–1 home win over [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]]; his second goal, which came from a penalty, was his 100th goal in Serie A, all of which came with Sassuolo.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/soccer/2022/03/18/berardi-reaches-100-serie-a-goals-as-sassuolo-beats-spezia.html |title=Berardi reaches 100 Serie A goals as Sassuolo beats Spezia |work=The Toronto Star |date=18 March 2022 |access-date=18 March 2022 }}</ref> In the [[2022–23 Serie A|2022–23 season]], he scored 12 goals in Serie A, the most by an Italian player along with [[Ciro Immobile]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Thakur |first=Yash |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/Serie-a-top-scorers-2022-23/bltf981fcc7946c1001#cs37ada19a7fd3fe9e |title=Serie A top scorers 2022-23: Osimhen, Martinez, Lookman & the race for the Golden Boot |publisher=Goal.com |date=4 June 2023 }}</ref>

On 23 September 2023, Berardi celebrated his milestone of 300 games in Serie A with a goal against Juventus, in the eventual 4–2 home win.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.legaseriea.it/en/media/serie-a/sassuolo-4-2-juventus-13b3e5edl60ol8 | title=Sassuolo 4-2 Juventus }}</ref> On 28 September 2023, during weekday away game against Inter Milan, he scored the winning goal in a 2–1 comeback for Sassuolo.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.legaseriea.it/en/media/serie-a/inter-1-2-sassuolo-13b77c07156e0j | title=Inter 1-2 Sassuolo }}</ref>

On 3 March 2024, after returning to action from an injury to his left knee sustained in January, Berardi suffered an injury to his right ankle in the second half of a 1–0 away defeat to [[Hellas Verona FC|Verona]] in Serie A, which immediately forced him off the pitch.<ref>{{cite web |title=Italy forward Berardi injured playing for Sassuolo; could miss Euro 2024 |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/article/italy-forward-berardi-injured-playing-for-sassuolo-could-miss-euro-2024/ |publisher=www.sportsnet.ca |access-date=4 March 2024}}</ref> After surgical reparation of a torn Achilles tendon, he began rehabilitation expected to last approximately 10 months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football-italia.net/official-sassuolo-confirm-serious-injury-and-surgery-for-berardi/|title=Official: Sassuolo confirm serious injury and surgery for Berardi - Football Italia|date=4 March 2024|website=football-italia.net}}</ref>

During the 2024 summer transfer window, Berardi was linked with a transfer to several clubs, including former club [[Juventus]]. However, he stayed at Sassuolo despite the club's recent relegation to the Serie B in his absence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-B/Sassuolo/09-07-2024/berardi-infortunio-e-recupero-obiettivo-agosto-l-interesse-di-juve-bologna-fiorentina.shtml|title=Dove va Berardi? Ad agosto torna, può essere il jolly del mercato. Le piste per lui|website=La Gazzetta dello Sport}}</ref>

In October 2024, Berardi returned to playing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football-italia.net/berardi-makes-sassuolo-return-seven-months-out/|title=Berardi makes Sassuolo return in Serie B after seven months out - Football Italia - October 5 latest|date=5 October 2024|website=football-italia.net}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Berardi was a component of the [[Italy national under-19 football team|Italian under-19 national team]], but did not answer his call-up for qualifications to the European Championship of the age group and was disqualified for nine months for violation of the code of ethics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calcionewstime.com/sassuolo-berardi-squalificato-diserto-la-convocazione-under-19/ |title=SASSUOLO: Berardi squalificato, disertò la convocazione con Under 19 |publisher=Calcionewstime.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202152958/http://www.calcionewstime.com/sassuolo-berardi-squalificato-diserto-la-convocazione-under-19/ |archive-date=2 February 2014 |access-date=2 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.calcionews24.com/sassuolo-caso-berardi-si-allontana-la-maglia-azzurra-339232.html |title=Sassuolo, caso Berardi: si allontana la maglia azzurra |language=it |publisher=Calcio News 24 |date=20 June 2014 |access-date=2 October 2016 }}</ref>

Berardi has played for the [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italian under-21 national team]].<ref name="SW"/> He received his first call-up on 28 February 2014, for the team's European qualifying match against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]] on 5 March.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ansa.it/web/notizie/rubriche/calcio/2014/02/27/21-convocati-Di-Biagio_10155742.html|title=Under 21: i convocati di Di Biagio|publisher=Ansa.it|language=it|date=28 February 2014|access-date=26 August 2016}}</ref> On 2 March, however, he elbowed [[Cristian Molinaro]] during Sassuolo's league fixture against Parma, and was subsequently excluded from the squad for violating the team's code of ethics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzettadiparma.it/news/sport/170862/La-gomitata-a-Molinaro-costa-a.html|title=La gomitata a Molinaro costa a Berardi la convocazione in Under21|publisher=La Gazzetta di Parma|language=it|date=2 March 2014|access-date=26 August 2016}}</ref> He made his debut under Italy under-21 manager [[Luigi Di Biagio]] on 4 June 2014, in a 4–0 home win over [[Montenegro national under-21 football team|Montenegro]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Under 21, amichevoli: l'Italia cala il poker al Montenegro|url=http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/Nazionale/2014/articoli/1037059/under-21-amichevoli-l-italia-cala-il-poker-al-montenegro.shtml|access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal on his third appearance for the ''azzurrini'', the match-winning goal in a 3–2 win over [[Serbia national under-21 football team|Serbia]] in a [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification Group 9|2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualifying match]], which allowed Italy to progress to the [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification play-offs|playoffs]], and eventually qualify for the [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|final tournament]], which would be held in the Czech Republic.<ref>{{cite web|title=Under 21 – Italia, rimonta-show con Belotti e Berardi|url=https://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/notizie/under-21-italia-rimonta-show-belotti-berardi-205546442--sow.html|access-date=26 January 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410051726/https://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/notizie/under-21-italia-rimonta-show-belotti-berardi-205546442--sow.html|archive-date=10 April 2015}}</ref>

On 1 June 2015, Berardi was selected in Di Biagio's 27-man provisional squad for the 2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/2528287/2015/06/News.shtml|title=Verso l'Europeo: 27 Azzurrini convocati da Di Biagio per il raduno di Appiano Gentile|publisher=FIGC|language=it|date=1 June 2015|access-date=15 June 2015}}</ref> on 7 June, he was included in the final 23-man squad which would take part at the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/2528362/2015/06/News.shtml|title=Ufficializzata la lista dei 23 convocati per la Fase Finale del Campionato Europeo|publisher=FIGC|language=it|date=7 June 2015|access-date=15 June 2015}}</ref> Berardi scored a goal from a penalty in Italy's opening match of the tournament, against [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden]], on 18 June, which ended in a 2–1 loss.<ref name=Sweden>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0ded6dc7a39a-bbf789e254b4-1000--sweden-surge-leaves-italy-defeated/|title=Sweden surge leaves Italy defeated|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|first=Kevin |last=Ashby|date=18 June 2015|access-date=18 June 2015}}</ref> On 24 June, he set up [[Andrea Belotti]]'s goal in Italy's 3–1 win over [[England national under-21 football team|England]] in Italy's final group match, although the result was not enough to see the Italian under-21 side progress to the semi-finals, as the ''azzurrini'' finished third in their group, behind the two eventual finalists [[Portugal national under-21 football team|Portugal]] and Sweden.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Nazionale/24-06-2015/europeo-under-21-inghilterra-italia-0-2-ma-biscotto-ci-condanna-belotti-benassi-120299937665.shtml|title=Europeo Under 21, Inghilterra-Italia 1-3, ma il biscotto condanna gli Azzurrini|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|first=Luca |last=Bianchin|language=it|date=24 June 2015|access-date=4 July 2015}}</ref>

In June 2017, Berardi was included in the Italy under-21 squad for the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] by manager Di Biagio.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/103752/u21-italy-squad-euros-named|title=U21: Italy squad for Euros named|publisher=Football Italia|date=6 June 2017|access-date=16 June 2017}}</ref> In Italy's second group match on 21 June, he scored his team's only goal in a 3–1 defeat to [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/match/2021152--czechia-vs-italy/ |title=Czech Republic 3-1 Italy |website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=21 June 2017 |access-date=6 March 2019 }}</ref> Italy were eliminated by [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain]] in the semi-finals on 27 June, following a 3–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/european-under-21-championship/2284/blog/post/3149736/italy-fall-to-familiar-foe-spain-at-u21-euros-but-there-is-hope-for-the-future|title=Italy fall to familiar foe Spain at U21 Euros but there is hope for the future|publisher=ESPN FC|first=James |last=Horncastle|date=28 June 2017|access-date=24 October 2017}}</ref>

===Senior===
Berardi received his first [[Italy national football team|senior international call-up for Italy]] from manager [[Antonio Conte]] in October 2015, ahead of Italy's [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|UEFA Euro 2016 qualifiers]] against [[Azerbaijan national football team|Azerbaijan]] and [[Norway national football team|Norway]] on 10 and 13 October; he suffered a muscular injury in Sassuolo's pre-match warmup against [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] on 4 October, however, which forced him to pull out of the national side for the two upcoming fixtures.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gazzettaworld.gazzetta.it/news/serie-a/sassuolo/berardi-injury/?refresh_ce-cp|title=Berardi suffers another injury setback|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|first=Ogo |last=Sylla|date=5 October 2015|access-date=5 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/italy/story/2649912/domenico-berardi-pulls-out-of-italy-squad-with-muscle-injury|title=Uncapped Domenico Berardi pulls out of Italy squad with muscular injury|publisher=ESPN FC|date=5 October 2015|access-date=5 October 2015}}</ref>

In May 2017, Berardi was selected by Italy's senior head coach [[Gian Piero Ventura]] for the team's unofficial friendly against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]] in [[Stadio Carlo Castellani|Empoli]] on 31 May.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://it.eurosport.com/calcio/qualificazioni-mondiali-europa/2018/convocati-per-l-amichevole-contro-san-marino-ventura-chiama-emerson_sto6181095/story.shtml |title=Convocati per l'amichevole contro San Marino, Ventura chiama Emerson |publisher=eurosport.com |language=it |date=25 May 2017 |access-date=27 August 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://it.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/newsid=2473685.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170615153121/http://it.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/newsid=2473685.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 June 2017 |title=Italia, i convocati per l'amichevole con San Marino |website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|language=it |date=25 May 2017 |access-date=27 August 2018 }}</ref> He made his unofficial senior international debut in the match, [[Captain (association football)|captaining]] the squad, and starting in Italy's eventual 8–0 win, setting up [[Gianluca Lapadula]]'s second goal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Italy waiting for Berardi |url=https://www.football-italia.net/104319/italy-waiting-berardi |publisher=Football Italia |first=Matthew |last=Santangelo |date=18 June 2017 |access-date=27 August 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/nazionale/2017/05/31/news/italia-san_marino_8-0_tripletta_di_lapadula_ventura_sorride-166933984/ |title=Italia-San Marino 8-0: tripletta di Lapadula, Ventura sorride |publisher=La Repubblica |first=Jacopo |last=Manfredi |language=it |date=31 May 2017 |access-date=27 August 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/mondiali-2018/italia/2017/05/31-26548944/italia-san_marino_8-0_la_nazionale_sperimentale_si_scatena/?cookieAccept |title=Italia-San Marino 8-0: Lapadula-show, è tripletta |publisher=Il Corriere dello Sport |language=it |date=31 May 2017 |access-date=27 August 2018 }}</ref>

Berardi made his official senior international debut for Italy under [[Roberto Mancini]], starting in a 3–1 friendly loss to [[France national football team|France]] in Nice on 1 June 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/122286/caldara-azzurri-right-track |title=Caldara: 'Azzurri on right track' |publisher=Football Italia |date=2 June 2018 |access-date=2 June 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/122275/italy-experimental-azzurri-test-france |title=Italy: Experimental Azzurri test France |publisher=Football Italia |date=1 June 2018 |access-date=2 June 2018 }}</ref>

Berardi scored his first senior goal for the national team on 7 October 2020, the final goal of a 6–0 home win against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/160290/italy-6-0-moldova-caputo-and-el-sha-shine-azzurri|title=Italy 6-0 Moldova: Caputo and El Sha shine for Azzurri|publisher=Football Italia|date=7 October 2020}}</ref>

In June 2021, Berardi was included in Italy's squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/mancini-names-uncapped-striker-raspadori-final-italy-euro-2020-squad-2021-06-01/ |title=Mancini names uncapped striker Raspadori in final Italy Euro 2020 squad |work=Reuters |date=1 June 2021 |access-date=5 June 2021 }}</ref> In the opening match of the tournament on 11 June, a 3–0 win over [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]], his cross led to the opening goal of the game, an own–goal by [[Merih Demiral]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://football-italia.net/turkey-0-3-italy-azzurri-dominate-euro-2020-debut/ |title=Turkey 0-3 Italy: Azzurri dominate Euro 2020 debut |publisher=Football Italia |last1=Campanale |first1=Susy |date=11 June 2021 |access-date=12 June 2021 }}</ref> In the following group match on 16 June, he set up [[Manuel Locatelli]] for Italy's opening goal in an eventual 3–0 win over [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/italy-switzerland-result-score-euro-2020-b1867416.html |title=Manuel Locatelli dazzles as Italy dominate Switzerland |work=The Independent |date=16 June 2021 |access-date=17 June 2021 }}</ref> On 11 July, Berardi won the European Championship with Italy following a 3–2 [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] victory over [[England national football team|England]] at [[Wembley Stadium]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2020 Final|final]], after a 1–1 draw in [[Overtime (sports)|extra-time]]; Berardi came on as a substitute for [[Ciro Immobile]] in the second half of regulation time, and later scored Italy's first spot-kick in the shoot-out.<ref name="Euro2020Final">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51198762|title=England lose shootout in Euro 2020 final |first=Phil |last=McNulty|work=BBC Sport|date=11 July 2021 |access-date=11 July 2021 }}</ref>

On 10 October, Berardi scored the match–winning goal from a penalty in a 2–1 home victory over [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the bronze medal match of the [[2020–21 UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://football-italia.net/nations-league-italy-2-1-belgium-azzurri-take-bronze-medal/ |title=Nations League - Italy 2-1 Belgium: Azzurri take bronze medal |publisher=Football Italia |date=10 October 2021 |access-date=10 October 2021 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
{{quote box|width=33%|align=right|quote="He's our symbol, the [[Francesco Totti]] of Sassuolo."|source=—Sassuolo CEO Giovanni Carnevali on Berardi.<ref name="The Totti of Sassuolo"/>}}
A quick, tenacious, technically gifted and hardworking left-footed [[Forward (association football)|forward]], with an eye for goal, Berardi is capable of being deployed in several offensive positions across the pitch. He has been utilised as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] and as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|supporting forward]], although his preferred position is on the [[Forward (association football)#Winger|right wing]], which allows him to cut into the centre and shoot on goal with his stronger left foot, or link up with teammates to create goalscoring opportunities for other players.<ref name="Europe's next generation of stars: Berardi, Sanches, Dembele, Gabigol"/><ref name="Why Domenico Berardi is the man"/><ref name="Domenico Berardi">{{cite web|url=http://vivoazzurro.it/soccer-player/domenico-berardi/|title=Domenico Berardi|website=vivoazzurro.it|access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="World Cup Squad Selector: Berardi">{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/47417/world-cup-squad-selector-berardi|title=World Cup Squad Selector: Berardi|publisher=Football Italia|first=Livio |last=Caferoglu|date=5 April 2014|access-date=6 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="Berardi, Sassuolo's trump card">{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/56967/berardi-sassuolo%E2%80%99s-trump-card|title=Berardi, Sassuolo's trump card|publisher=Football Italia|first=Aman |last=Sehdev|date=8 October 2014|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://metro.co.uk/2016/03/09/domenico-berardi-could-make-tottenham-transfer-this-summer-5743643/|title=Domenico Berardi could make Tottenham transfer this summer|publisher=Metro|first=Will |last=Giles|date=9 March 2016|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref> Berardi has also been praised for his movement, positional sense, and work-rate off the ball, as well as his determination, maturity, tactical intelligence, decision making, and composure; however, he has also drawn criticism at times for his behaviour, lack of discipline, and a tendency to pick up unnecessary cards.<ref name="Why Domenico Berardi is the man"/><ref name="Berardi, Sassuolo's trump card"/><ref name="Ero certo delle qualità di Berardi L'Italia è piena di giovani talenti"/> He has also struggled with injuries throughout his career.<ref name="The Totti of Sassuolo">{{cite web |title='The Totti of Sassuolo' - Is Italy's former bad boy Berardi set for superstardom? {{!}} Sporting News Canada |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/soccer/news/the-totti-of-sassuolo-is-italy-former-bad-boy-berardi-set-for-superstardom/1jgtmb3rnxpjrz2qqfp047xoe |publisher=www.sportingnews.com |access-date=4 March 2024 |date=16 June 2021}}</ref> An accurate finisher from both inside and outside the area, and in one on one situations,<ref name="Why Domenico Berardi is the man"/> he is also an accurate [[Direct free kick|set-piece]] and [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty taker]].<ref name="Why Domenico Berardi is the man"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/calcio/fantanews/storie/20-08-2015/fantacalcio-tutti-rigoristi-vice-20-squadre-serie-magic-rigori/sassuolo.shtml|title=Fantacalcio: tutti i rigoristi (e i vice) delle 20 of his generation;<ref name="Europe's next generation of stars: Berardi, Sanches, Dembele, Gabigol">{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/blog/espn-fc-united-blog/68/post/2931824/europes-next-generation-of-stars-berardi-sanches-dembele-gabigol|title=Europe's next generation of stars: Berardi, Sanches, Dembele, Gabigol|publisher=ESPN FC|first=James |last=Horncastle|date=17 August 2016|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/24-03-2014/titolo-80301204619.shtml|title=Teen generation: i migliori Under 20 del mondo|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first1=Luca |last1=Bianchin|first2=Giulio |last2=Di Feo|date=5 April 2014|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref> in 2013, 2014, and 2015, ''[[Don Balón]]'' listed him as one of the top-100 young players in the world.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/esclusiva-tmw-berardi-nella-top-101-dei-talenti-pea-si-vedevano-subito-le-qualita-501852|title=ESCLUSIVA TMW - Berardi nella Top 101 Milan|AC Milan]] and [[Italy national football team|Italy]] manager [[Arrigo Sacchi]] described Berardi as "a player of great talent, a modern footballer who constantly plays with and for the team all over the field. Liveliness, intuition, temperament, physical strength, stamina combined with a good technique are his main attributes."<ref name="Why Domenico Berardi is the man">{{cite web|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/why-domenico-berardi-man-take-juventus-next-level|title=Why Domenico Berardi is the man to take Juventus to the next level|publisher=Four Four Two|first=Adam |last=Digby|date=23 May 2014|access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="Berardi-Sacchi: ieri faccia a faccia in azzurro">{{cite web|url=http://gazzettadimodena.gelocal.it/sport/2014/01/15/news/berardi-sacchi-ieri-faccia-a-faccia-in-azzurro-1.8476017|title=Berardi-Sacchi: ieri faccia a faccia in azzurro|publisher=La Gazzetta di Modena|language=it|date=15 January 2014|access-date=16 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Ero certo delle qualità di Berardi L'Italia è piena di giovani talenti">{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/premium/plus/Calcio/13-01-2014/ero-certo-qualita-berardi-italia-piena-giovani-talenti-202062003756.shtml|title=Ero certo delle qualità di Berardi L'Italia è piena di giovani talenti|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|first=Arrigo |last=Sacchi|date=14 January 2014|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref> In 2015, [[1982 FIFA World Cup]] winner [[Giancarlo Antognoni]] described Berardi as "...the young [[Roberto Baggio|[Roberto] Baggio]] of this generation" who "mixes creativity with strength. Just like when [[Michel Platini|Platini]] called Baggio 'a nine and a half.' He must only learn to control his character. At times his temper betrays him but he will learn."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzettaworld.com/news/serie-a/sassuolo/antognoni-sassuolo-roberto-baggio-generation/?refresh_ce-cp|title=Antognoni: Sassuolo's Berardi is the Baggio of this generation|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|first=Luca |last=Calamai|date=4 August 2015|access-date=6 June 2016}}</ref> In a 2015 interview, Berardi stated that his main influences as a footballer were [[Lionel Messi]], [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] and [[Arjen Robben]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/69687/berardi-self-control-not-easy|title=Berardi: 'Self-control not easy'|publisher=Football Italia|date=25 July 2015|access-date=6 June 2016}}</ref> In 2017, he revealed that [[Inter Milan]] was his favorite childhood team, also describing [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] and [[Diego Milito]] as his biggest footballing idols at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/inter-are-my-heart-says-sassuolo-star-berardi|title=Inter are in my heart, says Sassuolo star Berardi|publisher=FourFourTwo|date=14 May 2017|access-date=22 February 2019}}</ref>

'''Prampram''' is a coastal town in the [[Greater Accra Region]] of [[Ghana]].<ref name=pramp>{{Cite news|title=Hope City moved to Prampram|url=http://graphic.com.gh/Business-News/hope-city-moved-to-prampram.html|location=Accra, Ghana|access-date=3 August 2013|newspaper=[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Daily Graphic]]}}</ref> The town is located in the [[Ningo Prampram District]].

Prampram (Gbugbla), the capital of Ningo-Prampram, is 15 minutes' drive from the port city of Tema and 45 minutes from Accra, the national capital, and is an emerging center of industrial activities.

==Places of interest==
The town is set to become an international hub as the government has acquired more than 60 acres of land to construct the country's first [[Aerotropolis]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ghana To Get Aerotropolis In Ningo-Prampram |url=https://www.modernghana.com/news/862849/ghana-to-get-aerotropolis-in-ningo-prampram.html |access-date=2026-10-24 |website=Modern Ghana |language=en}}</ref>

<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-07-12 |title=Government considers aeropolis offers |url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/business/Government-considers-aeropolis-offers-557912 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250101131156/https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/business/Government-considers-aeropolis-offers-557912 |archive-date=2025-01-01 |access-date=2026-05-16 |work=GhanaWeb |language=en-US}}</ref>Prampram features several white sand beaches and recreational facilities for tourists.

The town is home to the first and only bulletproof police station in Ghana, built by the Danes.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-02-17 |title=Oldest, bulletproof police station at Prampram |url=https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/oldest-bulletproof-police-station-at-prampram.html |location=Accra, Ghana|access-date=2026-05-16 |newspaper=[[Daily Graphic (Ghana)|Daily Graphic]]|language=en-gb}}</ref>

A small English trading fort, [[Fort Vernon]], built in 1742, is located in Prampram.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fort Vernon, Prampram|url=http://www.ghanamuseums.org/forts/fort-vernon.php|website=Ghana Museums & Monuments Board|access-date=12 May 2020}}</ref>

A video showing the [[Dancing Pallbearers]], carrying a coffin and dancing to remember the deceased person's life, soon became viral, and later an [[internet meme]].

In February 2021, Romco Group opened a non-ferrous recycling facility in Prampram, consisting of two furnaces.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://aluminiumtoday.com/news/industry-overhaul-continues-as-romco-metals-ltd-opens-second-eco-recycling-facility-in-ghana | title=Industry overhaul continues as Romco Metals Ltd opens second… }}</ref>

=== Notable natives ===
Notable natives and residents of Prampram include:
* Nene Annorkwei II<ref>{{Cite web |title=File:Nene Annorkwei II, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah.jpg – Wikimedia Commons |url=https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nene_Annorkwei_II,_Osagyefo_Dr._Kwame_Nkrumah.jpg |access-date=17 July 2022 |website=commons.wikimedia.org}}</ref>
* [[Kofi Adumua Bossman]], former Justice of the Supreme Court of Ghana<ref>{{cite journal|date=1960|title=Ghana Year Book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=c9cgAQAAMAAJ&q=adumua+prampram|publisher=Graphic Corporation|page=166}}</ref>
* W. A. N Adumua Bossman, former President of [[Ghana Bar Association]]
* [[Enoch Teye Mensah]] (E. T. Mensah), former member of the [[Ghana Parliament]] for [[Ningo-Prampram (Ghana parliament constituency)|Ningo-Prampram]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.parliament.gh/honmensah_enoch_teye.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091027054626/http://www.parliament.gh/honmensah_enoch_teye.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 October 2009|title=Hon.Mensah Enoch Teye {{!}} The Parliament of Ghana|date=27 October 2009|access-date=10 December 2019}}</ref>
* Naa Morkor Busia, former first Lady, wife of late Dr. Kofi Abrefia Busia
* [[Ernestina Naadu Mills]], former Ghana first lady, wife of the late President [[John Atta Mills]]
* Members of the [[Dancing Pallbearers|Nana Otafrija Pallbearing Service]], also known as The Dancing Pallbearers
*[[Charles Akonnor]], Ghanaian football coach, Head Coach of the [[Ghana national football team]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Profile of National Team Coaches: CK Akonnor|url=https://www.ghanafa.org/profile-of-national-team-coaches-ck-akonnor|access-date=8 September 2021|website=ghanafa.org|publisher=[[Ghana Football Association]]}}</ref>

1383164107.title: Mino (straw cape)
1383164107.content:
{{short description|Traditional Japanese straw raincoat}}
{{More citations needed|date=September 2018}}
{{Italic title}}
[[File:Mino.JPG|thumb|upright=1.0|A {{transliteration|ja|mino}} straw cape]]
A {{nihongo||蓑|'''mino'''}} is a traditional Japanese [[raincoat]] made out of [[straw]], originally invented in China.{{citation needed}} Traditional {{transliteration|ja|mino}} are an article of outerwear covering the entire body, although shorter ones resembling [[grass skirt]]s were also historically used to cover the lower body alone. Similar straw capes were also used in [[China]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://costumes.unc.edu/costar/view/NowesArk/public/Spage.jsp?spageId=377 |title=Japanese Mino (Rainwear) |website=costumes.unc.edu |access-date=2019-11-24 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220924120436/http://costumes.unc.edu/costar/view/NowesArk/public/Spage.jsp%3FspageId=377 |archive-date=24 September 2022}}</ref> [[Vietnam]] and [[Korea]].

==Overview==
[[File:Straw_namahage.2.jpg|thumb|upright=1.0|Several {{transliteration|ja|[[namahage]]}} wearing outfits incorporating {{transliteration|ja|mino}}.]]
[[Rice]] straw has naturally [[Waterproofing|water-repellent]] properties, with water droplets that hit a mat of straw tending to flow along the length of the fibres, rather than penetrating underneath it. For this reason, early Japanese rain gear was often made of straw, which had the added benefit of being cheap to acquire, easy to weave and fasten, and being light in weight; however, this rain gear was also bulky in size, and highly flammable. In earlier eras,{{when|date=February 2022}} straw clothing had the additional advantage of affording a significant degree of [[camouflage]] in certain terrain,<ref name=":0"/> including forests and wetlands, similar to modern [[ghillie suit]]s.

As [[synthetic fiber]]s and later [[plastic]]s were introduced to Japan, {{transliteration|ja|mino}} lost much of their practicality and fell out of use. Today, however, they are still worn as costumes in various traditional folk traditions and [[Matsuri|festivals]], such as the New Year celebrations of the [[Oga Peninsula]], where men dress as [[ogre]]-like {{transliteration|ja|[[namahage]]}} wearing masks and {{transliteration|ja|mino}}. {{transliteration|ja|Mino}} are also seen in some [[kabuki]] plays.<ref>{{cite book |last1=M. Shaver |first1=Ruth |title=Kabuki Costume |date=1966 |publisher=Charles E. Tuttle Company: Publishers |location=Vermont |page=91 |edition=1st |chapter=6 |quote="Actors went to great lengths to produce striking effects. For example, Bandō Shūka, playing the role of an ''onna hinin'' (beggar woman), appeared on the stage covered with a ''komo'' (straw mat sometimes used as a raincape) made of gold threads instead of the usual rice straw.}}</ref>

== Popular culture ==
{{nihongo3|"The Monkey's Raincoat"|猿蓑|[[Sarumino]]}} is a 1691 anthology of [[Matsuo Bashō|Bashō]]-school poetry. It is widely considered to be one of the most important compilations of [[Classical Japanese language|classical Japanese]] verse.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basho-yamadera.com/en/yamadera/sarumino/|title=Sarumino (The Monkey's Raincoat), book in hanshibon format, two volumes Edited by Kyorai and Boncho Genroku 4 (1691) Izutsuya Shobei, publisher {{!}} 細道・より道・松尾芭蕉|website=basho-yamadera.com|access-date=2019-11-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SN72QCVBpVAC&q=sarumino+%22magnum+opus%22&pg=PA86|title=Early Modern Japanese Literature: An Anthology, 1600-1900|last=Shirane|first=Haruo|date=2008-04-21|publisher=Columbia University Press|isbn=978-0-231-51614-3|language=en|edition=Abridged}}</ref>

The [[Bagworm moth|bagworm]] [[Pokémon]], Burmy, is called {{nihongo||ミノムッチ|Minomucchi}} in Japanese, which is a [[portmanteau]] of {{nihongo|ミノムシ|minomushi}}, the Japanese word for bagworm, and the Japanese suffix {{transliteration|ja|-cchi}}, which denotes a cute nickname. {{transliteration|ja|Minomushi}} itself is a portmanteau of {{transliteration|ja|mino}} and {{transliteration|ja|mushi}}, meaning "bug". This means that Burmy's Japanese name roughly translates to mean "a cutie in a straw coat".<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schmidt-Jeffris|first1=R. A.|last2=Nelson|first2=J. C.|date=2018-09-15|title=Gotta Catch 'Em All!Communicating Entomology with Pokémon|journal=American Entomologist|language=en|volume=64|issue=3|pages=159–164|doi=10.1093/ae/tmy048|issn=1046-2821|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The Ice-type Pokémon Snorunt is based on a {{transliteration|ja|yukinko}}, a Japanese folklore spirit from the snow, which also wears a {{transliteration|ja|mino}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Snorunt (Pokémon)|url=https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Snorunt_(Pok%C3%A9mon)|website=Bulbapedia|date=2025-11-20|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en}}</ref>

The sound ninja from [[Naruto (TV series)|Naruto]] Dosu Kinuta wears a ''mino'' on his shoulders.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Kishimoto|first1=Masashi|date=2006-07-05|title=Naruto Anime Profiles, Vol. 1|publisher= Viz media|volume=15|issue=1|pages=221|url=https://archive.org/details/narutoanimeprofi0000unse/page/221/mode/1up|isbn=1421506572}}</ref>

1383163798.title: Unreleased Half-Life games
1383163798.content:
{{Short description|Unreleased video games}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Unreleased ''Half-Life'' games}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=February 2026}}
''[[Half-Life (series)|Half-Life]]'' is a series of [[first-person shooter]] games created and published by [[Valve Corporation|Valve]]. Since the release of the original ''[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]'' for [[Windows]] in 1998, several ''Half-Life'' projects have been canceled, including some developed by other studios.

In 1999, Valve canceled a ''Half-Life'' [[Porting|port]] for [[MacOS|Mac]] developed by Logicware. '''''Half-Life: Hostile Takeover''''', an [[expansion pack]] for ''Half-Life'' developed by [[2015 (company)|2015]], was cancelled in 2000. In 2001, [[Sierra Entertainment|Sierra]], the publisher of the original ''Half-Life'', canceled a port for [[Dreamcast]] after [[Sega]] announced its discontinuation.

After releasing ''[[Half-Life 2: Episode Two]]'' in 2007, Valve struggled to settle on a direction for a new ''Half-Life'' game. ''[[Half-Life 2: Episode Three|Episode Three]]'' was canceled after Valve abandoned [[Episodic video game|episodic]] development and began developing a new [[game engine]], [[Source 2]]. Another ''Half-Life 2'' episode, by [[Junction Point Studios]], was canceled after Junction Point was acquired by [[Disney Interactive Studios]]. Valve moved the project to [[Arkane Studios]], who developed it as ''Ravenholm,'' set in the [[Ravenholm|town infested with zombies]] from ''[[Half-Life 2]]'' (2004). Valve canceled it as they felt it was creatively restrained.

Valve developed '''''Half-Life 3''''' between 2013 and 2014, experimenting with [[Procedural generation|procedurally generated]] levels, but canceled it as the Source 2 engine was still unfinished. A [[Virtual reality game|virtual reality]] (VR) game set on a time-travelling ship, ''Borealis'', was canceled as the VR technology and tools were not complete. As of 2026, [[Data mining|datamines]] and leaks suggested that a ''Half-Life'' game codenamed '''''HLX''''' is in development using Source 2.

== ''Half-Life'' era (1998–2004) ==
=== ''Half-Life: Hostile Takeover'' ===
On November 23, 1999, ''[[GameSpot]]'' reported that [[2015 (company)|2015]] was developing a ''Half-Life'' [[expansion pack]] to follow ''[[Half-Life: Opposing Force]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ajami |first=Amer |date=November 23, 1999 |title=New Half-Life Add-on Coming |url=http://headline.gamespot.com/news/99_11/23_pc_halfadd/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000301003051/http://headline.gamespot.com/news/99_11/23_pc_halfadd/index.html |archive-date=March 1, 2000 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=[[GameSpot]]}}</ref> On March 18, 2000, the ''Adrenaline Vault'' reported that the expansion was named ''Half-Life: Hostile Takeover'' and that it had appeared on retail product lists with a release date of late August.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laprad |first=David |date=March 18, 2000 |title=New Half-Life Expansion Coming |url=http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=3182000-91229 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000607145116/http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=3182000-91229 |archive-date=June 7, 2000 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=The Adrenaline Vault}}</ref> On August 7, the ''Adrenaline Vault'' reported that [[Sierra Entertainment|Sierra]], the publisher of ''[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]'', had informed them that ''Hostile Takeover'' had been canceled. The [[stock keeping unit]] for ''Hostile Takeover'' was repurposed by online retailers for ''[[Counter-Strike (video game)|Half-Life: Counter-Strike]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laprad |first=David |date=August 7, 2000 |title=Confusion Surrounds Half-Life Add-On Pre-Sales |url=http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=872000-133010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010521163812/http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=872000-133010 |archive-date=May 21, 2001 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=The Adrenaline Vault}}</ref> On June 21, 2001, Valve filed a video game [[trademark]] for "Hostile Takeover". After several extensions, the trademark expired on October 3, 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HOSTILE TAKEOVER |publisher=[[United States Patent and Trademark Office]] |url=https://tsdr.uspto.gov/#caseNumber=76275717&caseType=SERIAL_NO&searchType=statusSearch |access-date=August 11, 2020 }}</ref>

=== Dreamcast port ===
On February 14, 2000, Sierra announced that a port of ''Half-Life'' for the [[Dreamcast]] console was in development by Captivation Digital Laboratories with Valve and [[Gearbox Software]]. It would feature improvements including higher-[[Polygon mesh|polygon]] character models and new lighting effects. Gearbox, who had developed ''Opposing Force'', created a new single-player campaign for the port, ''[[Half-Life: Blue Shift]],'' focusing on the security guard [[Barney Calhoun|Barney]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 14, 2000 |title=HALF-LIFE COMING TO SEGA DREAMCAST |url=https://www.bluesnews.com/pressreleases/hld.shtml |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423010222/https://www.bluesnews.com/pressreleases/hld.shtml |archive-date=April 23, 2019 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=Blue's News}}</ref>

The port was delayed to September 2000,<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDjFRH6hzA8 |title=Half-Life Dreamcast commercial |date=August 9, 2010 |publisher=Combine OverWiki |access-date=July 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160814212108/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDjFRH6hzA8 |archive-date=August 14, 2016 |via=YouTube |url-status=live}}</ref> then November,<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 14, 2000 |title=Half-Life: Blue Shift Announced |url=https://www.bluesnews.com/a/61 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107114414/https://www.bluesnews.com/a/61 |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=Blue's News}}</ref> when game publications began to receive early copies for review. Reception was mixed, with criticism for the inconsistent [[frame rate]], long loading times and lack of online play.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nair |first=Chandra |date=January 2001 |title=Half-Life |journal=Dreamcast Magazine |publisher=Paragon Publishing |issue=15 |pages=56–58}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Half-Life Dreamcast Review |journal=Computer and Video Games |issue=228}}</ref> Sierra planned to release a version with online multiplayer using [[SegaNet]]. The Gearbox CEO, [[Randy Pitchford]], said he suggested adding multiplayer modes and [[Mod (video games)|mods]] from the Windows version, including ''[[Team Fortress Classic]]'' and the multiplayer modes from ''Opposing Force.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bramwell |first=Tom |date=September 26, 2000 |title=''Half-Life'' Dreamcast Multiplayer |url=http://eurogamer.net/articles/article_29304 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107021506/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/article_29304 |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dreamcast Previews: Half-Life Feature Preview |url=http://zdnet.com/gamespot/stories/previews/0,10869,2653878,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010225172303/http://zdnet.com/gamespot/stories/previews/0,10869,2653878,00.html |archive-date=February 25, 2001 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=[[GameSpot]]}}</ref> Sierra delayed the port again and said they hoped to finish development that year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Satterfield |first=Shane |date=November 8, 2000 |title=Sierra Explains Half-Life Delay |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/sierra-explains-half-life-delay/1100-2651756/ |access-date=October 26, 2008 |website=[[GameSpot]]}}</ref>

|url=http://pc.ign.com/articles/092/092908p1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205024123/http://pc.ign.com/articles/092/092908p1.html |archive-date=December 5, 2008 === Mac port ===
A version of ''Half-Life'' for [[Classic Mac OS|Mac OS]] was announced by Logicware on April 23, 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIERRA STUDIOS TO DELIVER BEST-SELLING HALF-LIFE TO THE MAC |url=http://planetfortress.com/syndicate/files/HLmac1.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223180543/http://www.planetfortress.com/syndicate/files/HLmac1.txt |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 23, 2012 |access-date=December 11, 2023 }}</ref> However, Valve canceled it a few months later in October 1999.<ref name="Blue's News">{{Cite web |title=Mac Half-Life Cancelled - Blue's News Story |url=https://www.bluesnews.com/s/6736 |access-date=December 11, 2023 |website=Blue's News}}</ref> The Valve CEO, [[Gabe Newell]], said the port was substandard, citing a separate multiplayer network, no automatic update utility and the inability to include Valve's multiplayer mod ''Team Fortress Classic''. He said he did not want to make Mac players "second-class customers" and preferred to write off the investment rather than "take money from Mac customers and short-change them".<ref name="Blue's News" /> [[Rebecca Heineman]], the co-founder of Logicware, denied this, saying that Valve cancelled the port as [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] had angered them by misrepresenting sales projections. She said the port was complete and three weeks from release.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lPTLPXNtb2I&ab_channel=RMC-TheCave |title=Rebecca Heineman - Developer & Co-Founder of Interplay {{!}} Retro Tea Break |date=February 2, 2023 |time=1:36:41 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> In 2013, Valve released a port for [[OS X]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ingraham |first=Nathan |date=January 25, 2013 |title=Original ''Half-Life'' finally available for OS X through Steam nearly 15 years after its release |url=https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/25/3915338/original-half-life-finally-available-for-os-x-through-steam |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=[[The Verge]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== ''Half-Life 2'' era (2004–2008) ==
=== ''Half-Life 2: Episode Three'' ===
{{main|Half-Life 2: Episode Three}}
In May 2006, Valve announced a trilogy of [[Episodic video game|episodic games]] that would continue the story of ''[[Half-Life 2]]'' (2004).<ref name="GameSpot2">{{Cite news |date=May 24, 2006 |title=Half-Life 2: Episode One gold, Two dated, Three announced |work=GameSpot |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/half-life-2-episode-one-gold-two-dated-three-announced/1100-6151796/ |archive-date=November 25, 2013}}</ref> ''[[Half-Life 2: Episode One|Episode One]]'' was released in 2006, followed by ''[[Half-Life 2: Episode Two|Episode Two]]'' in 2007.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/half-life-2-episode-one/critic-reviews/?platform=pc|title=Half-Life: Episode One on Metacritic|publisher=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=August 18, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=August 18, 2020|url=http://www.metacritic.com/games/platforms/pc/halflife2episode2|title=Half-Life 2: Episode Two|publisher=[[Metacritic]]|archive-date=February
