1383164318.content:
{{Short description|Unreleased video games}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Unreleased ''Half-Life'' games}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=February 2026}}
''[[Half-Life (series)|Half-Life]]'' is a series of [[first-person shooter]] games created and published by [[Valve Corporation|Valve]]. Since the release of the original ''[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]'' for [[Windows]] in 1998, several ''Half-Life'' projects have been canceled, including some developed by other studios.

In 1999, Valve canceled a ''Half-Life'' [[Porting|port]] for [[MacOS|Mac]] developed by Logicware. '''''Half-Life: Hostile Takeover''''', an [[expansion pack]] for ''Half-Life'' developed by [[2015 (company)|2015]], was cancelled in 2000. In 2001, [[Sierra Entertainment|Sierra]], the publisher of the original ''Half-Life'', canceled a port for [[Dreamcast]] after [[Sega]] announced its discontinuation.

After releasing ''[[Half-Life 2: Episode Two]]'' in 2007, Valve struggled to settle on a direction for a new ''Half-Life'' game. ''[[Half-Life 2: Episode Three|Episode Three]]'' was canceled after Valve abandoned [[Episodic video game|episodic]] development and began developing a new [[game engine]], [[Source 2]]. Another ''Half-Life 2'' episode, by [[Junction Point Studios]], was canceled after Junction Point was acquired by [[Disney Interactive Studios]]. Valve moved the project to [[Arkane Studios]], who developed it as ''Ravenholm,'' set in the [[Ravenholm|town infested with zombies]] from ''[[Half-Life 2]]'' (2004). Valve canceled it as they felt it was creatively restrained.

Valve developed '''''Half-Life 3''''' between 2013 and 2014, experimenting with [[Procedural generation|procedurally generated]] levels, but canceled it as the Source 2 engine was still unfinished. A [[Virtual reality game|virtual reality]] (VR) game set on a time-travelling ship, ''Borealis'', was canceled as the VR technology and tools were not complete. As of 2026, [[Data mining|datamines]] and leaks suggested that a ''Half-Life'' game codenamed '''''HLX''''' is in development using Source 2.

== ''Half-Life'' era (1998–2004) ==
=== ''Half-Life: Hostile Takeover'' ===
On November 23, 1999, ''[[GameSpot]]'' reported that [[2015 (company)|2015]] was developing a ''Half-Life'' [[expansion pack]] to follow ''[[Half-Life: Opposing Force]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ajami |first=Amer |date=November 23, 1999 |title=New Half-Life Add-on Coming |url=http://headline.gamespot.com/news/99_11/23_pc_halfadd/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000301003051/http://headline.gamespot.com/news/99_11/23_pc_halfadd/index.html |archive-date=March 1, 2000 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=[[GameSpot]]}}</ref> On March 18, 2000, the ''Adrenaline Vault'' reported that the expansion was named ''Half-Life: Hostile Takeover'' and that it had appeared on retail product lists with a release date of late August.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laprad |first=David |date=March 18, 2000 |title=New Half-Life Expansion Coming |url=http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=3182000-91229 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000607145116/http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=3182000-91229 |archive-date=June 7, 2000 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=The Adrenaline Vault}}</ref> On August 7, the ''Adrenaline Vault'' reported that [[Sierra Entertainment|Sierra]], the publisher of ''[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]'', had informed them that ''Hostile Takeover'' had been canceled. The [[stock keeping unit]] for ''Hostile Takeover'' was repurposed by online retailers for ''[[Counter-Strike (video game)|Half-Life: Counter-Strike]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laprad |first=David |date=August 7, 2000 |title=Confusion Surrounds Half-Life Add-On Pre-Sales |url=http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=872000-133010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010521163812/http://avault.com/news/displaynews.asp?story=872000-133010 |archive-date=May 21, 2001 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=The Adrenaline Vault}}</ref> On June 21, 2001, Valve filed a video game [[trademark]] for "Hostile Takeover". After several extensions, the trademark expired on October 3, 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HOSTILE TAKEOVER |publisher=[[United States Patent and Trademark Office]] |url=https://tsdr.uspto.gov/#caseNumber=76275717&caseType=SERIAL_NO&searchType=statusSearch |access-date=August 11, 2020 }}</ref>

=== Dreamcast port ===
On February 14, 2000, Sierra announced that a port of ''Half-Life'' for the [[Dreamcast]] console was in development by Captivation Digital Laboratories with Valve and [[Gearbox Software]]. It would feature improvements including higher-[[Polygon mesh|polygon]] character models and new lighting effects. Gearbox, who had developed ''Opposing Force'', created a new single-player campaign for the port, ''[[Half-Life: Blue Shift]],'' focusing on the security guard [[Barney Calhoun|Barney]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 14, 2000 |title=HALF-LIFE COMING TO SEGA DREAMCAST |url=https://www.bluesnews.com/pressreleases/hld.shtml |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423010222/https://www.bluesnews.com/pressreleases/hld.shtml |archive-date=April 23, 2019 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=Blue's News}}</ref>

The port was delayed to September 2000,<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDjFRH6hzA8 |title=Half-Life Dreamcast commercial |date=August 9, 2010 |publisher=Combine OverWiki |access-date=July 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160814212108/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDjFRH6hzA8 |archive-date=August 14, 2016 |via=YouTube |url-status=live}}</ref> then November,<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 14, 2000 |title=Half-Life: Blue Shift Announced |url=https://www.bluesnews.com/a/61 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107114414/https://www.bluesnews.com/a/61 |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=July 23, 2020 |website=Blue's News}}</ref> when game publications began to receive early copies for review. Reception was mixed, with criticism for the inconsistent [[frame rate]], long loading times and lack of online play.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nair |first=Chandra |date=January 2001 |title=Half-Life |journal=Dreamcast Magazine |publisher=Paragon Publishing |issue=15 |pages=56–58}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Half-Life Dreamcast Review |journal=Computer and Video Games |issue=228}}</ref> Sierra planned to release a version with online multiplayer using [[SegaNet]]. === Mac port ===
A version of ''Half-Life'' for [[Classic Mac OS|Mac OS]] was announced by Logicware on April 23, 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIERRA STUDIOS TO DELIVER BEST-SELLING HALF-LIFE TO THE MAC |url=http://planetfortress.com/syndicate/files/HLmac1.txt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223180543/http://www.planetfortress.com/syndicate/files/HLmac1.txt |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 23, 2012 |access-date=December 11, 2023 }}</ref> However, Valve canceled it a few months later in October 1999.<ref name="Blue's News">{{Cite web |title=Mac Half-Life Cancelled - Blue's News Story |url=https://www.bluesnews.com/s/6736 |access-date=December 11, 2023 |website=Blue's News}}</ref> The Valve CEO, [[Gabe Newell]], said the port was substandard, citing a separate multiplayer network, no automatic update utility and the inability to include Valve's multiplayer mod ''Team Fortress Classic''. He said he did not want to make Mac players "second-class customers" and preferred to write off the investment rather than "take money from Mac customers and short-change them".<ref name="Blue's News" /> [[Rebecca Heineman]], the co-founder of Logicware, denied this, saying that Valve cancelled the port as [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] had angered them by misrepresenting sales projections. She said the port was complete and three weeks from release.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lPTLPXNtb2I&ab_channel=RMC-TheCave |title=Rebecca Heineman - Developer & Co-Founder of Interplay {{!}} Retro Tea Break |date=February 2, 2023 |time=1:36:41 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> In 2013, Valve released a port for [[OS X]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ingraham |first=Nathan |date=January 25, 2013 |title=Original ''Half-Life'' finally available for OS X through Steam nearly 15 years after its release |url=https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/25/3915338/original-half-life-finally-available-for-os-x-through-steam |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=[[The Verge]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Junction Point Studios episode ===
[[File:11.30.10WarrenSpectorByLuigiNovi1.jpg|thumb|[[Warren Spector]] (pictured in 2010) led development of a canceled ''Half-Life 2'' episode.]]
Another ''Half-Life 2'' episode was developed by [[Junction Point Studios]], led by [[Warren Spector]]. The episode showed how the town of [[Ravenholm]] from ''Half-Life 2'' became infested with [[Characters of the Half-Life series|headcrabs]] and zombies, with the return of the character of [[Father Grigori]].<ref name="Scott-Jones-2017">{{Cite web |last=Scott-Jones |first=Richard |date=March 27, 2017 |title=Ravenholm features in another cancelled Half-Life 2 episode, now with snow and magnetism |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/half-life-2/half-life-2-episode-snowy-ravenholm-junction-point |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328105333/https://www.pcgamesn.com/half-life-2/half-life-2-episode-snowy-ravenholm-junction-point |archive-date=March 28, 2017 |access-date=March 27, 2017 |website=[[PCGamesN]]}}</ref> It included a "magnet gun", which fired projectiles that magnetized metal surfaces and attracted objects and enemies, and was used for combat and puzzles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benson |first=Julian |date=September 20, 2017 |title=Warren Spector reveals how the magnet gun would have worked in cancelled Half-Life episode |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/half-life-3/half-life-3-ravenholm-episode-warren-spector-junction-point |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921000718/https://www.pcgamesn.com/half-life-3/half-life-3-ravenholm-episode-warren-spector-junction-point |archive-date=September 21, 2017 |access-date=September 20, 2017 |website=[[PCGamesN]]}}</ref>

Junction Point worked on the game for a year, producing enough content to demonstrate one section, and a [[vertical slice]] that demonstrated the magnet gun. Valve lost interest in the project and Junction Point, who had been acquired by [[Disney Interactive Studios]] partway through, canceled it to instead develop ''[[Epic Mickey]]''.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Turi |first=Tim |date=April 24, 2015 |title=Abandoned Half-Life Episode Featured Magnet Gun, Warren Spector Says |magazine=[[Game Informer]] |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2015/04/24/half-life-abandoned-lost-episode-magnet-gun-valve-warren-spector.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813045505/https://www.gameinformer.com/b/news/archive/2015/04/24/half-life-abandoned-lost-episode-magnet-gun-valve-warren-spector.aspx |archive-date=August 13, 2019 |access-date=May 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Rick |date=November 8, 2017 |title=Warren Spector discusses his cancelled Half-Life 2 Ravenholm Episode |url=http://www.pcgamer.com/warren-spector-discusses-a-return-to-ravenholm-in-his-cancelled-half-life-2-episode/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108210135/http://www.pcgamer.com/warren-spector-discusses-a-return-to-ravenholm-in-his-cancelled-half-life-2-episode/ |archive-date=November 8, 2017 |access-date=November 8, 2017 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Disney buys game developer Junction Point|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-jul-13-fi-disney13-story.html|date=July 13, 2007|access-date=January 15, 2022|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> Screenshots appeared in early 2017.<ref name="Scott-Jones-2017" />

{{Anchor|Episode Four|Return to Ravenholm}}In 2007 or 2008, Valve gave the Junction Point project to [[Arkane Studios]] in Lyon, France. They developed it into a game with the working title ''Ravenholm'',<ref name="noclip arkane doc">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h4kdqwdbZZ8 |title=The Untold History of Arkane: Dishonored / Prey / Ravenholm / LMNO / The Crossing |date=May 26, 2020 |publisher=[[Noclip]] |time=33:00 |access-date=May 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200527035500/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h4kdqwdbZZ8 |archive-date=May 27, 2020 |url-status=live |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> referred to by some sources as ''Episode Four.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sheridan |first=Connor |date=May 21, 2020 |title=Half-Life 2: Episode 4 footage emerges a decade after it was canceled |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/half-life-2-episode-4-footage-emerges-a-decade-after-it-was-canceled/ |access-date=November 24, 2023 |website=[[GamesRadar]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="McLeand-2015" /> Players controlled Adrian Shephard from ''Opposing Force,'' working alongside Father Grigori, who had taken refuge in an abandoned psychiatric hospital. Arkane also implemented a nail gun that could create paths to conduct electricity and set traps.<ref name="noclip arkane doc" />

Valve gave Arkane freedom to develop ''Ravenholm'', as they had with Gearbox and ''Opposing Force'', providing feedback and technical support.<ref name="noclip arkane doc" /> With approximately one year left of development, Valve canceled the project. === ''Half-Life 3'' ===
''Half-Life 3'' was in development between 2013 and 2014. Valve planned to use [[Procedural generation|procedurally generated]] levels alongside a "crafted experience", similar to the [[Left 4 Dead (franchise)|''Left 4 Dead'' series]]; the game would generate different routes through environments each time it was played. The team took new scans of the face of Frank Sheldon, whose likeness was used for the [[G-Man (Half-Life)|G-Man]] character in ''Half-Life 2''. The Source 2 engine was still unfinished and the project was canceled early in development.<ref name="Skrebels-2020">{{Cite web |last=Skrebels |first=Joe |date=July 9, 2020 |title=Details of multiple cancelled Valve projects revealed, including ''Half-Life 3'' |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/half-life-3-left-4-dead-3-details-cancelled-valve |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713154054/https://www.ign.com/articles/half-life-3-left-4-dead-3-details-cancelled-valve |archive-date=July 13, 2020 |access-date=July 19, 2020 |website=[[IGN]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== ''Borealis'' ===
Shortly before his departure from Valve in 2016, Laidlaw led a [[virtual reality]] (VR) project on the Source 2 engine, ''Borealis'', set on the time-travelling ship mentioned in ''Episode Two'' and ''[[Portal 2]]''. The game would skip between the Combine's conquering of Earth before ''Half-Life 2'' and a time set shortly after ''Episode Two''. A minigame in which players would fish off the bow of the ship was also proposed.<ref name="Skrebels-2020" /> Laidlaw said the project ended because it was too early to be working in VR: "When people are struggling with the basic tools they need to rough out a concept, it's hard to convey any sort of vision, and it all evaporated pretty quickly."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Peel |first=Jeremy |date=March 1, 2023 |title='The narrative had to be baked into the corridors': Marc Laidlaw on writing ''Half-Life'' |language=en |work=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]] |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/the-narrative-had-to-be-baked-into-the-corridors-marc-laidlaw-on-writing-half-life |access-date=March 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230302232014/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/the-narrative-had-to-be-baked-into-the-corridors-marc-laidlaw-on-writing-half-life |archive-date=March 2, 2023}}</ref>

=== ''HLX'' ===

Following the release of ''[[Half-Life: Alyx]]'' in 2020, [[Data mining|dataminers]] examining updates to the Source 2 engine discovered that Valve was developing a non-VR game codenamed ''HLX''.<ref name="Valentine">{{Cite web |last=Valentine |first=Rebekah |date=November 19, 2025 |title=Why is everyone posting about a ''Half-Life 3'' announcement soon? |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/why-is-everyone-posting-about-a-half-life-3-announcement-soon |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=[[IGN]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="pcgamer" /> ''[[PC Gamer]]'' noted that the codename resembled ''HLVR'', Valve's codename for ''Alyx''.<ref name="pcgamer">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/fps/half-life-3-re-re-re-confirmed-a-valve-dev-just-said-hlx-out-loud/|title=Half-Life 3 re-re-re-confirmed: A Valve dev just said 'HLX' out loud|last=Chalk|first=Andy|website=[[PC Gamer]]|date=October 22, 2026|access-date=October 22, 2026}}</ref> On December 31, 2024, [[Michael Shapiro (actor)|Mike Shapiro]], the voice actor for the G-Man, posted a cryptic message on [[X (social network)|X]] suggesting "unexpected surprises" in the new year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=January 2, 2025 |title=Half-Life 3 Rumors Ramp Up After G-Man Voice Actor Issues Cryptic Tweet — His First in Years |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/half-life-3-rumors-ramp-up-after-g-man-voice-actor-issues-cryptic-tweet-his-first-in-years |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref> In April 2025, it was reported that ''HLX'' was being [[playtest]]ed and would be a sequel to ''Episode Two''.<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 4, 2025 |title=Half-Life 3 is not just in development, it's now "playable, end-to-end", leaker suggests |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/half-life-3-is-not-just-in-development-its-now-playable-end-to-end-leaker-suggests |access-date=November 20, 2025 |work=[[Eurogamer]] |language=en}}</ref> Industry insiders, dataminers and leakers reported that Valve was planning a 2025 announcement for ''HLX'', and that it could be ''Half-Life 3''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Claire |date=November 12, 2025 |title=Half-Life 3 rumors swirl in the wake of Valve's Steam Machine announcement |url=https://www.polygon.com/steam-machine-announcement-revives-half-life-3-rumors/ |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 27, 2025 |date=November 18, 2025 |first=Sjaak |last=Stechman |title=Is ''Half-Life 3'' finally on the way? The rumors are getting very loud |url=https://nordic.ign.com/half-life-3/101062/feature/is-half-life-3-finally-on-the-way-the-rumors-are-getting-very-loud |website=[[IGN]]}}<!-- auto-translated from unknown (Italian or Spanish) by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name="Valentine" /> In December 2025, the ''Insider Gaming'' senior editor Mike Straw said ''HLX'' had been planned as a launch game for Valve's [[Steam Machine]] hardware, released in June 2026, and that its announcement had been delayed by the [[2025–present global memory supply shortage|rising cost of RAM]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Chester |first=Edward |title=Half-Life 3 Steam Machine rumors just won't go away, with high RAM prices now somehow connected |website=[[PCGamesN]] |date=December 15, 2025 |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam-machine/half-life-3-rumors |access-date=December 17, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Koepp |first=Brent |title=Half-Life 3 Reportedly Delayed Due to Steam Machine Price, Leak Claims |website=[[Vice (website)|Vice]] |date=December 15, 2025|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/half-life-3-reportedly-delayed-due-to-steam-machine-price-leak-claims/ |access-date=December 17, 2025}}</ref> In October, the Valve composer [[Mike Morasky]] mentioned ''HLX'' briefly during a Q&A panel at [[GameSoundCon]], seemingly by mistake, but gave no details.<ref name="pcgamer" />

'''Tidiam Diadie Stephan Gomis''' (born 8 August 2006) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for German {{German football updater|RBLeipzi}} club [[RB Leipzig]].<ref>{{Soccerway|id=801316}}</ref>

== Club career ==
On 13 September 2022, Gomis signed his first professional contract with [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]], a deal until 2025, becoming the club's youngest ever professional.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-13 |title=Caen : Tidiam Gomis passe pro et marque l'histoire du SMC |url=https://www.foot-national.com/ligue-2/caen--tidiam-gomis-passe-pro-et-marque-l-histoire-du-smc-793822 |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=Foot National |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2022-09-13 |title=Premier contrat professionnel pour Tidiam Gomis |url=https://www.smcaen.fr/2022-2023/actualites/infos-club/premier-contrat-professionnel-pour-tidiam-gomis |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=Stade Malherbe Caen |language=fr}}</ref> On 12 August 2023, he made his professional debut in a 2–0 [[Ligue 2]] win over [[Pau FC|Pau]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-08-15 |title=Premières minutes avec les Pros pour Tidiam Gomis |url=https://www.smcaen.fr/2023-2024/actualites/groupe-pro/premieres-minutes-avec-les-pros-pour-tidiam-gomis |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=Stade Malherbe Caen |language=fr}}</ref> He became the fourth-youngest player in Caen history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-13 |title=La première de Tidiam Gomis à 17 ans et 4 jours sous le maillot du SM Caen : "Je la voulais, elle est arrivée" |url=https://www.francebleu.fr/sports/football/la-premiere-de-tidiam-gomis-a-17-ans-et-4-jours-sous-le-maillot-du-sm-caen-je-la-voulais-elle-est-arrivee-9989970 |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=ici, par France Bleu et France 3 |language=fr}}</ref> Described as one of the "brightest French players of his generation", Gomis was subject to interest from [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in the final days of the 2023 summer [[transfer window]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-01 |title=SM Caen. Tidiam Gomis reste malgré les assauts de Leverkusen |url=https://actu.fr/normandie/caen_14118/sm-caen-tidiam-gomis-reste-malgre-les-assauts-de-leverkusen_60033168.html |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=actu.fr |language=fr}}</ref> Although he agreed personal terms with Leverkusen, Caen rejected all offers for the player.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Malherbe, Tidiam Gomis, un choix sportif, un risque financier |url=https://www.footnormand.fr/actualites/sm-caen/malherbe-tidiam-gomis-un-choix-sportif-un-risque-financier |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=Foot Normand |language=fr}}</ref>

On 3 February 2025, Gomis signed a four-and-a-half-year contract with [[RB Leipzig]] in Germany.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=RB Leipzig|url=https://rbleipzig.com/en/news/tidiam-gomis-new-signing-rb-leipzig-sm-caen-2024-25|title=Tidiam Gomis joins RB Leipzig!|date=3 February 2025|access-date=4 February 2025}}</ref>

== International career ==
Born in France with Senegalese descent, Gomis is a France youth international.<ref>{{FFF player|id=10487-gomis-tidiam}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-13 |title=Caen : Tidiam Gomis signe pro |url=https://wiwsport.com/2022/09/13/caen-tidiam-gomis-signe-pro/ |access-date=2023-09-07 |language=fr-FR}}</ref> In May 2023, he was selected to play at for the [[France national under-17 football team|under-17s]] at the [[2023 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]], finishing as runners-up.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-09-01 |title=Tidiam Gomis au tournoi de Limoges |url=https://www.smcaen.fr/2023-2024/actualites/groupe-pro/tidiam-gomis-au-tournoi-de-limoges |access-date=2023-09-07 |website=Stade Malherbe Caen |language=fr}}</ref> In September 2023, he received his first call-up to the [[France national under-18 football team|under-18s]] for the [[Tournoi de Limoges]].<ref name=":0" />

1383164294.title: List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2026
1383164294.content:
{{Short description|none}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:List of ''EastEnders'' characters introduced in 2026}} [[File:EastEnders.svg|thumb|''EastEnders'' logo]] ''[[EastEnders]]'' is a [[BBC]] [[soap opera]] that first aired on 19 February 1985.{{cite web |last1=Hughes |first1=Johnathon |title=How long has 'EastEnders' been running? |url=https://www.whattowatch.com/features/how-long-has-eastenders-been-running |website=[[What to Watch]] |publisher=[[Future plc]] |access-date=7 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114062456/https://www.whattowatch.com/features/how-long-has-eastenders-been-running |archive-date=14 January 2025 |date=28 September 2021}} This is a list of characters who have debuted or are set to debut in 2026. All characters are introduced by the serial's [[executive producer]], [[Ben Wadey]].{{cite magazine |last1=Knight |first1=Lewis |title=''EastEnders'' confirms Chris Clenshaw's final episode air date ahead of new era |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/eastenders-chris-clenshaw-final-episode-ben-wadey-newsupdate/ |magazine=[[Radio Times]] |access-date=9 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260909225344/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/eastenders-chris-clenshaw-final-episode-ben-wadey-newsupdate/ |archive-date=9 September 2026 |date=5 June 2025 |issn=0033-8060 |oclc=952210169 |url-status=live}} The first character to debut in 2026 is [[Bea Pollard]], portrayed by [[Ronni Ancona]], who made her first appearance in January. [[Dawn Steele]] debuted in March, portraying [[#Sandra Goodwin|Sandra Goodwin]], the adoptive mother of [[Josh Goodwin (EastEnders)|Josh Goodwin]] ([[Joshua Vaughan]]). In April, [[#Ivy Knight-Mitchell|Ivy Knight-Mitchell]], the newborn daughter of [[Nicola Mitchell]] ([[Laura Doddington]]) and [[George Knight (EastEnders)|George Knight]] ([[Colin Salmon]]), was introduced. [[#Bruce|Bruce]] (Tyler Kinhorn), the probation officer for [[Eddie Knight]] ([[Christopher Fairbank]]), debuted in May, followed by gangster [[#Russell Delaney|Russell Delaney]] ([[Anthony Skordi]]). [[#Sheila Atkins|Sheila Atkins]] ([[Sheila Ruskin]]), the grandmother of serial killer [[Gray Atkins]] ([[Toby-Alexander Smith]]), first appeared in June, as well as [[#Ria Virdi|Ria Virdi]] (Aaria Sharma), the foster daughter of [[Suki Panesar|Suki]] ([[Balvinder Sopal]]) and [[Eve Panesar-Unwin]] ([[Heather Peace]]). In July, the arrivals of [[#DC Craig Ingram|DC Craig Ingram]] ([[Matthew James-Bailey]]) and [[#Clive Masters|Clive Masters]] ([[Jason Durr]]) took place. August introduced Nicola's extended family, the Hawkins. This introduction began with her sisters, [[#Gemma Hawkins|Gemma]] ([[Patricia Potter]]) and [[#Jodie Hawkins|Jodie]] ([[Anna Constable]]), along with their mother [[#Rose Hawkins|Rose]] ([[Marian McLoughlin]]). They were later joined by Gemma's husband, [[#Ned Hawkins|Ned]] ([[Jamie Bamber]]), and their son, [[#Ryder Hawkins|Ryder Hawkins]] ([[Felix Uff]]). Additionally, [[#Darnell Larson Jr|Darnell Larson Jr]] ([[Christopher Colquhoun]]), the long-lost half-brother of [[Denise Fox]] ([[Diane Parish]]), and his daughter, [[#Grace Larson|Grace Larson]] ([[Krysstina Frempong]]), were also introduced. In addition to the aforementioned arrivals, several [[#Other characters|other characters]] appear throughout the year. == Ethan Branning-Panesar == {{Infobox soap character | name = Ethan Branning-Panesar | series = [[EastEnders]] | portrayer = | years = | first = {{Start date|2026|01|01|df=y}}{{Efn|Ethan Branning-Panesar first appeared as an unnamed character during the New Year's Day 2027 flash-forward episode, which broadcast on 1 January 2026. He was later re-introduced as Ethan during the 16 September 2026 episode.}} | introducer = [[Ben Wadey]] | family = [[Mitchell family|Mitchell]]
[[Branning family|Branning]] | father = [[Harry Mitchell (EastEnders)|Harry Mitchell]]
[[Vinny Panesar]] (legal) | mother = [[Penny Branning]] | grandfathers = [[Teddy Mitchell]]
[[Jack Branning]] | grandmothers = {{Plain list| * [[Nicola Mitchell]] * [[Suki Panesar]] (legal) * [[Selina Branning]] }} | aunts = [[Amy Mitchell (EastEnders)|Amy Mitchell]]
[[Ivy Knight-Mitchell]] | uncles = {{Plain list| * [[Barney Mitchell]] * [[Ricky Branning]] * [[James Branning]] }} | relatives = {{Plain list| * [[Max Branning]] * [[Lauren Branning]] * [[Oscar Branning]] * [[Annie Carter]] * [[Louie Beale]] * [[Jimmy Beale]] }} }} '''Ethan Branning-Panesar''' is the son of [[Harry Mitchell (EastEnders)|Harry Mitchell]] ([[Elijah Holloway]]) and [[Penny Branning]] ([[Kitty Castledine]]). He first appeared during the 1 January 2026 episode, which served as a flash-forward episode to New Year's Day 2027 where Ethan was under the guardianship of [[Jack Branning]] ([[Scott Maslen]]) whose life was saved by his brother [[Max Branning]] ([[Jake Wood]]).{{cite magazine |last1=Knight |first1=Lewis |title=21 ''EastEnders'' questions after that Max Branning flashforward episode |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/eastenders-flashforward-2027-max-branning-bride-pregnancy-questions-newsupdate-explained/ |magazine=[[Radio Times]] |access-date=13 October 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013171215/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/eastenders-flashforward-2027-max-branning-bride-pregnancy-questions-newsupdate-explained/ |archive-date=13 October 2026 |date=1 January 2026 |issn=0033-8060 |oclc=952210169 |url-status=live}} Several months later, he is revealed to be conceived after Harry and Penny have a one-night-stand, shortly before she begins dating [[Vinny Panesar]] ([[Shiv Jalota]]). Ethan makes his present day introduction during the 16 September 2026 episode. Initially, Vinny believes that he is Ethan's father and at his naming ceremony in accordance to Vinny's [[Sikh]] faith, his mother [[Suki Panesar]] ([[Balvinder Sopal]]) announces that the baby's name should begin with the letter E. Penny's father [[Jack Branning]] ([[Scott Maslen]]) suggests the name Ethan.
